audits.jarvis_gap: Both moves landed close to their design intent and are enforced in the actual CI gate rather than merely documented: the owner-time AST guard (frontend/scripts/check-owner-time-ast.mjs) and the visual-role registry-plus-guards (frontend/src/lib/visual-token-roles.ts, eslint.config.js's no-private-identity-token rule, visual-role-css-guard.mjs) are real, non-trivial static-analysis machinery wired into `npm run test`, which CI runs on every PR, and both show stable post-merge history with no follow-up patches needed. The remaining gap is narrow and expected: the owner-time guard's exception lists are hand-maintained rather than self-proving, and the visual-role guard's long correction tail during review shows the CSS/JS grammar-evasion surface is genuinely hard to fully close, though no known bypass currently exists in the codebase. Neither move is a skin over a stub; both constitute real repository invariants doing real work today.

All three move-set items landed and are wired to real, tested backend/frontend code, not skins. The heartbeat authority (bu-6jv4m.4) and Issues condition ledger (bu-6jv4m.3) match their specs closely: a single clock-driven health value flows from the WebSocket hook through the shell indicator, polling cadence, and announcer, and reachability onset/recovery/recurrence is now server-computed and independent of probe sample timestamps, with an audit-to-issue deep link that returns an honest found/not-found/503 trichotomy instead of a fuzzy client-side substring search. The Spend forecast math (bu-6jv4m.2) is also fully replaced with a deterministic, fixed-clock, cron-cycle-aware monthly estimator with dedicated fixed-clock tests -- the specific 24h-sample-times-30 bug is gone. The one real gap is the routing-rule deletion side of bu-6jv4m.2: the shipped Undo is a client-side recreate-at-position action, not a server-backed exact-order restore, and the team deliberately walked back an earlier version that overclaimed order restoration -- the current UI explicitly discloses that first-match order is not guaranteed to be restored. That is an honest, tested compromise (no fabricated calm), but it is neither of the two spec-sanctioned outcomes (exact-order Undo or an explicit irreversible gate at delete time), so the move set overall reads as landed-with-gaps rather than fully as-designed.

findings.detail: Spec called for deletion of a first-match routing rule to be either an exact-order server-backed Undo, or an explicit irreversible gate if restoration cannot be guaranteed. What shipped is a third path: a client-side recreate-at-recorded-position mutation with an honest on-screen disclaimer that first-match order is not guaranteed restored, and a preimage banner kept on failure so the rule definition is never lost. This is calm-honest (no fabricated restoration claim) but does not meet either spec-sanctioned outcome -- there is no server-backed atomic undo and no irreversible-action gate at delete time; a rule deleted while another insert/reorder races it can permanently land at the wrong position with no warning at delete-confirm time that this can happen.

findings.title: Autonomy rule-tier label bypasses the token system: raw Tailwind color for a local category, state-red repurposed for a non-state classification
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/approvals/autonomy-panel.tsx:37-44 (SCOPED_RULE_TIER_CLASS = "text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400"; tierClass() returns "text-[var(--red-text)]" for the "full autonomy" tier)
findings.detail: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md Requirement 'Surface Palette' scenario 'No invented colors' requires every color reference to resolve to a token in frontend/src/index.css, with raw literals confined to the token file itself; the 'Semantic Visual Role Matrix' requires a local taxonomy (exactly what 'full autonomy' vs 'scoped' is) to resolve through categoricalHueVar/categoricalColor → --categorical-1..12, never a raw Tailwind class and never a state token. Here the 'scoped' tier uses a hard-coded text-blue-600/400 Tailwind literal (an explicit eslint-disable acknowledges it isn't following the state-color rule, but doesn't route it through the categorical ramp either), and 'full autonomy' is painted with --red-text — the exact token the rest of this same page reserves for genuine alarm states (rejected approvals, push-failed banners, attention-ledger 'failed' counts). A standing full-autonomy grant is a calm classification, not an active failure; borrowing the alarm color for it both violates the token contract and risks desensitizing the owner to real red elsewhere on the same panel.

findings.title: Decisions row's only meaningful action (open the underlying Bead) has no keyboard verb — breaks the j/k triage rhythm
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/DecisionsPage.tsx:161-169 (per-row "Open Bead detail" <Link>, rendered outside the button/roving-selection element) and :283-287 (useListTriage called with no `verbs`, comment: "this read-only summary has no action payload or mutation endpoint")
findings.detail: th-design/design-bar bias 7 (discoverable power: frequent actions grow shortcut paths) and the walkthrough's 'Habit' question. useListTriage (frontend/src/hooks/use-list-triage.ts:50-65) explicitly supports a verb whose handler is any callback, not just a mutation — ApprovalsPage already uses it for pure client-side scheduling. DecisionsPage conflates 'no mutation' with 'no keyboard act': the single next step an owner takes after reading a decision's inline context is to open its Bead (the only interactive affordance in the row besides selection), yet reaching it requires abandoning the j/k rhythm to Tab or click the link. On a page whose entire premise is triage-by-keyboard (mirrors ApprovalsPage/IssuesPage per this file's own header doc), the one door out of every row is the one thing the shortcut layer was never taught.

findings.title: Bead detail's breadcrumb is a hard-coded dead link back to /decisions — discards the selection context and the actual navigation origin
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/BeadDetailPage.tsx:205 (breadcrumbs={[{ label: "Decisions", href: "/decisions" }, ...]}), compare frontend/src/pages/DecisionsPage.tsx:258-271 (selectDecision writes ?bead=<id> via setSearchParams so a direct /decisions?bead=<id> URL restores selection)
findings.detail: Systemic sin 'drill-down dead ends (links that discard their context)'. DecisionsPage maintains exactly the URL shape needed to restore the owner's place (?bead=<id>), but BeadDetailPage's only way back links to the bare /decisions, discarding it — the owner returns to an unselected list and must re-find the row. The same static breadcrumb also appears identically whether the bead was reached from a decision row, from an escalated_blocked_id link (DecisionsPage.tsx:218), or from another bead's own dependency link (BeadDetailPage.tsx:161) — chaining through two or three dependency hops, 'Decisions' is the only advertised way back regardless of which bead you actually came from, and it always loses the trail.

audits.ideal: The ideal attention surface treats /approvals and /decisions as two lanes of one triage instrument, not two disconnected pages the owner must remember to check separately: every row — approval or decision — is reachable, selectable, and actionable entirely from the keyboard, with an act-verb for every meaningful next step including "open the evidence" (not just mutate); every classification (rule tier, decision priority, escalation kind) reads through the exact token the design language assigns it, so color never has to be re-learned per panel; and every drill-down — approval → session, decision → bead, bead → bead-via-dependency — is a two-way door: the destination remembers exactly where the owner came from and can return them to that precise scroll/selection state in one hop, not just to the section root. Nothing on this surface fabricates an all-clear (already true here) and nothing forces the owner out of keyboard flow to reach the one thing they actually want to do next.
audits.jarvis_gap: ApprovalsPage is close to the ideal already — ranked queue, evidence-rich dossier, undo-windowed keyboard triage, an attention ledger that refuses to render suppressed-but-undelivered sources as calm, and degraded-fan-out honesty applied with unusual rigor throughout. The gap that remains is smaller and more surgical than prior runs' systemic sins: a handful of concrete inconsistencies where the surface's own high bar slips — a classification label borrowing the alarm-red token instead of the categorical ramp the spec built for exactly this case, a triage page whose single next-action has no keyboard verb despite the shared hook fully supporting one, and a breadcrumb that forgets the URL-preserving selection state the same file just built two components away. None of these touch the acknowledged, in-flight Decision Desk buildout (bu-ckkpz) — they are defects sitting alongside it in the parts of the surface that are already considered "done."

audits.jarvis_gap: The page already meets most of the north-star bar: degraded-source notes replace fabricated zeros everywhere (BoardFooter.tsx:150-172, ButlerVerdictOpener degraded-source clauses), quarantine/overdue reasons are root-evidence text not bare status words (NeedsYouStrip.tsx:33-43, ButlerDetailActions.tsx:110-118), consequential quarantine flips get an undo window (ButlersPage.tsx:170-206, ButlerDetailActions.tsx:181-201), and the board plus detail tabs are fully keyboard-reachable (arrow/enter cursor in ButlersPage.tsx:104-152, numbered+bracket tab shortcuts in ButlerDetailPage.tsx:200-226). The one crack: the single action this page exists to let an owner take with confidence, pause, resume, or restore a butler, writes to a data source the rest of the page does not read. useSetEligibility (use-general.ts:58-84) optimistically patches and invalidates only the switchboard-registry query. Every other rendering of that same butler's liveness on the same screen, the status-board cell rail/chip (StatusBoardCell.tsx, driven by useButlerStatusBoard -> the butlers/board query), the NeedsYouStrip membership, the SiblingButlerNav tone dot, and the ButlerDetailHeader activity-tone label (ButlerDetailHeader.tsx:110-113), is driven by the separate butlers/board query. That query is bus-covered only for session start/end events (event-cache-registry.ts:124-152); no eligibility/registry event exists in EVENT_CACHE_REGISTRY (event-cache-registry.ts:246-262), so an eligibility mutation never invalidates it. During normal bus-healthy operation the board only reconciles every POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS, five minutes (poll-policy.ts:35). Net effect: the instant an owner clicks Restore on ButlersPage or Pause/Resume on ButlerDetailPage, the button/chip that fired the mutation flips immediately (optimistic registry patch) while the board-driven cell tone, needs-you strip, sibling-nav dot, and header activity chip for that exact same butler keep showing the pre-action state for up to five minutes, two contradictory verdicts about the same butler on the same screen at the same time. This is a new instance of the implicit-evidence-cohort/two-sources-of-truth pattern, specifically in the one flow (bu-86c4c.15's restore-with-undo, and its Pause/Resume sibling) built to be the trustworthy quarantine control.

findings.title: Eligibility mutation writes only the registry cache; the board cache (which drives every other status rendering on the page) never updates
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-general.ts:58-84 (useSetEligibility cancelQueryKeys/invalidateQueryKeys only switchboard-registry); frontend/src/hooks/use-butlers.ts:50-59 (butlers/board is a distinct query, refetchInterval from useBusAwarePollInterval); frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:246-262 (EVENT_CACHE_REGISTRY has no eligibility/registry event type, so board is never bus-invalidated by a pause/resume/restore); frontend/src/lib/poll-policy.ts:35 (POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS = 5*60_000, the board's own fallback poll while the bus is healthy); consumers of the stale board: frontend/src/components/butlers/StatusBoardCell.tsx (rail/chip from row.eligibility/activity), frontend/src/components/butlers/NeedsYouStrip.tsx:63-72 (membership from row.activity), frontend/src/components/butler-detail/SiblingButlerNav.tsx:44-69 (tone dot from row.activity), frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerDetailHeader.tsx:98-113 (activity chip from activeRow.activity), while frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerDetailActions.tsx:104-108 computes isPaused from a wholly separate useRegistry() fetch.
findings.failure_scenario: Click Pause on ButlerDetailPage (or Restore on ButlersPage): the button/chip that owns the mutation flips instantly via the optimistic registry patch, but the status-board cell rail/chip, the needs-you strip, the sibling-butler-nav dot, and the detail-header activity label for that identical butler keep rendering the pre-action state, because they all read the butlers/board query which the mutation never touches and which is not bus-covered for eligibility changes, so they only catch up on the next 5-minute (bus-healthy) or 30s (bus-down) reconciliation poll.
findings.short_summary: Pause/resume/restore updates registry cache but not the board cache

audits.jarvis_gap: The calendar workspace is one of the more mature surfaces in the fleet: freshness plaques are tested for partial fan-out honesty (CalendarWorkspacePage.freshness-plaque.test.ts), audit rows carry session provenance links, undo is durable and receipt-bearing, and every panel (search, overlays, day-briefing, duplicates) distinguishes loading/error/degraded/empty with role="alert"/role="status" rather than collapsing to a silent []. What is missing to be JARVIS-grade is less about honesty and more about the owner's kinesthetic loop: a person scanning their day should never have to reach for the mouse to change range, and every chip that names a person or a domain record should be a door to that record, not a pointer back into the same grid. Today the calendar tells the truth about what it knows, but two classes of context it already holds in hand (an entity_id on every linked-person chip, and butler/kind metadata on every overlay chip) dead-end back into the calendar itself instead of opening the specialist page or entity profile that would let the owner verify or act on the underlying fact. The ideal surface would make every named entity a live link, bind day/week/month range switching and the search palette to single keystrokes alongside the already-good t/←/→/c set, and let the quick-add correction flow accept natural date typing instead of demanding raw ISO 8601 strings when a parse needs a nudge.

An owner looking at a meeting with 'Sarah' has no one-click path to Sarah's relationship profile (last contact, notes, other upcoming events) even though the exact entity_id is already in the payload — a drill-down dead end with the destination route already built and idle.

audits.ideal: Chronicles is the JARVIS retrospective spine: it opens on the most recent settled day with a voice paragraph whose provenance (live LLM / cached / templated / stale) is always legible and one click from regeneration; an attention rail that deep-links straight into the exact supporting evidence (episode drawer, correction prompt, source badge) with zero context loss; a day ribbon and Gantt where every rendered pixel traces to a real point event, and every source failure surfaces as an honest degraded badge rather than a quiet gap; a scrubber and map trail that either show real location evidence or explicitly say 'location signal unavailable' instead of rendering an indistinguishable empty trail; full keyboard/command-palette reach for day navigation, refresh, and regeneration; and a correction loop that writes back into the same evidence used to render the episode, closing the audit trail end to end. Nothing is ever rendered that the system cannot prove, and a 'no data' state is always visually and semantically distinct from a 'data existed but failed to load' state.
audits.jarvis_gap: Chronicles has closed most of the ground run 08 flagged: voice_source staleness now has a first-class 'stale' badge and Regenerate affordance (ChroniclesPage.tsx:347-449), non-content days (no_data/unavailable/degraded) never borrow quiet-day copy or fabricate KPI/attention content (ChroniclesPage.tsx:83-99, 330-338, 487-499), and Manual Refresh invalidates all 11 day-scoped query families together so the day effectively refreshes atomically from the owner's point of view (ManualRefreshButton.tsx, use-chronicles.ts:121-133). Nearly every drilldown panel (Gantt, DayRibbon, Balance, Trends, Rollups, WhoYouWereWith, SourceState, CorrectionPrompts) now renders its own SourceDegradedNote on isError rather than a fabricated empty state. The one lane that did not get this treatment is the point-events fetch that feeds both the Scrubber's snap markers and the map trail: DrilldownBody destructures only `data` from useChroniclesPointEvents and never checks isError, and neither Scrubber nor FloatingMapMinimap has any fallback of its own — so a genuine GET /chronicler/events failure renders identically to a day with zero location signal. This is the literal carry-forward of run 08's 'point-event availability... incomplete' grade: partially closed everywhere except this one lane, which is exactly the errors-impersonating-calm-empty-states sin the rest of the page now guards against.

findings.title: Point-events fetch failure is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty day (Scrubber + map trail)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:113-116 (destructures only `data` from useChroniclesPointEvents, isError discarded); frontend/src/hooks/use-chronicles.ts:449-459 (useChroniclesPointEvents carries no source_error degraded envelope contract, unlike balance/trends/rollups/who-you-were-with); no isError/degraded handling present in frontend/src/components/workspace/Scrubber.tsx or frontend/src/components/chronicles/FloatingMapMinimap.tsx
findings.detail: On a genuine GET /chronicler/events failure, `pointEvents` silently resolves to `[]` (ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:116), so the Scrubber gets no snap markers and FloatingMapMinimap gets no trail — both render exactly as they would for a day with no location signal at all. The owner has no way to tell 'nothing recorded' from 'could not load,' the precise sin the surrounding panels (DayRibbon, BalanceRings, TrendsLens, DayNarrative, WhoYouWereWithPanel, CorrectionPromptsPanel, GanttSwimlane, SourceStateBadgeStrip) all already guard against with an explicit SourceDegradedNote.

audits.ideal: The ideal Overview is a five-second fleet-verification instrument: a single honestly-sourced headline that can never contradict the attention list beneath it (already true here via the shared attention model), a Needs-attention list where every row is both explainable and actionable without leaving the pane (already true for approvals via inline approve/deny/defer), and — critically — where every row that names a specific piece of evidence (a timeline event, a QA patrol, a session) is a door directly to that evidence's own detail view, not a generic list the owner must re-search. Keyboard triage (j/k/a/d/x/u) covers every actionable queue on the page, not just the primary one, and no signal on the page is ever weaker than the deep link the backend already computed for it.
audits.jarvis_gap: The Overview's composite-model architecture (shared attention model, per-source degraded rows, undo-windowed inline decisions) is genuinely strong and already closes most of the 'errors impersonating calm' and 'fabricated data' sins that earlier runs found elsewhere. What remains is a narrower but still real violation of the evidence-spine promise: two of the Now/Needs-attention row builders in model.ts have the specific evidence id in hand (a timeline event id, a QA patrol id) but discard it when building the href, sending the owner to the generic /timeline or /qa list instead of the exact event or patrol the row is about — even though both destination routes already support the specific deep link. This is the same 'drill-down dead end' class earlier runs fixed for the runtime-attention and approval rows (which correctly deep-link to /butlers/:name and /approvals/:id) but it was never swept across the timeline-activity and QA-failure row builders, so the pane still occasionally hands the owner a door back to square one instead of straight to the evidence.

audits.ideal: The ideal /education is a single addressable learning command center: every curriculum, active or completed or abandoned, stays one filter away and never falls off the page's own map; every node the owner is pointed at from anywhere in the dashboard (a butler-detail overdue row, a notification, a search hit) resolves via a URL that lands exactly there with its evidence panel already open; every analytics card on the page states the same three-way loading/error/empty contract with the same retry affordance, so a degraded endpoint always reads as degraded and never as 'nothing to see'; and the visual language (mastery-status color, badges, chart hues) renders identically across all its own states because the tokens are the single source of truth for both meaning and paint. The owner opens the page, sees fleet-wide review load and portfolio mastery in the first two tab clicks, drills into any struggling concept in one click from anywhere it's mentioned, and never has to re-derive which curriculum something belonged to.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today's /education surface gets the epistemics right on its primary hot path — the curriculum-request receipt panel (CurriculumRequestReceiptPanel.tsx) is a model instance of the doctrine (acceptance vs. completion vs. named failure, unavailable-store honesty), and most analytics cards (MindMapGraph, MasteryTrendChart, StrugglingNodesCard, QuizHistoryList) correctly distinguish loading/error/empty with retry. But the surface breaks down exactly where a JARVIS system must not: at the edges of its own state machine and at its doors to other surfaces. The curriculum lifecycle is a dead end — abandoning a curriculum removes it from the only list the page ever fetches (status=active), so the Re-activate control that exists in CurriculumActions.tsx becomes permanently unreachable and there is no way to browse or resurrect a completed/abandoned course; the owner's learning history silently evaporates from the UI the moment it stops being 'active'. And the page has zero URL-addressable state, so the two places elsewhere in the dashboard that link into it (the butler detail Reviews tab's review-item/frontier-item rows) land the owner on an arbitrary auto-selected curriculum instead of the specific overdue node they clicked — a broken evidence door on a hot recovery loop. One analytics card (CrossTopicChart) also regresses the page's own honesty bar by swallowing isError and disappearing instead of degrading like its siblings, and a token-generation quirk silently strips the background tint off three of five mastery-status badge states. None of these are exotic: they are the ordinary seams (state transitions, cross-surface navigation, one inconsistent card) that a five-second, no-fabrication, unbroken-door bar exists to catch.

findings.title: Curriculum abandon -> reactivate is a broken, unreachable loop; no archive/completed view
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/EducationPage.tsx:28 (useMindMaps({status:"active"}) is the page's only mind-map fetch, no status filter UI anywhere in the file), :47 (selectedMap = mindMaps.find(...) — null once the map leaves the active-filtered list), :161-172 (Select options are exactly `mindMaps`, so a non-active map disappears from the picker), :187-192 (CurriculumActions only renders when `selectedMap` is truthy); frontend/src/components/education/CurriculumActions.tsx:70-79 (the "Re-activate" button, gated on status==="abandoned", is the ONLY UI verb that can undo an abandon); frontend/src/api/types.ts:4667-4671 (MindMapListParams.status is a free string, so a status selector was possible but was never built)
findings.failure_scenario: Owner clicks Abandon on the currently selected curriculum. The mind-maps query invalidates and refetches with status=active; the just-abandoned map is no longer in the list, so selectedMap becomes null and CurriculumActions unmounts — the Re-activate button the owner needs to undo the action never appears again, and the curriculum plus all its mastery/quiz history vanishes from /education with no owner-facing path back.

findings.title: Cross-page drill-down from Butler Education Reviews tab discards the target node (no URL deep-link)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerEducationReviewsTab.tsx:444-449 (`<Link to="/education" ...>{entry.label}</Link>` for a specific overdue review row) and :504-509 (same pattern for a specific frontier node); frontend/src/pages/EducationPage.tsx has no `useSearchParams`/`useLocation` usage anywhere in the file — selectedMapId/selectedNodeId are pure `useState`, always reset to `mindMaps[0]` on mount via the effect at :40-44
findings.failure_scenario: Owner clicks an overdue 'Photosynthesis' row on the butler detail Reviews tab. The Link points at bare /education with no query param naming the map or node, and EducationPage has no mechanism to read one even if passed. They land on whatever curriculum happens to be first in the active list, with the specific node they came to review nowhere in view.

findings.title: CrossTopicChart drops isError and vanishes on fetch failure, unlike every sibling card on the same tab
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/education/CrossTopicChart.tsx:14 (`const { data: analytics } = useCrossTopicAnalytics();` — isError never destructured) and :16-18 (`if (!analytics || analytics.topics.length === 0) return null;` — a failed fetch and a genuinely empty portfolio render identically: nothing). Compare frontend/src/components/education/MasteryTrendChart.tsx:19,28-44 and StrugglingNodesCard.tsx:23,30-46, both on the same Analytics tab, which render SourceDegradedNote with a retry action on isError.
findings.failure_scenario: The cross-topic-analytics endpoint goes down. On the Analytics tab, the Cross-Topic Portfolio card simply does not render — no error text, no retry — while the mastery trend and struggling-concepts cards two inches away correctly show 'could not be reached' with a Retry button. The degraded backend reads as calm 'no portfolio data'.

findings.title: Mastery-status badges lose their background tint for three of five states (Tailwind arbitrary-value class never emitted)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/education/mastery-status.ts:40-44 (`masteryStatusBadgeClassName` builds `bg-[${bg}]/10 text-[${text}]` via template-literal interpolation, consumed at frontend/src/components/education/NodeDetailPanel.tsx:79); repo-wide grep confirms the literal strings `bg-[var(--mfg)]/10`, `bg-[var(--dim)]/10`, and `bg-[var(--border-strong)]/10` (the bg classes for "reviewing", "diagnosed", "unseen") appear nowhere else in frontend/src as static text, whereas `bg-[var(--green)]/10` and `bg-[var(--amber)]/10` (used for "mastered"/"learning") appear literally elsewhere (e.g. QuizHistoryList.tsx:12,16; ButlerManagementTab.tsx:404) and so get picked up by Tailwind v4's static source scan.
findings.failure_scenario: Tailwind v4's automatic content detection only emits CSS for class strings it finds as literal text somewhere in the source tree; a class assembled at runtime via string interpolation is invisible to it unless the same literal text coincidentally exists elsewhere. Opening a node in NodeDetailPanel whose mastery_status is 'reviewing', 'diagnosed', or 'unseen' shows the status badge with correct text color but no background tint, while 'mastered'/'learning' render fully styled — a silent, state-dependent visual inconsistency.

moves.title: Close the curriculum lifecycle loop: status filter + always-addressable CurriculumActions
moves.why: Design-bar bias 1 (repeat-safe controls) and bias 8's recovery expectation: an action (Abandon) must not destroy the only path back to its own undo (Re-activate). Vision's 'boring, trusted system' requires the owner's learning history to stay reachable regardless of status.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add a status selector (Active/Completed/Abandoned/All) next to the curriculum picker, backed by MindMapListParams.status. 2) Resolve selectedMap/CurriculumActions from a direct per-id fetch (like MindMapGraph already does via useMindMap) rather than from the status-filtered list, so abandon/reactivate controls stay mounted regardless of which filter is active.

audits.jarvis_gap: The entities surface (Plex, Index, Concentration, Circles, Detail) is one of the more mature corners of the dashboard: the main data paths on every one of these pages correctly separate loading/error/empty states, halo and search failures render distinct SourceDegradedNote affordances instead of collapsing to false calm, and PlexPage in particular ships a genuinely JARVIS-grade radial exploration canvas with a real keyboard map (find-as-you-type, hop trail, drag-to-retier) and honest degraded notes for the halo fetch. The gap to world-class is narrow but real: one right-flank panel on the Plex (the neighbour-mode entity dossier) silently drops query errors so a facts/dates fetch failure renders as 'Nothing recorded yet' with real-data authority instead of an error; the Index page's rich bulk-curation keyboard map (cursor nav, multi-select, bulk merge/forget, create) has zero on-screen legend even though its sibling Plex page sets the precedent of showing one; and Circles' member-to-entity drill-down discards the originating-circle context, so a return trip requires re-navigating from scratch. None of these are structural failures — they are isolated regressions in an otherwise well-disciplined surface, which is exactly why they are worth closing: the rest of the surface has already set the bar these three spots fall short of.

findings.title: Entity dossier's Facts/Dates panel drops isError — a fetch failure renders as an honest empty record
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/relationship/PlexPage.tsx:1134-1144 (EntityDossier: `const { data: factsData, isLoading: factsLoading } = useEntityFacts(...)` and `const { data: datesData } = useEntityCoreDates(entityId);` — isError is never destructured from either hook) vs. line 1230 (`!factsLoading && facts.length === 0` renders "Nothing recorded yet.") and dates silently omit their whole section on empty (line 1200 `dates.length > 0 &&`).
findings.detail: useEntityFacts/useEntityCoreDates are standard react-query hooks that expose isError (confirmed at frontend/src/hooks/use-entities.ts:193-260); every sibling read in this same file (ranking, halo, neighbours) and every equivalent panel elsewhere in the codebase (ActivitySparkline, LatestInteractionsBlock, EntityDetailPage's timeline/gifts/drafts/loans/threads hooks at pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:631-959) correctly branch on isError. This one dossier panel does not: on a facts-service outage while hovering/centering a neighbour in Plex, the owner sees the same italic 'Nothing recorded yet.' shown for a genuinely empty record — a fetch failure impersonating a calm, current answer, on the exact axis (facts/provenance) the manifesto treats as load-bearing. The Dates section is worse: it just vanishes (no fallback UI at all), so an outage looks identical to 'no upcoming dates.'

findings.title: Entities Index bulk-curation keyboard map has no on-screen legend
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/relationship/EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:1303-1329 (handleListKeyDown implements ↑/↓ cursor, Space toggle, Shift+↑/↓ range select, Esc clear, Enter open, n create — documented only in a code comment) vs. grep for '↑|↓|Space|Shift+|kbd>' in the file returning zero UI-rendered legend, contrasted with PlexPage.tsx:2140-2143 which renders a visible 'type to find · esc back · enter open · 0 reset · drag a person to pin a tier' legend for its own keyboard map.
findings.detail: This is the Index's primary hot loop for triage (multi-select → merge/forget), yet nothing in the rendered page teaches an owner that arrow-key cursor navigation, Space-select, or Shift-range-select exist; discovery depends on reading source. The sibling page (Plex) in the same feature already establishes the pattern of a quiet bottom legend, so this is an inconsistency, not a missing capability to invent.

findings.title: Circle member drill-down discards the originating circle
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/relationship/CirclesPage.tsx:296-300 (`<Link to={`/entities/${member.entity_id}`}>` inside MemberRoster carries no `from=`/circle context, and EntityDetailPage's breadcrumbs (unlike Plex's URL-persisted hop trail at PlexPage.tsx:29-31) have no notion of a circle origin).

audits.ideal: A world-class Health surface would treat every headline number as a door: the vitals KPI strip on /health would click straight through to the exact trend behind it (as Spend and Chronicles already do), every measurement's staleness would be judged against a real per-type SLA with no silent blind spot for future KPI-eligible types, and the Conditions page would function as the actual care-context hub its copy promises — showing, and letting the owner set from the dashboard, which symptoms and research notes are attributed to each condition, not just what the butler happened to write. Nothing would render calm when it is stale, and no consequential number would be a dead end.
audits.jarvis_gap: The Health surface is one of the most heavily hardened pages in the fleet — prior JARVIS rounds (bu-w7b18.*, bu-mmdef, bu-ep4ks.7, bu-86c4c.2) already stamped out fabricated numbers (every cell falls back to "—", never a fake reading), calm-impersonating errors (SourceDegradedNote is threaded through every query boundary: vitals, adherence, dose history, nutrition totals, trend buckets), and the keyboard gap on all six add/log actions ("n" on every Tracker). What is left is narrower but still real: (1) the flagship overview page's vitals KPI strip is the one domain KPI strip in the app that never sets `href` on its cells, even though the exact door shape it would need (`/health/measurements?type=X`) is already implemented in the same file for insight routing — so the owner's five-second glance at a vital has zero-hop access everywhere else in the dashboard except from the vitals themselves; (2) the per-vital staleness SLA table only recognizes the four core vital types, and the KPI-slot selector is explicitly written (per its own comment) to anticipate the server marking other measurement types KPI-eligible in the future — when that day comes, any dynamic vital filling a core slot will render its age muted-calm forever, no matter how stale, because the SLA lookup silently returns undefined; and (3) `condition_id` is a real, typed relationship on both Symptom and HealthResearch (present in both their create and update request contracts) that the Health butler can populate, yet no dashboard form can set it, no list can filter by it, and Conditions — the page whose own description promises "care context" — shows no count or link into the symptoms or notes attached to a condition. None of these are fabrication or dead-empty-state defects; they are missing doors on relationships and freshness signals the data model and infra already support.

audits.jarvis_gap: Run 08's bu-6jv4m.11 correctly stopped checkpoint identities from impersonating independent connectors and gave the roster an honest 'unclassified' health lane with its own KPI-exclusion note — the fleet-liveness axis is now trustworthy. But the fix operated one axis (health/liveness) without auditing the adjacent auth axis that the same rows and the same AttentionStrip render beside it: `deriveConnectorDispatchInfo` intentionally keeps `authStatus: 'ok'` for every non-auth failure (offline, stale, generic degraded) as a documented modeling choice ('it's connectivity, not an auth diagnosis'), but the presentation layer never built a distinct treatment for 'auth is fine, everything else is on fire' — it just prints the literal word 'authorized' in green. The consequence is a second, live instance of the exact sin the fleet-health work was fighting: a status word now impersonates calm on rows that are, by definition, in the operator's attention queue. This is the direct 'what's NEXT' after bu-6jv4m.11 — the checkpoint-identity leak is closed, but the roster's remaining two-axis (health, auth) rendering model has never been reconciled for consistency, so an operator still cannot trust color at a glance on this page.

findings.title: Attention-worthy connectors render a green "AUTHORIZED" pill inside the attention/roster surfaces — health impersonated as calm by color, not just text
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ingestion/connectors/connector-auth.ts:98-105 (offline → authStatus 'ok'), :137-144 (stale → authStatus 'ok'), :165-172 (other degraded → authStatus 'ok'); authStatusLabel('ok')='authorized' and authStatusColor('ok')=green at connector-auth.ts:202-231; consumed verbatim by frontend/src/components/ingestion/connectors/ConnectorRosterRow.tsx:101,126-131,246-255 and frontend/src/components/ingestion/connectors/AttentionStrip.tsx:70,75-93
findings.detail: deriveConnectorDispatchInfo() deliberately keeps `authStatus: 'ok'` for offline/stale/other-degraded connectors (its own doc comment calls this 'connectivity, not an auth diagnosis'), but the roster row's Auth column and the AttentionStrip's colored label both render straight off `authStatus` via authStatusLabel/authStatusColor, with no separate rendering path for 'the auth axis is fine but the connector still needs attention'. The result: an OFFLINE connector — the worst health verdict on the page — displays a green, bold "AUTHORIZED" pill immediately next to (ConnectorRosterRow) or inside the literal "needs attention" strip (AttentionStrip) that lists it only because it needs attention. The health-dot column two cells over correctly says red "offline", so the same row visually contradicts itself: red 'offline' health verdict beside a green 'authorized' auth verdict, with the true explanation ('connector offline · check connectivity') demoted to small gray text underneath the green pill. This is a fresh instance of the run's core 'failure never impersonates health' sin — not the checkpoint-identity instance bu-6jv4m.11 already closed, but a new one it left standing on the same roster row and on the attention strip that move produced. It directly undermines five-second fleet verification: an operator scanning for red/amber signals sees a green word on the row causing the failure, and the AttentionStrip — the one place run-08 built specifically to surface actionable problems — mixes green 'authorized' text into its own red-count 'needs attention' list.

moves.why: Design-bar bias 5 (consistency: one color, one meaning everywhere) and the north star's 'failure never impersonates health' — a red health-dot row must not carry a green auth pill two columns over.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/ingestion/connectors/connector-auth.ts (authStatusLabel/authStatusColor), ConnectorRosterRow.tsx auth column, AttentionStrip.tsx label branch
moves.slice_plan: When health !== 'ok' and authStatus === 'ok', render a neutral 'n/a' or omit the auth pill entirely on the roster row (health dot already carries the verdict there); in AttentionStrip, drop the colored authStatusLabel/authStatusColor path for this case and show only the existing authNote text (already correct: 'connector offline · check connectivity') in the neutral/amber/red tone matching the underlying health, never green.

audits.ideal: The ideal /ingestion surface is a fleet-truth ledger where a five-second glance separates 'listening fine' from 'needs a human' with zero contradiction: every colored word on a row means the same thing everywhere it appears, checkpoint/registry bookkeeping never masquerades as a live connector or as a live problem, every drill-down (roster row → connector detail → recent event → timeline drawer, and the reverse) preserves its filter/scope context in the URL, bulk and reauth actions are keyboard-operable and idempotent, and every KPI, sparkline, and gate count either comes from a named live source or explicitly says which source is degraded — never a fabricated zero standing in for missing data.

audits.jarvis_gap: Issues/Audit-Log/Notifications already carry the load-bearing honesty machinery a JARVIS-grade surface needs: degraded-source notes instead of false all-clears, an exact server-resolved Audit→Issues evidence door (bu-6jv4m.3) that replaced a fuzzy text-match link, honest-pending remediation actions (ping/run-now/retry/escalate) that toast their real outcome, and URL-backed filters with j/k triage. The gap is that the newer verdict-opener layer built on top of this foundation does not yet inherit its own discipline: the Issues page's own severity/critical door promises a count computed from the page's full active scope (window + group + q + severities + butlers) but its href only encodes window+severity, so a scoped operator (filtered to one butler or one audit-derived group) who clicks '3 critical issues need review' lands on a differently-scoped page that no longer shows the 3 rows just described -- the exact 'door that discards its own context' failure mode bu-6jv4m.3 eliminated one hop upstream, now reappearing one hop downstream. Two smaller gaps sit beside it: Notifications renders two buttons ("Mark read", "Dismiss") wired to the identical handler on every actionable row, a redundant-affordance regression against the design bar's consistency bias; and Issues' Ping/Run-schedule-now remediation controls -- the fastest path from 'butler unreachable' to 'confirmed back' -- have no keyboard verb, forcing a mouse detour on the one hot loop where speed matters most (an unreachable butler mid-incident).

audits.ideal: The ideal /memory is exactly what bu-2ix8d already built toward: a five-second house-ledger where the Overture answers 'is remembering working' before any scroll, the Attention Rail is the one place state color lives, every register row is a keyboard-reachable door to its own evidence-bearing detail page (fact -> source episode -> session; episode -> derived facts; rule -> source episode), and every degraded fan-out is named rather than silently undercounted. On top of that base, the owner should never have to reach for a mouse to triage dozens of pending facts or standing orders: j/k moves a roving cursor down the ledger/daybook/standing-orders list, Enter opens the selected row, and a bound act-verb (confirm/retract on facts, the same verb the detail page already exposes) fires from the list itself and shows up in the '?' help sheet -- exactly the pattern already shipped for Dashboard, Issues, Approvals and Notifications. Every displayed ordinal or count is stable and non-duplicating across pages, so a rule's '§NN' is a citable, unique reference rather than a per-page artifact.
audits.jarvis_gap: The gap is narrow and concentrated in two places rather than diffuse. First, this is the one major row-list surface in the product (Facts/Rules/Episodes/Search-results, hundreds of rows per register) that never adopted the shared useListTriage j/k roving-selection + act-verb hook that Dashboard, Issues, Approvals, Notifications, AuditLog, Decisions, QaOverview and the education review timeline all use -- every register row here is mouse-only, and the commit-class Confirm/Retract verbs that already exist on FactDetailPage are unreachable from the ledger that lists the facts, forcing a click-in for every single triage action on what is explicitly the page's primary hot loop. Second, the standing-orders register's own doc comment promises '§NN numbering is global in render order across the filtered list,' but the ordinal is computed from the fetched page's local array index with no `+ offset`, so paging past the first 50 rules silently restarts numbering at §01 and duplicates ordinals already shown on page one -- a citable identifier that isn't actually unique, which is exactly the kind of small trust leak the north star's 'nothing fabricated' bar exists to catch, even though nothing here is a false all-clear.

findings.title: Memory's row registers are the one major list surface without j/k keyboard triage
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/memory/FactsRegister.tsx, RulesRegister.tsx, EpisodesRegister.tsx, SearchResults.tsx (no useRegisterShortcut/useListTriage usage) vs. frontend/src/hooks/use-list-triage.ts adopted in DashboardPage.tsx, IssuesPage.tsx, ApprovalsPage.tsx, NotificationsPage.tsx, AuditLogPage.tsx, DecisionsPage.tsx, QaOverviewPage.tsx, ReviewTimeline.tsx
findings.detail: The ledger/standing-orders/daybook registers and SearchResults render only mouse-activated RowLink/div rows; none registers j/k or an act-verb through useRegisterShortcut, so none of their bindings surface in the app's '?' shortcut sheet. The FactDetailPage Confirm/Retract commit footer (frontend/src/pages/FactDetailPage.tsx:76-141) is the only mutation surface on the whole page, but it is reachable only by clicking into a fact one at a time -- there is no way to roving-select and confirm/retract from the ledger itself, unlike every other triage-shaped list in the product.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner with 40 fading-but-still-important facts to confirm after a busy week (the exact scenario the Attention Rail's 'important facts fading' condition surfaces) must click into each fact's detail page, click Confirm, click back, and repeat -- 3+ actions x 40 rows -- instead of j/k + a single bound key, on a page whose own doctrine is keyboard-first and whose sibling list pages already ship that pattern.

findings.title: Standing-orders §NN ordinal is not actually global -- it resets and duplicates across pages
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/memory/RulesRegister.tsx:132 (ordinal = §${String(index + 1)...}) and :325-327 (ordered.map((rule, i) => <DirectiveRow ... index={i} />), no offset added); doc comment at RulesRegister.tsx:25-26 claims numbering is 'global in render order across the filtered list'; frontend/src/components/memory/RulesRegister.test.tsx only asserts §01/§02/§03 at offset 0 (lines 135-143, 214-216), never at offset>0
findings.detail: index is the row's position within the current 50-row fetched page only; the server-paginated offset is never added. Since the component's own comment (and its test file's comment, line 10) explicitly claims the numbering is global across the filtered list, paging to a second batch of standing orders re-renders §01..§NN instead of continuing §51..§NN, so two different rules on two different pages both display as, e.g., §03.

audits.jarvis_gap: QaOverviewPage is a genuinely strong dossier shell — url-persisted filters, a tri-state circuit breaker that never defaults to calm, an evidence-bearing reset confirm, real j/k list-triage, and a verdict opener that surfaces staffer/breaker/credential health nobody else exposed. The gap between this and a JARVIS-grade QA surface is at the edges rather than the core: (1) two standalone deep-link routes (/qa/patrols/:id, /qa/investigations/:id) collapse a genuine 404 and a dead API into the identical calm sentence 'not found', so an owner following a link during an outage is told the case never existed rather than that the staffer is unreachable; (2) the breaker-reset dialog — the one QA action that is consequential and hard to undo (re-admitting dispatches) — shows its evidentiary attempt IDs as inert truncated text with no door into the investigation each one names, so the owner must approve blind or abandon the dialog to go look; (3) the case rail's own backend already supports offset pagination but the UI never wires it, so once a filtered case list exceeds the page limit the only advertised escape is 'narrow filters', which can hide the very cases the owner came to see; and (4) QA is the one escalation-badged hot-loop page in the global rail with no keyboard chord, unlike every peer of comparable weight (Approvals p, Decisions d, Issues i, Sessions s), so reaching it from anywhere requires the mouse or the palette. None of these break the five-second-verification promise on the happy path, but each is a place where the surface quietly asks the owner to trust rather than verify.

findings.title: Patrol/investigation deep links render an unreachable source identically to a genuine 404

frontend/src/pages/QaPatrolDetailPage.tsx:200-209 (`if (!patrolId || isError || !patrol) return

Patrol not found.

`); frontend/src/pages/QaInvestigationDetailPage.tsx:28-48 (both the not-found branch and the `caseQuery.isError` branch render the identical string 'Investigation not found.')

audits.ideal: The sessions/timeline surface is the fleet's evidentiary spine end to end: every telemetry row — timeline event, session row, KPI, verdict clause — is one keystroke from its root evidence (stderr/exit_code, trace, request_id, parent session), every fetch that can partially fail names exactly which pool dropped and gates the calm empty state on it, and the whole surface (Sessions list, Timeline ledger, Session dossier) speaks one Dispatch dialect: hairline rows, no boxed cards, j/k roving focus and Enter/y/Esc on every list, with the same chord grammar from /timeline to /sessions to a session's own dossier.

The remaining gap is narrower and mostly cosmetic/parity rather than structural: Sessions has not been ported onto the Dispatch surface primitives that Timeline (its Telemetry-section sibling, one chord away) already uses, so the two pages visually disagree about what "one elevation" means; and Timeline, despite being explicitly called out in its own code as the fleet's densest telemetry page, still lacks the row-level j/k roving-focus keyboard loop that Sessions, Issues, and Approvals already share, so a keyboard-only owner can filter and jump-to-latest on Timeline but cannot rove and open individual rows without a mouse.

audits.jarvis_gap: The /secrets Passport (DirectionPassport) is genuinely close to the bar: honest degraded-source banners, a documented truth-amnesty fix for fabricated 'verified within the hour' copy, roving-tabindex keyboard nav, and command-palette verbs for probe-all/add. But /settings/permissions — the page that actually grants butlers access and moves credentials and full data exports — was clearly built to a different, earlier standard: it talks to the API through six hand-rolled `fetch('/api/...')` calls that hardcode the bare-root path client.ts's own header comment says is 'a dead link on every deployment except a bare-root one' (Tailscale path-mounted deployments are the documented norm), and that skip the 15s-timeout AbortController every other surface gets, so a hung backend spins the matrix, the webhook table, and every mutation forever with no visible acknowledgment. The same page lets an operator delete a webhook or rotate its (irreplaceable) signing secret with a single click and no confirmation, while a genuinely reversible thing (a permission flip) is gated behind a modal. And the passport's own multi-identity chip renders a live, hover-cursor, chevron-bearing button whose click handler is a no-op — a control that lies about being interactive. None of this is fabricated data or masked failure in the run-08 sense; it is process-fidelity debt (bar regression, not a new pattern) concentrated on the one settings sub-page that wasn't rebuilt with the rest. The ideal version has every settings/secrets mutation on one typed, timeout-bounded, deployment-path-correct client; irreversible actions gated the same way everywhere; and zero controls that render as affordances without delivering behavior.

findings.title: Permissions/webhooks page bypasses API_BASE_URL — dead on any non-root-mounted deployment, and has no request timeout
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:131,143,155,162,167,189,214 use bare `fetch("/api/permissions")`, `fetch("/api/webhooks")`, etc., instead of `apiFetch`/`resolveApiHref`; contrast frontend/src/api/client.ts:443-444 (`API_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL ?? "/api"`) and the comment at client.ts:450-453 explicitly documenting that 'the same app is served at /butlers (API at /butlers-api/api) and /butlers-dev (API at /butlers-dev-api/api) behind Tailscale path mounts, so a backend-built /api/... path is a dead link on every deployment except a bare-root one.' apiFetch also wraps every call in a 15s AbortController timeout (client.ts:497,509-529); the raw fetch() calls in SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx have none.
findings.detail: Every mutation and read on the Permissions page — the permission matrix, its cell-flip PUT, and all five webhook CRUD/test calls — is wired with hardcoded root-relative paths that were flagged in the codebase's own client.ts as broken under the project's documented multi-mount deployment pattern. On any instance not served at bare root, GET /api/permissions 404s against the wrong origin path and the whole page falls back to its generic 'No permissions or butlers found' / webhooks-degraded state, misrepresenting a routing bug as an empty policy. Where the request does reach a slow/hung backend, there is no timeout: the Loading/Saving/Deleting spinners on this page can spin indefinitely with no escape, unlike every other apiFetch-backed surface in the app (violates design-bar bias 8, 'fast beats fancy' / no dead waits, and bias 1 seamless UX).

findings.title: Webhook delete and secret regeneration are single-click irreversible actions with zero confirmation
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:1043-1050 (`handleDelete` calls `deleteWebhook(id)` directly from the row's 'Delete →' InlineActionLink at line 1211, no dialog/confirm) and :1092-1106 (`handleRegenerate` calls `updateWebhook(webhook.id, {regenerate_secret:true})` directly from the 'Regenerate secret' button, no confirm) — contrast the same file's `CellFlipModal` (lines 242-323), which requires a typed non-empty reason before a *reversible* permission flip.
findings.detail: Deleting a webhook destroys its signing secret and endpoint config permanently, and regenerating a secret instantly invalidates the old one for any consumer still verifying `X-Butler-Signature` with it — both are irreversible, consequential actions, yet both fire on a single click with no confirm dialog and no undo window, while the page's actually-reversible permission-grant toggle is the one gated behind a reason-required modal. This inverts design-bar bias 1/'Recovery': 'require explicit confirmation where [an action] is not reversible.'

findings.title: Multi-identity chip on /secrets renders as a live dropdown control but its click handler is a no-op
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/DirectionPassport.tsx:445-454 renders `<IdentityChip ... onClick={() => {/* handled via spine */}} />`; IdentityChip (frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/atoms.tsx:358-428) renders a `<button>` with `cursor-pointer` styling and a '▾' chevron glyph whenever `onClick` is truthy (atoms.tsx:384, 403-407, 410-421) — the chevron and cursor are the component's own signal for 'this opens something.'
findings.detail: When an instance has more than one identity (showIdentityChip, DirectionPassport.tsx:367), the header chip is keyboard-focusable, shows a pointer cursor, and carries a dropdown-affordance chevron, but clicking or activating it does nothing — the actual identity switch lives in the Spine sidebar instead, reachable only by scrolling/scanning it. A control that visually promises interactivity and delivers none is a discoverability dead end (design-bar bias 7: features must be reachable via the control that advertises them) and a consistency violation (bias 5: a chevron+cursor pairing means 'opens a menu' everywhere else in this design language).

audits.ideal: A JARVIS-grade Spend page treats every write with blast radius proportional to its confirm/undo weight: routing-rule deletion already gets a full consequence preview, confirm, and recoverable undo (bu-6jv4m.2), and the monthly ceiling -- the single control that can silently deny every dispatch fleet-wide -- would get the same or stronger treatment, with an inline warning the instant the typed value would put MTD at or above it, plus an immediate refetch of the halt-detection query so the owner sees the consequence before their next real dispatch does. Every signal on the page (posture, movers, breakdown, evidence tables) already refuses to fabricate calm and already opens a door to root evidence; the last mile is making every dimension of every drill-down (not just butler) equally deep, and making the one write path with fleet-wide reach as safety-gated as the read paths are honest.
audits.jarvis_gap: Spend is one of the most disciplined surfaces in the dashboard: every breakdown, chart, and table already refuses to fabricate calm (source_error/unavailable_butlers footnotes everywhere), the honest per-butler daily stripe chart replaced the old fabricated smear, the by-schedule forecast states its basis instead of a silent x30, and bu-6jv4m.2 gave routing-rule deletion a full consequence-preview + confirm + recoverable-undo treatment the design bar would sign off on. The gap between this and world-class is concentrated in exactly one place the redesign didn't reach: the monthly-ceiling control. The page's own commentary states, correctly, that the ceiling is the single most consequential lever on the surface -- it denies EVERY dispatch fleet-wide the instant MTD reaches it (spawner.py:1670-1690) -- and the page devotes an entire dedicated banner + evidence drawer to detecting that state after the fact. Yet the control that sets the ceiling is a bare number input with a Save button: no comparison to current MTD, no warning, no confirm, and no immediate refetch of the halt-detection query, so a fat-fingered save (e.g. an owner meaning to raise headroom for the day types `50` instead of `500`) silently DoSes the entire fleet, discoverable only once dispatches start failing and the bus-aware poll catches up.

findings.title: CeilingEdit can silently halt fleet-wide dispatch with no warning, confirm, or immediate feedback
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:568-635 (CeilingEdit: numeric input -> updateCeiling(usd) on Save, no comparison to liveForecast.mtd_usd, no confirm); src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py:2156-2183 (update_spend_ceiling accepts any monthly_usd>0, no floor/warning relative to MTD); src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1665-1690 (once MTD>=ceiling, every dispatch is denied fleet-wide via quota_skip); frontend/src/hooks/use-fleet-halt.ts:1-30 (halt is detected only from actual quota_skip dispatch-attempt rows, not from the ceiling mutation itself, so the banner lags until a real dispatch is denied)
findings.detail: SpendPage.tsx's own comment (line 2296) calls the ceiling halt 'the most consequential thing the spend system can do', and gives it a dedicated red banner + attempts drawer for after-the-fact detection. But the write path that triggers it has none of the safety the design bar requires for a not-cleanly-reversible action: no inline comparison of the new value to current MTD spend, no 'this will halt dispatch immediately' warning, no confirm dialog (unlike the routing-rule delete right below it on the same page, which got exactly this treatment under bu-6jv4m.2), and the mutation's onSuccess only invalidates ['spend-forecast'] -- not the fleet-halt query -- so FleetHaltBanner does not update until its own poll or the bus event from the next (now-denied) dispatch. An owner who mistypes a lower ceiling gets zero feedback that they just stopped every butler in the fleet until something downstream fails.

findings.title: CeilingEdit's inline input has no aria-label and no Enter-to-save / Escape-to-cancel

audits.jarvis_gap: Today's /system page is an unusually disciplined ownership-facts surface: nearly every tile (Backup, Drift, Deployment, Egress, Security Posture, Insight Delivery, Standing Conditions) goes out of its way to render an honest 'unknown'/'unverified' instead of a fabricated all-clear, and the verdict banner composes a real judgment from those same sources with sources-still-loading guards. The chat surface (FloatingChatWidget/ChatPanel) is equally careful about SSE error classification, optimistic-message reconciliation, and stop-turn honesty. What is missing is the last mile of JARVIS behavior: (1) every fact on this page must also be a door to its own evidence, and today the Standing Conditions ledger -- the one tile that carries owner commitments and open incidents -- renders as inert text with no way to reach the session, source, or audit trail that produced it; (2) the page's one keyboard hot-loop action ('r' / 'Refresh system status') silently only refreshes two of the page's eleven-plus data sources, so an owner who trusts the shortcut's label can act on stale Backup/Drift/Deployment/Security data without knowing it; (3) the full-width Ecosystem Topology graph -- the page's single richest drill-down surface, wired to real butler/connector detail routes -- is reachable only by mouse click, with no keyboard path to activate a node, breaking the keyboard-first mandate for a large fraction of the page's real estate. An ideal version keeps every one of the existing honesty guarantees, but turns every condition row into a link that reaches the session/source/entity that raised it, makes the refresh affordance either honest about its scope or complete in what it refreshes, and gives the topology graph the same node-level keyboard activation every other list row on this page already has (RowLink on ButlerHeartbeatTile is the pattern to copy).
