audits.ideal: A world-class fleet console is verifiable in five seconds through any channel, including a screen reader and a keyboard alone. Accessibility is structural, not per-page courtesy: the router frame — not each page's discipline — guarantees every route has a document title, an h1, and a spoken route change; one focus vocabulary (a single ≥3:1 `--focus` outline token, non-overridable, identical on native controls, Radix primitives and hand-rolled widgets) is the only way focus is ever drawn; the type scale is seven named rem-based roles minted as tokens, so browser font-size preferences scale the whole dashboard and no surface invents a 9.5px size; section rhythm is carried by eyebrow-*styled headings*, so the eyebrow aesthetic and the h1→h2→h3 outline are the same object and heading-navigation works as the SR equivalent of scanning; every list with a keyboard cursor goes through one `useListCursor` primitive that owns roving focus or `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-selected`, and an `announce()` on every cursor and bulk-selection change, so a consequential merge/archive/forget selection is never a visual-only state; every chart — recharts or hand-rolled SVG — passes through one `ChartFrame` that mints role/name and a keyboard-reachable tabular readout of the same series, so the numbers behind a verdict are a door, not a hover; load-bearing explanations (breaker exclusions, verification failures, routing evidence) live in `Tip`, never a native `title=`; and motion honors `prefers-reduced-motion` in JS as well as CSS. Each of these is enforced by a lint rule or a typed primitive in the same style the repo already uses for hex colors, `animate-pulse`, `window.confirm`, and hand-rolled overlays — so the guarantee holds for code not yet written.
audits.jarvis_gap: Today the primitives are unusually good and the generalization is unusually incomplete: every one of these mechanisms exists somewhere and is enforced nowhere. There is a shell announcer (`lib/shell-announcer.ts`) used by 5 call sites; a `Tip` primitive written expressly to retire `title=` (components/ui/tip.tsx:34-45) adopted by 8 files while 54 raw `title=` attributes remain, several carrying breaker-exclusion and verification-failure reasons; a `useModalChoreography` overlay contract backed by a lint rule; `role="img" aria-label` on ~20 hand-rolled SVGs and on zero of the 10 recharts charts; a global 18:1 focus floor at index.css:619 written with `:where()` (zero specificity) that the five most-used primitives override with `outline-none` + a 1.52:1 `ring-ring/50`; a `contrastRatio()` helper with no consumer outside its own test; and a `Page` primitive that owns `document.title` and the route announcement which exactly half the page files never import, leaving 20 routes on the literal tab title `frontend`. The binding spec compounds one gap rather than closing it: `Eyebrow Section Titles` mandates section titles "in lieu of headings" and `components/ui/Eyebrow.tsx:18` accordingly renders only span/div/p, so across 376 component files there are 34 `<h2>` against 83 `<Eyebrow>` and 197 hand-rolled eyebrow clusters — heading navigation, the screen-reader equivalent of five-second scanning, is structurally unavailable. bu-6jv4m.12 will close the route-state axe manifest, alpha-composited *text* contrast, and the existence of focus replacements; it does not touch non-text (1.4.11) contrast of the replacements, the heading outline, virtual-cursor semantics, chart alternatives, the `title=` tail, the px type scale, or JS-driven motion.

findings.title: The global focus floor is written at zero specificity and is overridden by every core primitive with a 1.5:1 replacement
findings.evidence: frontend/src/index.css:619 (`:where(a, button, [role='button'], [tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--fg) }`); frontend/src/components/ui/button.tsx:8, input.tsx:11-12, select.tsx:32, textarea.tsx:11, tabs.tsx:67 (all carry `outline-none` + `focus-visible:ring-ring/50 focus-visible:ring-[3px]`); frontend/src/index.css:55 (`--ring: oklch(0.708 0 0)`), :511 (dark `oklch(0.556 0 0)`); openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:385-391 ("Focus is visible — 2px outline of `--fg` at 2px offset")
findings.detail: Measured (OKLCH→sRGB, WCAG formula) against the real tokens: `ring-ring/50` composites to 1.52:1 on light `--bg` / 1.87:1 on dark `--bg`; full `ring-ring` reaches only 2.48:1 light. WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for focus-state indicators; the spec-mandated `--fg` outline measures 18.01:1. Because index.css:619 wraps its selector in `:where()`, the rule has the same specificity as the `.outline-none` utility and loses on source order to Tailwind's utilities layer — so the floor is decorative wherever a primitive opts out. This is a second focus dialect at 88 `ring-ring` occurrences across 49 files plus 135 `outline-none` sites. bu-6jv4m.12 AC5 requires a *replacement* to exist; it does not require the replacement to meet 3:1 or to be the spec's single vocabulary, so every one of these sites can satisfy .12 and still be a 1.5:1 focus ring.

findings.title: The design language mandates section titles that are not headings, collapsing the screen-reader heading outline fleet-wide
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:236 ("Sections SHALL be titled with eyebrows … in lieu of headings"); frontend/src/components/ui/Eyebrow.tsx:18 (`as?: "span" | "div" | "p"`), :31; 83 `<Eyebrow>` uses across 23 files and 197 hand-rolled `tracking-[0.1Nem]` eyebrow clusters vs 34 `<h2>` in 26 files out of 376 non-test .tsx files
findings.detail: Heading navigation (rotor / H-key) is how a screen-reader user performs the five-second scan the north star promises sighted operators. On Dispatch-language pages the outline is one `<h1>` (via `Display`, components/ui/Display.tsx:36, default `as="h1"`) followed by nothing — every band, ledger, rail and receipt panel is titled by a `<span>`. This is not a page-level miss but a spec requirement, so it will reproduce in every future surface; it is invisible to axe (no rule fires on a styled span) and therefore outside bu-6jv4m.12's axe-manifest scope. The fix is non-visual: an `Eyebrow level={2|3}` that emits `h2`/`h3` with byte-identical styling.

findings.title: Half of all routes bypass the Page primitive, so they have no document title and never announce the route change
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/page.tsx:340-350 (sole `document.title` owner and sole `announce(\`Page: ${title}\`)` caller); 20 of 40 files in frontend/src/pages/ do not import it — ApprovalsPage, CalendarWorkspacePage, DecisionsPage, EducationPage, HealthOverviewPage, IngestionConnectors/Filters/TimelinePage, Meals/Measurements/MedicationsPage, MemoryPage, Qa{Overview,InvestigationDetail,PatrolDetail}Page, SecretsPage, Settings{Console,Models,Permissions}Page, TimelinePage; frontend/index.html:10 (`<title>frontend</title>`); frontend/src/router-config.tsx:95,105,129,150,167 (all are real routes)
findings.detail: WCAG 2.4.2 (Page Titled) fails on those 20 routes: the tab reads `frontend` or retains the previously-visited page's title, and in an SPA the browser fires no navigation announcement, so `lib/shell-announcer.ts` — built precisely to solve this (RootLayout.tsx:38-46) — stays silent. Title and route announcement are per-page opt-in when they are properties of routing; `router-config.tsx` already knows every route's identity. Not covered by bu-6jv4m.12, whose ACs concern axe/keyboard/contrast/focus, not navigation announcement.

findings.title: Keyboard list cursors and bulk selection are visual-only on the entity index — the consequential merge/archive/forget surface
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/relationship/EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:1541-1546 (`role="grid"` on a plain div wrapping `<EntityTable>`), :1313-1371 (`handleListKeyDown`: Arrow/Shift-Arrow/Space/Enter over a numeric `cursor`), :686-687 (`aria-selected` bound to the *cursor*, not to `selectedIds`), :702-707 (checkbox is the only carrier of multi-selection); zero `aria-activedescendant` in the entire frontend; bulk verbs at :1495-1530 (Merge/Archive/Forget)
findings.detail: Arrow keys move a virtual cursor without moving DOM focus and without `aria-activedescendant`, so a screen-reader user hears nothing as the cursor traverses rows; Shift+Arrow range-selects an arbitrary number of entities with no announcement and no `aria-selected` on the selected rows; `role="grid"` promises a grid keyboard/ownership model the div does not implement (its only child is a `<table>`, an invalid owned child). The correct pattern already exists twice in the repo and was never generalized: pages/ButlersPage.tsx:181-189 moves real DOM focus, and pages/SpendPage.tsx:1524-1577 announces every reorder step through `announce()`. Distinct from bu-6jv4m.12 (keyboard *scripts* over route states, not the widget contract itself).

findings.title: Ten recharts charts carry no accessible name, role, or text alternative, while every hand-rolled SVG does
findings.evidence: `role="img"` + `aria-label` on ~20 hand-rolled SVGs (components/ingestion/connectors/Sparkline.tsx:93, components/butlers/DayBars.tsx:62, components/relationship/ActivitySparkline.tsx:63, components/chronicles/BalanceRings.tsx:77, …) vs zero `accessibilityLayer` and zero aria on the recharts wrappers: components/costs/CostStripeChart.tsx:227-229, components/dashboard/SessionStripeChart.tsx:214, components/health/MeasurementChart.tsx:437, components/education/MasteryTrendChart.tsx:65, CrossTopicChart.tsx:36, components/butler-detail/{ButlerGeneralCollectionsTab.tsx:369, ButlerHealthMeasurementsTab.tsx:330, ButlerFinanceFinancesTab.tsx:229, ButlerHomeDevicesTab.tsx:438, ButlerEducationReviewsTab.tsx:619}
findings.detail: The charts that carry the spend, session-volume, mastery and measurement signal are unnamed graphics containers; their values exist only inside hover tooltips, so the evidence behind a verdict is reachable by pointer alone. The `role="img" aria-label` convention is established and consistently applied in the hand-rolled family — it simply stops at the library boundary, and nothing enforces it. No shared chart frame exists to attach the name or a tabular readout to.

findings.title: The Tip primitive that exists to retire load-bearing `title=` has migrated 8 files; 54 raw `title=` attributes remain, including failure explanations
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/tip.tsx:34-45 ("the focusable, screen-reader-announced replacement for a load-bearing `title=`… a native `title` tooltip never surfaces on keyboard focus"); 8 importing files; 54 raw `title=` on host elements across ~26 files, worst offenders pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx (7), pages/SettingsModelsPage.tsx:1449, :1476, :1494, :1501, pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx (4), components/schedules/ScheduleTable.tsx (3), components/system/StandingConditionsTile.tsx (3), components/layout/Sidebar.tsx (3)
findings.detail: SettingsModelsPage puts exactly the content the north star calls consequential behind hover-only text: the verification-failure reason on a `✗` span (:1449), the reason a model is `Excluded by breaker after N consecutive dispatch failures` (:1476), and the routing-score evidence `n=…, p95…, success…` (:1494-1501). A keyboard or touch user cannot reach any of it and a screen reader announces it inconsistently at best — failure declines to explain itself through a non-visual channel. The repo enforces far less consequential invariants (animate-pulse, window.confirm, hex literals) with `no-restricted-syntax`; `title=` has no such rule.

findings.title: The type system is 1053 hard-px sizes in 21 distinct values against a 7-role spec scale, with 92 sites below 10px
findings.evidence: 1053 `text-[Npx]` occurrences across 157 .tsx files and zero `text-[Nrem]`; distribution 10px×497, 11px×340, 9.5px×47, 9px×40, plus off-scale 12.5/13.5/11.5/10.5px; 8-9px sites in pages/SettingsModelsPage.tsx, components/layout/Sidebar.tsx, components/relationship/PlexPage.tsx, components/butlers/StatusBoardCell.tsx and 16 more; openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:201-209 defines exactly seven roles (44/24/14/13/16/10/11px); the primitives themselves hard-code px (components/ui/Display.tsx:43, Title.tsx:38, Eyebrow.tsx:36)
findings.detail: Two compounding problems. (1) Absolute px ignores the browser's default-font-size preference entirely — a low-vision user who sets 24px base sees no change anywhere in the dashboard (WCAG 1.4.4 is satisfiable by zoom, but the *stated* accessibility floor in spec.md:18-19 is not met in spirit for the 10-11px mono that carries timestamps, deltas, IDs and eyebrows — 837 of the 1053 sites). (2) Five sizes in active use (9, 8, 9.5, 10.5, 11.5, 12.5, 13.5px) are not in the spec scale at all, and 92 of them sit below the smallest legal role, usually paired with `--mfg`/`--dim`. Contrast tokens are governed and audited; size is not.

findings.title: JS-initiated smooth scrolling escapes the global reduced-motion floor the CSS rule claims to own
findings.evidence: frontend/src/index.css:787-796 (global `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` collapsing animation/transition and `scroll-behavior: auto !important`), :773-785 (comment: "This single global rule collapses every CSS animation/transition… The JS hook remains the right tool for canvas/SVG work"); explicit `behavior: "smooth"` at components/chat/MessageThread.tsx:305, components/ingestion/TimelineTab.tsx:1280, components/ingestion/timeline/EventDrawer.tsx:642, pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:3181, pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2707
findings.detail: Per CSSOM-View, an explicit `behavior` argument to `scrollIntoView()` overrides the computed `scroll-behavior`, so `scroll-behavior: auto !important` cannot reach these five call sites. MessageThread.tsx:305 fires on every incoming message, making it repeated involuntary motion in a live chat surface for a vestibular-sensitive user. `usePrefersReducedMotion` (hooks/use-prefers-reduced-motion.ts) exists and is consulted by exactly 2 components (RegisterCrossfade, ButlerHealthMeasurementsTab); the floor's own comment asserts a completeness it does not have.

moves.title: Mint one focus token and make the floor unbeatable: `--focus` at ≥3:1 in both themes, `outline-none` bannable only with a measured replacement
moves.why: spec.md:385-391 already mandates a single 2px `--fg` focus outline; today index.css:619 loses the cascade to `outline-none` in the five primitives and the replacement measures 1.52:1 light / 1.87:1 dark against WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1. Payoff: every interactive element in 376 files gets one measured focus vocabulary, and bu-6jv4m.12's AC5 lands on a replacement that is actually compliant rather than merely present.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/index.css:55,511,619; frontend/src/components/ui/{button,input,select,textarea,tabs,checkbox,switch}.tsx; frontend/eslint.config.js (NO_UNGUARDED_OUTLINE_NONE_SELECTORS at :2544, currently allowlisted to 4 secrets-passport files); frontend/src/lib/contrast.ts:79-88 (contrastRatio/WCAG_AA_NORMAL_TEXT, no consumer today); frontend/src/lib/focus-visible-floor.test.ts
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add `--focus` (light/dark) and a `WCAG_AA_NON_TEXT = 3.0` constant; extend lib/contrast.test.ts to assert `--focus` and every state/border token used as a component boundary clears 3:1 in both themes, reading the literals from index.css as the existing test already does. 2) Rewrite index.css:619 without `:where()` (or as a `@layer utilities` rule) so it outranks Tailwind's `outline-none`, and delete `ring-ring` from the seven ui/ primitives. 3) Codemod the 88 `ring-ring` sites to the token. 4) Promote NO_UNGUARDED_OUTLINE_NONE_SELECTORS repo-wide and add a companion selector banning `ring-ring`.

moves.title: Make the eyebrow a heading: `Eyebrow level={2|3}` plus a spec amendment, so the rhythm and the outline are the same object
moves.why: spec.md:236 mandates eyebrows "in lieu of headings" and Eyebrow.tsx:18 obeys, leaving 34 `<h2>` against 83 Eyebrows and 197 hand-rolled eyebrow clusters — heading navigation, the SR equivalent of the five-second scan, does not exist on Dispatch pages. Zero visual change; pure semantic recovery.
moves.integration_points: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md §Eyebrow Section Titles (:234-246); frontend/src/components/ui/Eyebrow.tsx:16-31; frontend/src/components/ui/{Display,Title}.tsx; frontend/eslint.config.js PRIMITIVE_REDECLARATION_SELECTORS (:132) already bans local Eyebrow forks
moves.slice_plan: 1) Amend the spec requirement to "eyebrow-*styled* headings": a section eyebrow SHALL render as the correct heading level for its nesting depth. 2) Add `level?: 2|3|4` to Eyebrow (default keeps span for genuinely inline eyebrows like a metadata line), rendering `h2`/`h3`/`h4` with identical classes. 3) Migrate the 83 `<Eyebrow>` section titles and the 197 hand-rolled clusters onto the primitive with a level. 4) Add a route-level test asserting each page yields a monotonic h1→h2 outline.

moves.title: Route-level accessibility frame: title, h1 and route announcement become properties of routing, not page discipline
moves.why: components/ui/page.tsx:340-350 is the sole owner of `document.title` and the route announcement, and 20 of 40 page files never import it, so those routes read `frontend` (index.html:10) and announce nothing — WCAG 2.4.2 failing on half the fleet. The router already knows every route's identity (router-config.tsx, lib/route-registry.ts).
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/router-config.tsx:29-35 (`shellPage`/`routeElement`); frontend/src/lib/route-registry.ts; frontend/src/components/ui/page.tsx:340-350; frontend/src/lib/shell-announcer.ts; frontend/src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx:40-46; the 20 non-Page files in frontend/src/pages/
moves.slice_plan: 1) Move the title/announce effect out of Page into `routeElement`, sourced from the route registry's label, so it fires for every route regardless of what the page renders. 2) Keep Page's own title as an override for parameterized routes (butler/entity/session detail). 3) Assert in router.test.tsx that every route in the registry sets a non-default document.title and pushes exactly one announcement. 4) Then migrate the 20 pages onto Page for the h1/error/loading archetypes, which becomes a purely visual refactor.

moves.title: One `useListCursor` primitive owning roving focus, `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-selected` and selection announcements
moves.why: EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:1313-1371 drives a virtual cursor and Shift-range bulk selection feeding Merge/Archive/Forget (:1495-1530) with no DOM focus movement, no activedescendant, and no announcement; ButlersPage.tsx:181-189 (real focus) and SpendPage.tsx:1524-1577 (announcements) each solved half the problem locally. audits.jarvis_gap: Today the dashboard has genuinely strong speed primitives — one multiplexed fleet socket with a declarative cache-patch registry and a drift-catching coverage manifest (frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts, event-cache-manifest.ts), bus-aware poll cadence with lint-enforced named tokens (lib/poll-policy.ts, eslint.config.js POLL_POLICY_SELECTORS), a shared optimistic-mutation layer with an explicit OPTIMISTIC vs HONEST-PENDING doctrine (hooks/use-optimistic-mutation.ts), a module-scope undo-window scheduler that survives unmount (hooks/use-undo-window.ts), hover-intent prefetch of both route chunks and query data (hooks/use-prefetch-on-intent.ts, use-route-chunk-prefetch-on-intent.ts), a never-blank stale-list affordance (components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx, 90 call sites), and deliberate vendor chunking. The ideal is a dashboard where the owner's five-second fleet verification never pays for a round trip it could have avoided and never loses a scrap of context. The gap is that almost every one of those primitives stopped at the surface that motivated it. The live spine reaches 8 of ~20 domains and, even there, is payload-blind: every event throws away its own data and re-fetches over HTTP, while the one true delta-merge surface (Settings Console) proves the better shape exists and was never generalized. Data prefetch covers 13 of 46 destinations while chunk prefetch covers all 46, and nothing survives a reload — no cache persistence, no idle warming, so every F5 is a cold, skeleton-first boot in which even the owner's timezone is a guess. Nothing in the app manages scroll across route boundaries, so back-navigation from any detail page to a list drops the operator at the top and forward navigation inherits the previous page's offset. There is not one memo or transition boundary in a 237k-line frontend whose largest render root is 4,700 lines and re-renders on every pointermove of a calendar drag. And failure is a four-second dead end: 234 error toasts, none with a retry.
audits.ideal: Speed is a declared, enforced property of every destination rather than a per-surface craft decision. One capability manifest is the single source of truth for what a destination costs: each entry declares its route chunk, its warm-up cohort (or an explicit, rendered "no warm-up because…" receipt), and its live-update source — either a fleet event type or an honest "polled every N because no event source exists" that the UI shows rather than hides. The fleet bus carries typed, versioned payloads that patch the query cache in place (setQueryData) at socket latency, with invalidation demoted to a reconciliation sweep; the write path of every domain publishes onto the existing Postgres NOTIFY transport, so memory, health, secrets, QA, education and entity surfaces go live for the same cost the eight covered domains already paid. Cold start has memory: the last-known cache is restored from IndexedDB and rendered under an explicit "as of" stamp until revalidated, so a reload shows yesterday's fleet instantly and never lets stale data wear current-data authority; owner time is a resolved clock, never a hard-coded fallback silently flipping under the owner mid-read. Context is inviolable: the shell owns scroll memory keyed to history entries, filters and selection live in the URL, and every failed mutation keeps its input and offers a persistent retry in place. Render cost is bounded by construction — high-frequency state (drag, pointer, type-ahead) is rAF-coalesced and deferred behind memo boundaries, and page roots have a size ceiling. Every latency knob in the app — poll cadence, debounce, toast lifetime, undo window, prefetch delay — is a named token in one policy module, enforced by the same no-restricted-syntax family that already governs poll cadence, so a reviewer can read the app's entire latency budget in one file.

findings.title: No scroll management at any route boundary; the shell's scroll container persists across navigations
findings.detail: Shell renders the app's only scroll container as an inner element (`<main className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto">`) inside a `h-screen overflow-hidden` root, so the document itself never scrolls and browser-native scroll restoration cannot apply. `<ScrollRestoration/>` is never rendered (zero occurrences repo-wide) and nothing writes scrollTop at a route change — the only scrollTop/scrollIntoView writes are three component-local cases (calendar time-grid default hour, log tail autoscroll, chat thread). Because `<main>` is outer to `<Outlet/>` (layouts/RootLayout.tsx:108), its offset survives the route swap in both directions: navigating from a deep-scrolled Sessions/Timeline/Memory list into a detail route lands the operator mid-page on content they never scrolled to, and browser-Back to the list drops them at the position the detail page happened to leave. This is the skill's top-severity class ("Context survives: navigation, refresh, and failure preserve typed input, selection, scroll position") and it is absent on every list surface at once.

findings.title: Zero memo/transition boundaries in a 237k-line frontend whose largest render root re-renders on every pointermove
findings.detail: `React.memo`, `useDeferredValue`, `useTransition` and `startTransition` have zero non-test occurrences in frontend/src. CalendarWorkspacePage's root component spans lines 2481-7247 (~4,700 lines), owns 32 useState hooks and ~12 useQuery subscriptions, and holds `gridDrag`/`movedGhost` — pure pointer-frame state — at that root. `handleGridPointerMove` calls `setGridDrag` on every pointermove event (three branches: create/move/resize) with no rAF coalescing, so a single calendar drag re-renders the entire workspace tree (week grid, agenda, panels, dialogs, every query consumer) at pointer-event rate. The same shape recurs at smaller scale on EntityDetailPage (3,333 lines), SpendPage (3,027, 19 useState), TimelineTab (2,703) and PlexPage (2,190, an xyflow graph), all of which co-locate filter/search text state with chart, map and graph regions in one un-memoized subtree — the <100ms typing-echo budget is unprotected by construction, not by measurement.

findings.title: The live spine covers 8 of ~20 domains; the generic NOTIFY transport was built once and never extended to the rest
findings.detail: `publish_fleet_event` accepts any event_type and rides a generic Postgres NOTIFY channel (RFC 0022), but only eight publish sites exist: approvals gate, approvals email_guard, core/sessions, calendar, filtered_event_buffer, spawner (spend), chronicler jobs, _notifications, and switchboard ingest. Every other domain write is invisible to the bus, so its surfaces can only poll on fixed timers with no bus-awareness and no degradation signal: use-health.ts (13 queries at HEALTH_POLL_MS/HEALTH_POLL_SLOW_MS), use-memory.ts (9 queries, 15-60s), use-system.ts (9), use-education.ts (11), use-general.ts, use-qa.ts, use-schedules.ts, use-state.ts, use-secrets-inventory.ts, use-ingestion.ts, use-finance.ts, use-travel.ts, use-owntracks.ts, use-audit-log.ts, use-butler-logs.ts. The result is a two-tier dashboard: approvals/sessions/spend/calendar update in the same beat as the fleet, while a memory write, a secret rotation, a QA investigation transition or a health measurement can sit unseen for 15-120 seconds — and the coverage manifest only enforces the eight domains that already had events, so a hook with no live source is indistinguishable from one that lost its coverage.

findings.title: The fleet bus is payload-blind: every patch discards event.data and forces a REST round trip, and the one delta-merge surface was never generalized
findings.detail: Every entry in EVENT_CACHE_REGISTRY calls invalidateQueries only; `event.data` is read solely to pick an id for a narrower key. So the live path is socket -> invalidate -> full HTTP refetch -> render, even when the event already carries the changed row: a session event invalidates 7 key prefixes, a spend event 7 keys, a calendar event 10, and none of the resulting refetches is cheap (session-aggregate, spend-forecast, the ten calendar workspace projections). `applyFleetEvent` also performs each patch synchronously per envelope with no coalescing, so the reconnect snapshot replays the whole ring buffer (up to 200 events) as 200 sequential cache walks. The counter-example is in-repo and proven: settings_console.py runs a server-side 5s diff loop emitting typed header_delta/attention_add/attention_remove payloads, and use-settings-console-live.ts merges them into local state in place, explicitly to avoid "a full aggregation re-fetch on every delta" — exactly the cost every other surface still pays. That pattern was built for one page and generalized to none.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:57-73 (approvalPatch), :88-95 (spendPatch), :126-146 (sessionPatch), :190-204 (calendarPatch), and the applyFleetEvent tail (no coalescing); frontend/src/hooks/use-settings-console-live.ts:1-31; src/butlers/api/routers/settings_console.py:620-700 (run_settings_console_delta_loop, _CONSOLE_DELTA_INTERVAL_S=5.0)

findings.title: Cold start has no memory: no cache persistence, no idle warming, and query prefetch covers 13 of 46 destinations while chunk prefetch covers all 46
findings.detail: The shell capability manifest derives the route-chunk projection automatically from every entry's `loader` (route-chunk-registry.ts maps all non-dynamic capabilities), but `queryWarmup` is an optional field present on only 13 of 46 entries. The 33 without it include almost every high-traffic rail destination — /butlers, /qa, /approvals (list), /decisions, /memory, /entities, /secrets, /settings, /notifications, /issues, /audit-log, /system, /education, /calendar, /chronicles and all six /health subpages — so a deliberate hover warms the JS but not one row of data, and the click still pays a full cold fetch. Nothing warms at idle either (`requestIdleCallback` has zero occurrences). And the query cache is memory-only: query-client.ts configures no persister, so every reload, browser restart or crash re-renders the entire dashboard as skeletons even though the last-known fleet state was perfectly serviceable to show under an "as of" stamp. The compounding effect lands hardest on the north-star surface: DashboardPage fires ~14 independent queries on mount, each with its own loading state, all cold, all unwarmed.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts (13 `queryWarmup:` occurrences vs 46 `path:` entries; e.g. :117-120 /butlers, /qa, /approvals, /decisions, /memory have none); frontend/src/lib/route-chunk-registry.ts:11-17 (chunk projection is total); frontend/src/lib/query-client.ts:3-11 (no persister); grep: zero `requestIdleCallback`/`persistQueryClient` in frontend/src; frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:112-185

findings.title: Failure is a four-second dead end: 234 error toasts, zero retry affordances, and the Toaster runs under the repo's own actionable-toast bar
findings.detail: There are 234 non-test `toast.error` call sites across the frontend and not one attaches a retry action — the only toast actions in the app are five Undo affordances. A failed mutation therefore ends the interaction: the operator must re-locate the control and re-enter the input by hand, which is the skill's explicit "never make the user re-request" violation, at scale. Worse, the failure explanation self-destructs: `<Toaster />` is mounted with no `duration`, so it inherits sonner's TOAST_LIFETIME of 4000ms — under the >=5s floor the repo itself already applies to its Undo toasts (duration: UNDO_WINDOW_MS = 5_000) and under it for action-bearing toasts that set no duration at all (AttentionRail's four routed actions). A four-second error toast on a mutation that then leaves the surface looking unchanged is failure quietly resolving into apparent health.
findings.evidence: grep: 234 non-test `toast.error` sites in frontend/src, zero `label: "Retry"`; frontend/src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx:120 (`<Toaster />`, no duration); node_modules/sonner/dist/index.mjs:417 (TOAST_LIFETIME = 4000); frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:1901-1902 and pages/ButlersPage.tsx:217-218 (duration: UNDO_WINDOW_MS); frontend/src/components/memory/AttentionRail.tsx:234,260,277,288 (action toasts, no duration)

findings.title: Owner time is guessed on every cold boot and can stay guessed forever
findings.detail: App.tsx wraps the entire router in `AppTimezoneProvider timezone={generalSettings?.data?.timezone ?? DEFAULT_TZ}`, where DEFAULT_TZ is the hard-coded literal "Asia/Singapore". Until GET /api/settings/general resolves, every timestamp, day bucket, date-key and owner-day boundary in the app first paints under that guess and then silently re-renders to the real zone — a value that carries full current-data authority while being provisional. The settings query sets `retry: false`, so a single failed request leaves the whole dashboard rendering owner time in a hard-coded default indefinitely, with no pending state, no failure state and nothing on screen saying the clock is unresolved.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/App.tsx:14-16; frontend/src/components/ui/timezone-context.tsx:25 (DEFAULT_TZ = "Asia/Singapore"), :32 (context default); frontend/src/hooks/use-general-settings.ts:9-16 (`retry: false`)

findings.title: Every latency knob except poll cadence is an anonymous magic number; four different type-ahead debounces coexist
findings.detail: The repo built exactly the right enforcement mechanism for one knob: a repo-wide no-restricted-syntax selector forces every `refetchInterval` onto a named poll-policy token, with a documented rationale for why a bare number hides intent. Nothing analogous governs the other latency knobs, and they have drifted accordingly. Type-ahead delay is 180ms in two places (both hand-rolled setTimeouts that bypass the shared useDebounce hook), 200ms for the entity finder, 300ms for three list pages plus global search plus conversation search, and 400ms for the calendar butler-event draft — the same "type, then see results" interaction with a 2.2x spread and no stated policy. The undo grace window is likewise declared three separate times as the literal 5_000, and PREFETCH_INTENT_DELAY_MS / ROUTE_CHUNK_PREFETCH_INTENT_DELAY_MS are two independent 120ms constants for the same hover-intent gesture.

findings.title: placeholderData is set without a paired staleness affordance on several surfaces
findings.detail: `placeholderData: (prev) => prev` appears on ~25 query hooks so a filter or cursor change keeps the previous rows rather than blanking — correct stale-while-revalidate. The matching honesty affordance (FetchingDim, which sets aria-busy and dims stale rows during a background refetch) is adopted at 90 call sites but the pairing is unenforced, so surfaces exist where prior-filter rows render at full authority while a new query is in flight: ApprovalsPage sets a lane-guarded placeholderData with no FetchingDim anywhere in the file, and the contacts/entity-search hooks feed EntitiesIndexPage, which instead swaps in a Skeleton on isFetching — a third, inconsistent behaviour for the same state. Given the north star's "staleness never wears current-data authority", the pairing belongs in the query layer, not in each page's judgement.

moves.title: Shell scroll memory: one route-boundary scroll authority for the persistent <main> container
moves.why: Doctrine: interaction-speed names destroying work-in-progress and losing scroll/selection across navigation as the top-severity defect class, worse than any latency finding; the single-pane doctrine (docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md, Detect/Diagnose/Act loop) assumes the operator dives into a session and comes back to where they were. Today Shell.tsx:89 is a persistent inner scroll container with no reset and no restore, so every list->detail->back triage cycle in the fleet — Sessions, Timeline, Memory, Issues, Notifications, Audit Log — costs the operator their place. Payoff: the diagnose loop stops re-scrolling.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add `useShellScrollMemory` in RootLayout: on every navigation, write the outgoing `<main>` scrollTop into history state keyed by location.key; on POP, restore after the route's first non-placeholder paint; on PUSH, reset to 0. 2) Give Shell a ref to `<main>` and expose it via context so a page with its own inner scroller (Calendar time grid, chat thread) can opt out or register its own. 3) Cooperate with placeholderData: restore only once the restored route reports content height >= the saved offset, otherwise queue one rAF retry, so a skeleton-height frame does not clamp the restore to 0. 4) Playwright case per list surface: scroll, open detail, Back, assert offset within 4px. 5) Lint/test guard that RootLayout still mounts the hook.

moves.title: Payload-carrying fleet events: typed event data + setQueryData patches, invalidation demoted to reconciliation
moves.why: Doctrine: interaction-speed requires the UI to move at the speed of the signal and treats "refetch every time to be safe" as a latency defect wearing a correctness costume; the north star wants an unbroken signal-to-session spine. The bus already delivers the change at socket latency and then throws the payload away, so the owner waits socket + full-list HTTP for every live update (event-cache-registry.ts sessionPatch invalidates 7 prefixes, calendarPatch 10). The proof the better shape works is already in-repo and used by exactly one surface (settings_console.py's delta loop + use-settings-console-live.ts). Payoff: live surfaces update in one hop instead of two, and the API stops re-aggregating on every event.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Define a typed payload contract per event type shared between src/butlers/api/routers/events.py EVENT_TYPES and a new frontend `fleet-event-payloads.ts` (a row shape sufficient to patch: session summary, approval summary, spend delta, ingestion event header), with a contract test asserting both sides agree. 2) Extend CachePatch to `patch(qc, event)` implementations that call setQueryData for the row-level keys they can satisfy and fall back to invalidateQueries when the payload is absent/oversized (NOTIFY caps at 7800 bytes — the fallback is mandatory, not optional). 3) Coalesce: buffer envelopes in applyFleetEvent within one microtask/animation frame and apply a deduped patch set, so a reconnect snapshot of 200 events performs one pass, not 200. 4) Extend EVENT_CACHE_COVERAGE_MANIFEST rows with `mode: "patch" | "invalidate"` so the existing coverage test also catches a patch silently degrading to invalidate. 5) Migrate settings-console's bespoke reducer onto the same registry mode so there is one live-update mechanism, not two.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts; frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-manifest.ts; frontend/src/hooks/use-event-stream.ts; frontend/src/hooks/use-settings-console-live.ts; src/butlers/api/routers/events.py:60-110; src/butlers/fleet_events.py

moves.title: Extend the live spine to every domain: domain-write events + a mandatory liveness declaration per hook
moves.why: Doctrine: vision.md's success marker is a system whose state the owner can trust without asking, and the north star forbids staleness wearing current-data authority. The NOTIFY transport is already generic (src/butlers/fleet_events.py) but only 8 write paths publish, so memory, health, secrets, QA, education, entities, schedules and state-store surfaces are second-class: 15-120s fixed polls, no bus-awareness, no visible degradation. Payoff: one mechanism makes ~12 more surfaces live for a fraction of what the first eight cost, and every remaining poller states its reason on screen instead of implying freshness.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add a `domain_write` event type carrying {schema, table, op, id} and publish it from the shared write path (or per-module write helpers) for memory, health, education, secrets, entities, schedules, state, QA — reusing publish_fleet_event so no new transport is needed. 2) Map schema/table -> query-key prefixes in one registry table on the frontend, so adding a domain is a data row, not a hook. 3) Make liveness a required declaration: every useQuery hook with a refetchInterval must appear in the coverage manifest either with an event type or with `liveness: {source: "poll", reason, cadence}`; the existing coverage test enforces presence. 4) Render the declaration: a shared `SourceCadence` affordance on polled surfaces stating "polled every Ns — no live source", so the honest case is visible rather than inferred. 5) Migrate the newly covered hooks onto useBusAwarePollInterval so a dead socket degrades to fast polling on those surfaces too.

moves.title: Warm-start contract: required queryWarmup per capability, idle warming, and a persisted cache rendered under an honest as-of stamp
moves.why: Doctrine: interaction-speed mandates preloading what the user will probably want next and treats a blank screen that could have shown yesterday's data as a defect — except where stale misleads, which the north star answers with a visible staleness mark. Today the chunk projection is total and the data projection is 13/46, nothing warms at idle, and no cache survives a reload, so the five-second fleet verification starts from zero on every F5. Payoff: the rail's destinations open with data already there, and a reload shows the last-known fleet instantly, honestly labelled.

moves.title: useRecoverableMutation: every failed mutation keeps its input and offers retry in place
moves.why: Doctrine: interaction-speed requires "never make the user re-request: if it failed, offer retry with the input preserved", and toasts carrying an action must persist >=5s; the north star requires that failure never impersonates health. Today 234 error toasts offer no recovery and self-destruct in 4s (sonner default, Toaster sets no duration), after which the surface looks normal again. Payoff: the third loop of the single-pane doctrine (Act) becomes recoverable rather than a re-do-it-by-hand loop.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add `useRecoverableMutation` alongside the existing optimistic/honest-pending split: it captures the mutation variables on error, exposes `lastFailure {variables, error, retry}`, and posts a persistent toast whose action re-fires the exact call. 2) Add a shared inline `MutationFailureRow` affordance so the failure also persists next to the control (a toast is dismissible; a failed action must not vanish). 3) Set Toaster's default duration from a named token in the new latency-policy module, with the actionable floor >= UNDO_WINDOW_MS. 4) Migrate the highest-consequence mutation families first: butler trigger/pause, schedules, state-store writes, secrets rotate/revoke, memory retire/re-embed, QA retry, calendar writes. 5) Lint: forbid a bare `toast.error` inside a `useMutation` onError without a recovery handle, in the same no-restricted-syntax family as POLL_POLICY_SELECTORS.

moves.title: Render-cost boundaries: rAF-coalesced high-frequency state, deferred filter text, and a page-root size ceiling
moves.why: Doctrine: <100ms is the budget for every local interaction (typing echo, drag, toggle), and a hot-path interaction over budget is a defect regardless of what the backend costs. With zero memo/transition boundaries in 237k lines, a 4,700-line calendar root re-renders on every pointermove of a drag and every keystroke in a filter re-renders whole pages that host maps, charts and graphs. Payoff: the two heaviest owner interactions (calendar drag, list filtering) get a structural guarantee instead of luck.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add a `useFrameState` primitive that coalesces high-frequency updates to one rAF tick, and move CalendarWorkspacePage's gridDrag/movedGhost onto it. 2) Extract the drag preview into its own memoized component subscribing to that state, so a drag repaints the ghost, not the workspace. 3) Wrap chart/map/graph regions (recharts, maplibre, xyflow) in memo boundaries with stable props, and route filter/search text through useDeferredValue so the input echoes at keystroke speed while the expensive subtree lags one frame. 4) Add an ESLint max-lines/max-statements ceiling for files under pages/ with a documented allowlist that only shrinks, so the 3k-7k-line roots are decomposed rather than grown. 5) Add a Playwright interaction budget check on the calendar drag and one list filter (input -> visible echo) so the bar is measured, not asserted.

audits.jarvis_gap: Today the shell has a real spine — one command menu (`EntityFinder`), two registries (`command-registry.tsx`, `use-register-shortcut.tsx`), chords projected from a typed capability manifest, and one genuinely generalized affordance (`ListTriageFooterHint`, adopted by all 8 `useListTriage` call sites). But the spine stops short of the surfaces where the user actually meets a feature. Chords are carried in the manifest and dropped by both places a destination appears (sidebar tooltip, palette Pages rows), so they are learnable only in the `?` sheet — which the bar treats as "doesn't exist". Verbs are page-mortal: the only always-available command family is `Run <butler>`, and the shell's own chrome (theme, sidebar collapse, help, "Talk to Butlers") registers no command and no binding at all. Every palette group silently truncates at 5–8 rows with no count and no overflow row, so on a 12-butler roster the palette cannot enumerate its own global actions. Rich keyboard surfaces (the Plex canvas's type-to-find, the ingestion ledger's row navigation) live in element handlers the registry has no compliant way to represent, so "On this page" under-reports. The same semantic gets different keys per page (`j/k` vs arrows vs Ctrl+Shift+arrows) and `[`/`]` carries three different meanings. 36 of 38 `EmptyState` call sites offer no door, several while their own prose instructs an action they don't provide. And the layer that governs all of this is ungoverned: `dashboard-shell/spec.md` still specifies the deleted `CommandPalette`, and `dashboard-design-language/spec.md` has no requirement covering the command menu, chords, kbd chips, or layering. The ideal is one manifest for destinations *and* verbs, one binding vocabulary, hints rendered wherever the thing lives, and empty states that are doors — enforced by the repo's existing lint-as-test pattern rather than by discipline.
audits.ideal: One typed shell manifest declares both destinations and verbs. A verb names a semantic role (`cursorNext`, `axisPrev`, `jumpNow`, `open`, `copyId`, `focusFilter`, `commit`), and the shell — not the page — owns which key that role binds to, so `j` means "next row" on every list in the fleet and `[`/`]` never means three things. Registering a verb produces, from one declaration, the key handling, the `?`-sheet row, the palette entry with its binding chip, and the inline hint rendered next to the control it drives; a shortcut that isn't advertised where its action lives is structurally impossible, exactly as `usePageActions` and `useListTriage` already are for their two cases. Global verbs survive navigation: selecting "Approve next approval" from anywhere routes and then acts. Every destination in the manifest carries a chord, and that chord is rendered in the sidebar tooltip and the palette's Pages row as well as the help sheet. The palette is a complete index — per-group counts, an explicit "N more, refine the query" row instead of a silent `slice(0, 8)`, and mode prefixes to scope to actions, entities, or pages. Every page-level empty state is a door: a required action that is a route, a registered verb, or a seeded butler conversation, so "ask the relationship butler to create one" is a button, not an instruction. One shell-owned floating dock stacks the help, chat, and page-contributed affordances against a token layer scale rather than hand-tuned `z-50`/`z-40`/`z-30` and apology comments. A catch-all route keeps a wrong URL inside the pane and teaches the palette. And all of it is normative: the design-language spec gains a Shell Discoverability requirement, the shell spec describes the registries that actually exist, and lint-as-test files in `frontend/src/lib/` enforce chord advertisement, verb-role keys, empty-state doors, and layer tokens the way `status-color-eslint.test.ts` and `focus-visible-floor.test.ts` already enforce their contracts.

findings.title: Rich page keyboard surfaces bypass the shortcut registry, so "On this page" under-reports
findings.detail: The Plex canvas implements the fleet's most powerful keyboard interaction — type-to-find over any printable character, Backspace to edit, Enter to center or open, Esc to clear then pop the hop trail, `0` to reset the camera — entirely inside an element `onKeyDown`, registering nothing. findings.title: Six divergent EmptyLine primitives despite a docstring claiming they were consolidated
findings.detail: `butler-detail/atoms.tsx` exports `EmptyLine` with a header comment stating it "Replaces private per-tab EmptyLine definitions so the pattern is consistent across all tabs" — but five private copies survive and two of them drop the serif face the Voice tier requires, rendering the same empty state in a different typeface depending on which tab you are on. Two more add `py-8` the canonical one lacks. Beyond `EmptyLine` there are two further vocabularies for the same idea: `MonoLabel color="dim"` on butler overview and domain-event panels, and `DossierPlaceholder` on QA. Five spellings of "nothing here" is the opposite of a design language that reads as one hand.

findings.title: No catch-all route — a stale or mistyped URL drops the owner out of the single pane
findings.detail: The router declares 60 route entries and a careful set of legacy redirects, but no `path: '*'` and no `errorElement`. An unmatched path therefore renders react-router's bare default outside `RootLayout`: no sidebar, no header, no Cmd-K, no `?` sheet, no way back except the browser's Back button. This is the one moment where a teaching surface matters most (the owner already has a wrong mental model of the route map), and the shell is absent from it.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/router-config.tsx (60 `path:` entries; no `'*'` route, no `errorElement`); frontend/src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx:88-135 (all discovery surfaces mount inside the layout the unmatched route never reaches)

findings.title: EducationPage's tabs are not URL-addressable, hiding two destinations from every discovery surface
findings.detail: Butler detail syncs its active tab to `?tab=` and even binds `1`–`9`, `[` and `]` to it. EducationPage uses an uncontrolled `<Tabs defaultValue="curriculum">` with no search-param sync, so Reviews and Analytics cannot be linked, bookmarked, restored across a reload, reached from Cmd-K, or given a chord — three destinations collapse into one addressable page. The manifest has no notion of a sub-destination, so there is no shared way to fix this for the next tabbed surface either.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/EducationPage.tsx:175-200 (uncontrolled Tabs); frontend/src/pages/ButlerDetailPage.tsx:167, :246 (?tab= sync), :200-225 (tab shortcuts); frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts:39-53 (ShellCapability has no sub-destination concept)

moves.title: Extend the shell manifest from destinations to verbs: one typed SHELL_VERBS list with global and route-bound commands
moves.why: discoverability/SKILL.md § Shortcut surfaces: "Everything in menus is in the palette" and a palette "fuzzy-matches verbs and nouns". Today the only global verb family is `Run <butler>` (GlobalActionsRegistrar.tsx:35-57) and the shell's own chrome verbs register nothing (PageHeader.tsx:156-168, Shell.tsx:28-38, shortcut-hints.tsx:92-102), so the palette is a page-local verb surface. `shell-capability.ts:39-53` already proves the manifest pattern works for destinations; extending it to verbs makes the palette a fleet-wide act surface and lets a command declare a route so "Approve next approval" navigates then acts from anywhere. Payoff: the north star's signal-to-session-to-evidence spine becomes keyboard-reachable from any page, not only from the page that owns it.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/lib/shell-capability.ts (add SHELL_VERBS sibling + types); frontend/src/lib/command-registry.tsx (accept manifest-sourced commands); frontend/src/components/layout/GlobalActionsRegistrar.tsx (becomes the manifest projector); frontend/src/components/layout/PageHeader.tsx, Shell.tsx, ui/shortcut-hints.tsx, chat/FloatingChatWidget.tsx (declare their verbs); frontend/src/components/layout/EntityFinder.tsx (Actions group reads global + page scopes)

(2) Add `route?: string` to `ShellVerb` and a navigate-then-perform runner; migrate `Run <butler>` onto it. (3) Migrate the highest-value page verbs (approve next, acknowledge next, retry failed notification, refresh system) to route-bound global verbs and delete their page-local duplicates.

moves.title: One binding vocabulary: a typed ShellVerbRole that owns the key, enforced by a lint-as-test
moves.why: discoverability/SKILL.md § Keyboard paths: "Follow platform conventions before inventing chords" — and internally, a vocabulary is only a convention if it is the same everywhere. Today `j/k` (SessionsPage.tsx:352-353), arrows (ButlersPage.tsx:131-152) and Ctrl+Shift+arrows (ChatPanel.tsx:174-190) all mean "move the cursor", and `[`/`]` means pagination, tab switching and date stepping on three different pages (SessionsPage.tsx:355-365, ButlerDetailPage.tsx:213-224, ChroniclesPage.tsx:301-315). `ShortcutBinding.key` is a raw string (use-register-shortcut.tsx:58-60), so nothing prevents a fourth spelling. Payoff: the tenth use transfers between pages — the whole point of a keyboard-first shell built as if by one hand.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-register-shortcut.tsx (role-keyed bindings); frontend/src/lib/ (new shell-verb-roles.ts + shell-verb-roles-eslint.test.ts, following lib/status-color-eslint.test.ts and lib/poll-policy-eslint.test.ts); all seven useRegisterShortcut call sites; frontend/src/hooks/use-list-triage.ts and use-page-actions.ts
moves.slice_plan: (1) Define `ShellVerbRole` (cursorNext/cursorPrev/axisNext/axisPrev/jumpNow/open/copyId/focusFilter/commit) with the canonical key and display for each; add an optional `role` field to `ShortcutBinding` that fills `key`/`display`. (2) Migrate all existing bindings to roles, resolving the three conflicting `[`/`]` meanings onto axisPrev/axisNext and giving Butlers and Chat the shared cursor role. (3) Add the lint test: page bindings must use a role, no two roles share a key, and every role used on a page is published to the help sheet.

moves.title: Render the chord wherever the destination lives, and give every global destination one
moves.why: discoverability/SKILL.md § Keyboard paths: "Shortcuts are advertised where the action lives... A shortcut listed only in a help page doesn't exist"; § Shortcut surfaces: "the palette is where shortcuts are learned". The chord already flows into `nav-config.ts:79` and `route-registry.ts:36-40` and is then discarded by the sidebar tooltip (Sidebar.tsx:279-281) and by `PageEntry` (EntityFinder.tsx:89-101) — while the Actions group two groups below renders binding chips correctly (EntityFinder.tsx:945-954). This is the cheapest high-leverage fix in the lens: the data is already there. Payoff: five-second fleet verification gets its keyboard on-ramp taught in the two places the owner looks.

moves.why: The design-language spec already requires "a single action button" for the page tier (openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:406-408), and the north star holds that every consequential clause is a door. 36 of 38 call sites violate it, two of them by printing the instruction instead of the button (ScheduleTable.tsx:90-94, CirclesPage.tsx:452-456). No …

` empty copy outside the primitive, and extend conformance check #8 to audit the door.

moves.title: Hint-only shortcut registration, so element-owned keyboard surfaces stop being invisible
moves.why: discoverability/SKILL.md § Findability: a feature reachable only by accident or by reading source is hidden — "a defect in the product, not the docs". The Plex canvas's type-to-find, Esc-to-pop-trail and `0`-reset are documented in a docstring (PlexPage.tsx:33-40) and taught by a find bar that only appears after the first keystroke (PlexPage.tsx:2109-2125). Payoff: "On this page" becomes a true census, and the fleet's best interaction stops being tribal knowledge.

moves.title: Palette completeness contract: per-group counts, explicit overflow rows, and mode prefixes
moves.why: discoverability/SKILL.md § Findability: "Search over navigation once a surface is large" — a type-to-find path is only trustworthy if it does not silently hide matches. Every group in EntityFinder truncates (EntityFinder.tsx:271, :382, :397, :479-485, :518) with no count and no cue, and with 12 butlers the `Run <butler>` family cannot be fully enumerated even by typing "run". moves.title: A shell-owned floating dock and a z-layer token scale
moves.why: The floating layer is currently negotiated by hand-written comments: FloatingChatWidget carries a six-line apology for dodging the `?` button (FloatingChatWidget.tsx:800-807) while FloatingMapMinimap sits at the exact coordinates that comment warns about (FloatingMapMinimap.tsx:46, :66). index.css declares no layer tokens (one hard-coded `z-index: 20` at :764) against 47 ad-hoc `z-*` classes. The design-language spec, which is normative for exactly this kind of shared value, has no layering requirement. Payoff: global affordances stop occluding each other, and a page can contribute a floating control without reading other components' source.

moves.title: Rewrite the shell spec against the registries that exist, and add a Shell Discoverability requirement to the design language
moves.why: doctrine: development is spec-driven, and the design-language spec is binding for anything shared across surfaces. Today `dashboard-shell/spec.md:372-427` describes the deleted `CommandPalette` (wrong recents key and cap, wrong copy, a Settings clear control that does not exist), `:445-462` lists chords two of which point at the wrong routes and omits four, and `:685-697` specifies an empty-state icon the component deliberately never renders. The design-language spec's 25 requirements say nothing about the command menu, chords, kbd chips or layering — which is precisely why findings 1–6 could all drift without tripping a conformance gate. Payoff: the discoverability layer becomes governed, so the other moves stay done.

The router has 60 entries and careful legacy redirects but no `path: '*'` and no `errorElement`, so an unmatched path renders outside RootLayout with no sidebar, no Cmd-K and no help sheet. ButlerDetailPage already does this right (`?tab=` at :167/:246 plus 1–9 and [/] bindings), while EducationPage's `<Tabs defaultValue="curriculum">` (:175) makes Reviews and Analytics unlinkable, unbookmarkable, lost on reload and invisible to Cmd-K. `ShellCapability` has no sub-destination concept, so there is no shared fix. moves.title: A shared FilterField primitive that self-registers its focus key and advertises it inline
moves.why: discoverability/SKILL.md § Progressive power: "whatever annoys the tenth use is the shortcut to build". Sixteen filter inputs across the fleet have no keyboard route because `/` is claimed globally by the palette (use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts:38-42) and no page offers an alternative. Building it as a primitive rather than per page also settles the copy drift ("Filter by trigger..." / "Search collections..." / "Search entities…" — mixed verb, mixed ellipsis character). Payoff: the most common in-page control gains a fast path and a single voice in one change.

(3) Add a source-scan test that a bare `<Input placeholder="Search…">` outside the primitive fails lint.

audits.jarvis_gap: Dispatch is one of the better-specified design languages I have audited, and it has real machinery behind it: a typed visual-role registry (`lib/visual-token-roles.ts`), an executable contrast suite (`lib/contrast.test.ts`), a CSS identity-token guard (`scripts/visual-role-css-guard.mjs`), and fifteen `no-restricted-syntax` groups. But the language is enforced only where someone remembered to enforce it, and the token file itself is a drift engine. Today: two mutually contradictory type scales ship in `index.css` (the 1.2-ratio `--text-*` ladder wired to Tailwind alongside the Dispatch 44/24/14/13/16/10/11 roles), producing ~28 live font sizes including half-pixel steps; the `Title`/`Display`/`Eyebrow`/`Pill`/`KpiStrip`/`StateDot`/`Voice` primitives exist but are imported by 5-20 files each while 49-71 surfaces hand-roll the same thing; `Badge` (filled rounded pill, 166 sites) and `Pill` (Dispatch kind tag, 5 sites) are two opposite visual languages for the same concept; the single sanctioned state-color-on-fill exception (`.attention-row`) is used at 4 sites while ~40 hand-rolled state tints run at alphas the spec never permits, including one at 30%; ninety `text-muted-foreground/NN` and 188 `border-border/NN` alpha modifiers have minted an unnamed tier ladder that silently reopens the AA contrast fixes the tokens were darkened to close; ten recharts files govern their own axes, tooltips, radii and animation, four of them shipping recharts' hardcoded-white default tooltip into a dark-primary app; the butler dimension has no chart role at all, so two stacked-bar charts repeat colors across an 11-butler roster; and the dark-primary commitment itself does not survive first paint, because `.dark` is added in a `useEffect` behind an `index.html` that still says `<title>frontend</title>` and points at a `/vite.svg` favicon that does not exist. The gap to the north star is not taste — the flagship pages genuinely read calm. It is that nothing makes conformance a property of a route rather than a property of whoever last reviewed it, so "built by one hand" holds for the pages a bead touched and dissolves everywhere else.
audits.ideal: Every visual decision resolves through exactly one named role, and a route cannot claim to be in the language without proving it. There is one type scale — the seven Dispatch roles, exposed as role utilities, with no arbitrary pixel sizes and no 600/700 weights even loaded; one tag primitive, one status affordance, one attention treatment, one overlay treatment, one chart shell, one eyebrow. Alpha modifiers on semantic tokens are a lint error, because a fourth muted tier is a new token with a stated meaning or it does not exist. Charts are not free-form recharts: a single `<Chart>` shell owns axes, tick type, grid, legend geometry, square bars and `isAnimationActive={false}`, and a `butler-series` role in the visual-token registry colors butler-dimensioned data from each butler's own identity hue with a mandatory ButlerMark legend, so a stacked bar and a letter-mark agree everywhere and eleven butlers never collide in five slots. Theme is resolved before the first frame and every color channel — including the WebGL density ramp — is defined in both themes, so a dark-mode operator never sees a light flash, a white tooltip, or a heatmap whose intensity runs backwards. The three families are self-hosted, because a system whose doctrine is one owner on one box must not fall back to Helvetica when the box is offline. And the lint layer is generated from one registry rather than hand-spread across eight override blocks, with each route in `SHELL_CAPABILITIES` carrying a machine-checked record of which of the ten Page Conformance checks it has passed — making the visual language the same kind of unbroken, evidence-bearing spine the data surfaces are held to.

findings.title: index.css ships a second, contradictory type scale that Tailwind's named sizes bind to
findings.detail: index.css:280-286 declares a 1.2-ratio ladder (--text-xs 0.694rem … --text-3xl 2.074rem) and index.css:462-468 wires it to Tailwind's font-size utilities, so `text-2xl` resolves to 27.6px, not the Dispatch Title 24px. Title.tsx:40 documents the collision in a comment ("not text-2xl which is 1.728rem in this scale") rather than resolving it. Consequence across the fleet: 21 distinct arbitrary pixel sizes are in use (text-[8px] through text-[44px], including half-pixel steps 9.5/10.5/11.5/12.5/13.5px) plus 7 named Tailwind steps on the wrong scale — roughly 28 live type sizes against a 7-role spec. Nothing lints `text-[Npx]`.

findings.title: Alpha modifiers have invented an unnamed tier ladder that reopens the AA contrast fixes the tokens were darkened to close
findings.detail: 90 uses of `text-muted-foreground/{40,50,60,70,80}` across 31 files, 188 uses of `border-border/{30,40,50,60}` and `divide-border/{40,60}` across 64 files, and 12 distinct `opacity-*` values app-wide. index.css:40-45 and :129-134 record that --mfg and --dim were specifically darkened/lightened to clear 4.5:1 for the 9-11px mono type they carry; `/40` on that token reduces it to roughly 1.6:1, and no lint covers the modifier. The border case is worse than drift: `border-border/60` in dark mode resolves to exactly `--border-soft`, a token that already exists and is bypassed 118 times. Opacity also carries three meanings at once — disabled at 0.4 (spec), refetching at 0.6 (fetching-dim.tsx:33), and stale at 0.4 (Provenance.tsx:105) — so the same treatment means "you cannot use this" and "do not trust this".
findings.evidence: frontend/src/index.css:40-45,129-134; frontend/src/components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx:33; frontend/src/components/ui/Provenance.tsx:105; frontend/src/components/qa/QaKpiStrip.tsx:153

findings.title: Chart language is unowned: ten recharts files with independently drifted axes, tooltips, radii and animation
findings.detail: No chart shell exists. Tick sizes are 10px, 11px, 12px and `text-xs` (0.694rem) across four files. Bar radii are `[4,4,0,0]` (CrossTopicChart.tsx:43), `[0,4,4,0]` (ButlerFinanceFinancesTab.tsx:255) and `[2,2,0,0]` (ButlerGeneralCollectionsTab.tsx:398) — three radius vocabularies for one mark, in a language whose thesis is that hierarchy comes from type and rules. Four charts ship recharts' DEFAULT tooltip (MeasurementChart.tsx:442, CrossTopicChart.tsx:40, MasteryTrendChart.tsx:69, ButlerFinanceFinancesTab.tsx:254), which renders a hardcoded white box with a light-gray border into a dark-primary app; two others hand-roll a `shadow-md` card tooltip (ButlerGeneralCollectionsTab.tsx:389, CostStripeChart.tsx:94) against the no-cards/no-shadows prohibition. Those same four charts omit `isAnimationActive={false}`, so they play recharts' 1500ms grow-in on every load — forbidden by the four-entry motion table, and NOT caught by the global reduced-motion floor at index.css:787 because recharts animates in JS, not CSS.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/health/MeasurementChart.tsx:439-442; frontend/src/components/education/CrossTopicChart.tsx:38-43; frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerFinanceFinancesTab.tsx:245-255; frontend/src/index.css:787; openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:365-380

findings.title: Butler-as-a-data-dimension has no visual role, so stacked butler charts repeat colors inside one bar
findings.detail: SessionStripeChart.tsx:233-238 and CostStripeChart.tsx:249-254 both stack per-butler series and color them with `chartSeriesColor(index)`. `visualRoleToken` wraps mod `values.length`, which is 5 for chart-series (visual-token-roles.ts:151-157), against an 11-butler roster — so butlers at index 0 and 5 render identically inside the same stacked bar and the same legend, and the reader cannot tell which butler a stripe belongs to. The Semantic Visual Role Matrix has no butler-dimension role and the Butler Category Hues requirement confines `--category-*` to the letter-mark, so today there is no correct way to build these two charts. This is a gap in the language, not only drift.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/dashboard/SessionStripeChart.tsx:233-238; frontend/src/components/costs/CostStripeChart.tsx:249-254; frontend/src/lib/visual-token-roles.ts:151-157; openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:114-141,172-186

findings.title: The Chronicles density ramp is pinned to light-mode literals and inverts on the dark basemap
findings.detail: chart-colors.ts:95-97 fixes NEUTRAL_DENSITY_LOW at oklch L 0.55 and NEUTRAL_DENSITY_HIGH at L 0.18 — both read from index.css's LIGHT-mode --dim and --fg — and neutralDensityColor emits a literal rgb() with no theme input. MapWidgetInner.tsx:163-164 swaps the CARTO basemap to Dark Matter in dark mode and MapWidgetInner.tsx:112 paints hex fill-color straight from that ramp. On dark, the densest cells (L 0.18, near-black) sink into the dark basemap while the sparsest (L 0.55) are the most visible: the intensity encoding reads backwards for half the app's users, in the default theme.

findings.title: The sidebar's active-item indicator is a fourth semantic hue wearing the attention grammar for a routine state
findings.detail: Sidebar.tsx:90 marks the active nav item with `border-l-2 border-sidebar-primary bg-sidebar-primary/[0.05] dark:bg-sidebar-primary/[0.06]`. `--sidebar-primary` in dark is oklch(0.560 0.140 264.4) (index.css:519) — a saturated blue aligned to chart-1. That is a fourth semantic hue used as chrome on the single most-seen element in the app, in a language that permits three state hues plus identity plus the categorical/chart ramps; it is a left-border accent stripe (explicitly on the anti-pattern list); and it applies the tint+rail unit — reserved for rows that demand a human decision now — to a routine navigation state.

findings.title: An unsanctioned "informational blue" role exists purely as accumulated lint exemptions
findings.detail: rule-promotion-banner.tsx:29-37, autonomy-suggestions-banner.tsx:26-33, autonomy-panel.tsx:39, rule-promotion-stats.tsx:26 and approval-teaching-digest.tsx:24 each carry `eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-syntax -- informational …, not live operational status` over raw `blue-50/200/500/600/700/800/900/950` classes, including `bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 text-white` action buttons. The guard's question is "is this operational status?"; the Semantic Visual Role Matrix's question is "which of the five roles is this?" — and it has no informational role. The exemption grammar is wider than the spec's role set, so fourteen exemptions have minted a sixth hue role by attrition, complete with its own filled-CTA button form.

findings.title: Health conditions invert green's meaning and pair a dot with the literal word "active"
findings.detail: ConditionTracker.tsx:44-48 maps condition status to a dot: `active` → `--severity-low` (green, commented "currently ongoing"), `managed` → `--severity-medium` (amber), `resolved` → neutral gray. Green, whose single fleet-wide meaning is healthy/positive, here means the owner currently has an ongoing medical condition, while the genuinely good outcome (resolved) is rendered as absence. The file's own comment at :43-44 states "the colour alone carries the state, the word sits beside it in mono caps" — which is two affordances on one signal, and the word is literally `active`, the exact label the Composure Doctrine names as forbidden.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/health/ConditionTracker.tsx:43-48; openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:44-45,53-56

findings.title: Operational state resolved through the health-severity token family, including in the spec's showcase component
findings.detail: BriefingStatus.tsx:65-69 — the Process Status Pill the spec names by requirement — maps its amber/green/red dots to `var(--severity-medium)`, `var(--severity-low)` and `var(--destructive)`. AttentionList.tsx:103 colors the Sev glyph with `var(--severity-medium)`. The Semantic Visual Role Matrix assigns operational state to `--red`/`--amber`/`--green` through the `StateDot`/`stateColorVar` resolver; `--severity-*` is documented at index.css:78-88 as the health/symptom severity family. Two of the language's own reference components route state through the wrong token family, and no lint catches a cross-family request.

QaKpiStrip.tsx:150-179 forks it: five cells (the spec requires a four-column grid), `divide-border/60` instead of hairline `--border`, its own eyebrow and delta spellings, and `text-destructive` applied to the mega number. notification-stats-bar.tsx:54-134 is a fourth variant using `text-2xl font-bold` with state-colored numerals. findings.title: Dark-primary breaks on first paint on every cold load, and the shell wears the Vite starter's identity
findings.detail: useDarkMode.ts:25 defaults to dark per doctrine, but useDarkMode.ts:33-37 adds the `.dark` class inside a useEffect — after the first paint. index.html carries no pre-hydration theme script, index.css:626 sets `color-scheme: light` on `:root`, and index.css:17-18 paints `#213547` on `#ffffff` (the Vite starter's slate-on-white, and two raw literals that are not Dispatch tokens). Every cold load of the operations console therefore flashes the light theme before snapping to dark — the opposite of composure at the exact moment of five-second fleet verification. Alongside it: index.html:10 is `<title>frontend</title>` and index.html:5 points the favicon at `/vite.svg`, which cannot resolve because the frontend has no `public/` directory at all.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/useDarkMode.ts:25,33-37; frontend/index.html:5,10; frontend/src/index.css:17-18,626

findings.title: The type system requires the public internet; offline it falls back to the exact generic stacks the spec bans
findings.detail: index.html:9 loads Inter Tight, Source Serif 4 and JetBrains Mono from fonts.googleapis.com. There is no `public/` directory, no .woff2/.woff/.ttf anywhere in the repo, and no `@font-face` rule in src/. On a LAN-only or offline instance every fallback in index.css:325-327 fires and the whole dashboard renders in `ui-sans-serif, system-ui`, `Georgia` and `ui-monospace` — the generic stacks the Type System requirement explicitly forbids, and the sans/serif/mono meaning split collapses. This contradicts the sovereignty doctrine directly: one user, one instance, no dependence on an always-on internet connection.
findings.evidence: frontend/index.html:9; frontend/src/index.css:325-327; openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:193-199; about/heart-and-soul/vision.md:60-63,146-147

findings.title: Elevation and glass: 41 shadows across 7 strengths and 6 blur sites in a one-elevation language
findings.detail: Shadow strengths in use: xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, none. FloatingMapMinimap.tsx stacks four prohibitions in one component — `bg-card shadow-lg rounded-lg` at :66, `backdrop-blur` at :77, and a `scale-50` transform animation at :68 (scale-in is on the forbidden motion list). ButlerManagementTab.tsx:377,453,718 hand-roll three modals with `shadow-xl p-6` instead of the dialog primitive. EntityFinder.tsx:584 uses `shadow-2xl` on the command palette. CaseList.tsx:85 marks the active case row with `bg-white/[0.04]`, a raw non-token white that is invisible against the light-mode page. Overlays (dialog, sheet, popover, palette, floating widgets) have no defined surface role in the spec, so each one invented its own.

findings.title: One ordinal scale rendered in three color systems, and time buckets colored with state hues in raw Tailwind palette
findings.detail: QuizHistoryList.tsx:10-16 renders a single 0-5 grade scale as `--red`/`--amber` tints for 0-3, raw `bg-blue-100 text-blue-800` for 4, and a `--green` tint for 5 — an ordinal ramp expressed as state colors plus a light-only Tailwind chip with no dark variant; :21-24 adds `bg-purple-100`, `bg-sky-100`, `bg-slate-100` kind chips, also dark-blind. ReviewTimeline.tsx:31-34 colors time buckets `border-l-red-500` (Overdue), `border-l-amber-500` (Today), `border-l-blue-500` (This Week), `border-l-gray-300` (Later) — un-tokenized palette values, left-border accent stripes, no dark variant for gray-300, and red/amber carrying a temporal rather than a severity meaning. ReviewTimeline is not in BLUE_PURPLE_STATUS_AUDIT_FILES, so nothing flags it.

findings.title: The lint layer is a hand-maintained cartesian product with live holes
findings.detail: eslint.config.js:316-317 documents that flat config replaces rather than merges `no-restricted-syntax`, so eight override blocks each re-spread the global selector groups by hand. The `**/*.ts` block at eslint.config.js:2662 omits HEX_COLOR_SELECTORS, PRIMITIVE_REDECLARATION_SELECTORS and HANDROLLED_OVERLAY_SELECTORS — meaning raw hex colors are unguarded in exactly the .ts files that resolve color roles (`lib/visual-token-roles.ts`, `lib/chart-colors.ts`); the `src/components/ui/**` block at :2706 omits HANDROLLED_OVERLAY_SELECTORS. Any new visual guard must be registered in nine places or it silently does not apply to the files that most need it, which is why nothing today lints `text-[Npx]`, alpha-modified semantic tokens, state-hue backgrounds, or cross-family token requests.

findings.title: The Eyebrow is the app's most-repeated element and has three canonical spellings plus 49 hand-rolls
findings.detail: Eyebrow.tsx is imported by 20 files; kpi-eyebrow.ts's KPI_EYEBROW_STYLE is a second spelling (referencing `--muted-foreground` where Eyebrow references `--mfg`); 49 files spell `tracking-[0.14em]` inline, thirteen of them at `text-muted-foreground/70` or `/60`, dropping the muted token below its AA floor at 10px. Eyebrow.tsx:43 also hardcodes the DARK-mode --mfg literal as its own fallback (`text-[var(--mfg,oklch(0.708_0_0))]`), which would be a light-mode contrast failure if the token were ever absent — the same fallback-literal pattern appears in Title.tsx:41 and Display.tsx.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/Eyebrow.tsx:43; frontend/src/components/overview/kpi-eyebrow.ts:14-19; frontend/src/components/ui/Title.tsx:41

findings.title: A chatbot typing indicator with forbidden bounce motion, in the language whose thesis is "not a chatbot"
findings.detail: TypingIndicator.tsx:9,14,19 renders three `animate-bounce` dots with staggered 0/150/300ms delays inside a `rounded-2xl bg-muted` speech bubble. `bounce` is named on the forbidden-motion list, the animation is not one of the four vocabulary entries, and the component is the single most chatbot-coded element in UI convention — against a spec whose opening line is "a butler announcing, not a chatbot reporting". findings.title: The command palette uses an emoji as its action icon, beside a 12-file Unicode dingbat icon set
findings.detail: EntityFinder.tsx:694 and :939 render `⚡` (U+26A1, default emoji presentation on every major platform) and `↗` inside a `bg-muted` rounded square as the icon for every recent-item and action row in the keyboard-first command palette. The spec requires stroke-only, single-weight, currentColor, 16x16 icons and states "No emoji, ever". Beyond it, a parallel dingbat vocabulary (✓ ✗ ★ ✎ ✕ ⚠ ⚙ ◦ • ∅ –) spans 12 files with no registry — SettingsModelsPage.tsx:1443,1451, WhatBreaks.tsx:127, Provenance.tsx:167, passport/atoms.tsx:677 — duplicating lucide `Check`, `X` and `AlertTriangle`, which are already imported by 54 files.

findings.title: The 4px spacing rule is unlintable as written, and 906 sites are off-grid
findings.detail: The Density and Spacing requirement says "All spacing uses multiples of 4px exclusively" and then lists 14 and 18 among the common values, and prescribes 18px attention rows and 10px index rows — none of which are multiples of 4. The rule contradicts itself inside one paragraph, so it cannot be mechanically enforced. In code, 906 fractional Tailwind spacing steps are live (gap-1.5 x186, py-1.5 x109, py-0.5 x77, px-2.5 x55, p-3.5 x31, gap-4.5 x13), plus arbitrary values mt-[7px], pl-[22px], pl-[14px], p-[3px], gap-[2px]. The `--space-1..12` ladder at index.css:354-365 exists but is not what Tailwind's utilities resolve against.
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:256-265; frontend/src/index.css:354-365,476-487

findings.title: Page shell widths diverge three ways and only one surface uses the specified 1280px

moves.title: Collapse to one type-role scale, delete the competing ladder, and stop shipping the forbidden weights
moves.why: Spec § Type System (spec.md:193-232) defines seven roles; index.css:280-286 ships a second 1.2-ratio scale that Tailwind's named sizes bind to, and index.html:9 loads the weights spec.md:214-218 forbids. moves.title: Make the density ramp theme-resolved so intensity never reads backwards
