audits.jarvis_gap: Today the connector fleet is broad on *machine* signal and thin on *lived* signal. Fourteen ingestion/context sources exist (`src/butlers/connectors/`: gmail, google_calendar, google_drive, google_health, home_assistant + 5 HA helpers, owntracks, spotify, steam, telegram_bot, telegram_user_client, whatsapp_user_client, live_listener, activitywatch, discord_user-draft), and the Chronicler projects 20 adapters off them (`src/butlers/chronicler/jobs.py:212-543`). But every one of those is text, telemetry, or device state: there is not a single visual, media-consumption, nutrition, or generic-app-notification source in the ecosystem, and there is no way for a butler to *act* in the physical room it can already hear. The result is that three manifestos make promises nothing feeds — Lifestyle's "the show you just started, the book you're reading" (roster/lifestyle/MANIFESTO.md § What You Can Do) against a module list of only memory/calendar/contacts/spotify/steam (roster/lifestyle/butler.toml), Health's nutrition tracking against `roster/health/tools/diet.py:13-16` ("There is no external connector — meals are always entered manually"), and Chronicler's reading reconstruction against a keyword match on calendar titles (`src/butlers/chronicler/adapters/reading.py:1-22`). Meanwhile the perception→action spine is one-directional: `live_listener` captures ambient speech from the owner's rooms (`src/butlers/connectors/live_listener/__init__.py:1-6`) but `notify()` can only reach telegram and email (`openspec/specs/core-notify/spec.md:302`), so the system hears the room and answers on the owner's phone. The ideal is a perception tier where each *kind* of lived evidence — where you were, what you saw, what you consumed, what you ate, what your uninstrumented apps told you — has exactly one authoritative connector carrying provenance and freshness into the Chronicler spine, plus at least one egress channel co-located with each ingress channel so a signal can be answered where it was heard. The fleet is also carrying one honesty defect: the connector catalog advertises Discord as an available channel while its runtime is a self-declared non-production skeleton and `discord/discord` is not even a legal channel/provider pairing.

findings.title: No visual/photographic evidence source anywhere in the fleet
findings.detail: The Chronicler registers 20 projection adapters (sessions, calendar, owntracks point/place/ssid, activitywatch, owner_outbound, steam, meals, HA history + sensor activity, google_health sleep/workout/steps/HR, focus/reading/exercise/occupation inference, comms) and not one derives from an image. Photos are the densest and most human-legible record of lived time the owner already produces continuously, and the day-reconstruction surface cannot use any of it. Grepping the whole src tree for exif/photo/geotag returns only Google Contacts avatar parsing (src/butlers/modules/contacts/sync.py:155-184).
findings.evidence: src/butlers/chronicler/jobs.py:212-543; src/butlers/modules/contacts/sync.py:155-184

findings.title: Ambient voice ingress has no matching egress: the system can hear a room it cannot answer in
findings.detail: live_listener captures mic audio, VADs it, transcribes it, and submits ingest.v1 envelopes, but notify() supports only telegram and email; any voice-originated request is therefore answered on a different device in a different modality. Messenger's manifesto claims sole ownership of outbound user-channel delivery and enumerates only telegram/email/whatsapp tools, so no butler may legitimately route a spoken reply through ha_call_service either.

Only the game half has a source (steam module). The digest prompt therefore instructs the LLM to 'Search memory for recent facts' — i.e. to reconstruct consumption from whatever the owner happened to mention in chat, which is exactly the projection-from-conversation posture the vision rejects.

moves.title: Immich photo-library connector: visual evidence as the corroborating layer of lived time
moves.why: Chronicler's manifesto is to 'reconstruct lived past time from the evidence the other butlers already capture' and to 'preserve source provenance on every row', yet its 20 adapters (src/butlers/chronicler/jobs.py:212-543) contain zero image-derived evidence. Photos are the one signal that lets the owner verify a reconstructed day in five seconds without reading a table — an OwnTracks place cluster plus three photos taken inside it is proof; the cluster alone is an inference. Immich is self-hosted, keeps the vision's sovereignty rule intact (no cloud dependency, no third-party data custody), and exposes a metadata search API that returns taken_at, GPS, asset type, device and face/person ids without moving a single byte of image data into the butlers database. Payoff: the Chronicles day view gains a human-legible anchor lane; Relationship gains co-presence evidence (a face id recurring in the owner's photos is interaction evidence its 'interaction history' promise currently only gets from messaging); Lifestyle gains restaurant/meal/travel texture.
moves.integration_points: New connector src/butlers/connectors/immich.py (poll /api/search/metadata with an updatedAfter cursor via connectors/cursor_store.py, mirroring the Spotify/HA poll pattern); new evidence table connectors.immich_assets (asset_id, taken_at, lat/lon, place_label, asset_type, device, person_ids[], NO pixels, NO filename); account registry public.immich_accounts + immich_api_key entity_info type per RFC 0004 and the account-registry pattern in .claude/skills/adding-connectors-and-modules/references/account-registry-pattern.md; RFC 0003 amendment registering the photos/immich channel/provider pair (the list at about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0003-...:58); new Chronicler adapter src/butlers/chronicler/adapters/immich.py registered in src/butlers/chronicler/jobs.py emitting photo_capture point events (Privacy.sensitive, Precision.exact) and photo_burst episodes; specs openspec/specs/connector-immich/ and a chronicler-source-compatibility amendment; provider entry in src/butlers/secrets_provider_catalog.py:55. Serves roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md primarily, roster/relationship and roster/lifestyle secondarily.

S2: Chronicler photo_capture adapter + Chronicles lane with a per-asset provenance door back to the Immich asset id. S3: photo_burst episodes and place-cluster corroboration (an owntracks place episode carrying >=N overlapping photo_capture events gains a corroborated=true evidence field rather than a new episode). S4 (gated on an explicit owner decision): person_ids → public.entities resolution for Relationship co-presence, default off.

moves.title: Messenger-owned voice egress channel: answer in the room that was heard
moves.why: This is the single most JARVIS-shaped gap in the ecosystem. live_listener already captures, VADs, transcribes and routes ambient speech (src/butlers/connectors/live_listener/__init__.py:1-6), but notify() supports only telegram and email (openspec/specs/core-notify/spec.md:302), so the perception→session→response spine breaks at the last hop and the answer surfaces on a phone. Messenger's contract already claims sole ownership of outbound user-channel delivery, so the fix belongs there and nowhere else — a butler reaching tts.speak through the Home module's ha_call_service would violate that ownership. The north-star discipline applies directly: a spoken message into an empty room is a silent delivery failure, so this must record undeliverable_no_presence rather than sent, and fall back to the owner's preferred text channel — failure never impersonating health, in the most literal possible way.
moves.integration_points: openspec/specs/core-notify/spec.md § Supported channels (line 302) gains 'voice'; roster/messenger/MANIFESTO.md amendment adding voice_send_message to the enumerated channel tool surface (the manifesto is binding, so this is a formal amendment not a code change); new Messenger adapter speaking via Wyoming TTS or Home Assistant tts.speak against a speaker target; recipient resolution via a new voice_endpoint entity_info type joined to the live_listener mic_id so the reply lands on the speaker nearest the mic that heard the request; presence gate reading the Home Assistant occupancy entity or a recent live_listener VAD checkpoint (src/butlers/connectors/live_listener/checkpoint.py) before speaking; delivery outcome rows in the messenger schema alongside existing delivery intents; src/butlers/routing_guidance.py _SOURCE_TO_NOTIFY_CHANNEL gains live_listener→voice and _INTERACTIVE_ROUTE_CHANNELS gains live_listener so routed voice messages get reply guidance. Serves roster/messenger/MANIFESTO.md (amendment) and roster/home/MANIFESTO.md ('feel like magic: invisible, responsive').
moves.slice_plan: S1: notify channel + Messenger adapter + explicit-recipient sends only, outcome recorded, no presence logic. S2: mic→speaker binding so a live_listener-originated request routes its reply back to the originating room by default. S3: presence gate with the undeliverable_no_presence terminal outcome and text-channel fallback, surfaced as a typed recovery action on the notification recovery surface. S4: quiet-hours interaction with the existing notify deferral pass (voice must never be the channel a deferred flush composes into).

moves.title: Mobile notification mirror: one connector that perceives every uninstrumented service
moves.why: Every proposal in this lens except this one buys perception of exactly one service. This one buys perception of all of them: the bank push that beats the emailed receipt, the courier's 'out for delivery', the airline's gate change (which Travel's manifesto promises to surface 'before the airlines announce them' and which today waits on an email), the doctor's appointment SMS, the ride-hail arrival. It is the highest perception-per-build-unit move available and it retires the pressure to build a connector per vendor. The precedent already exists in-repo: OwnTracks is an authenticated push-in connector from an owner-controlled device (openspec/specs/connector-owntracks). The privacy posture must be inverted from every other connector — default-deny with an explicit per-app allowlist evaluated by the existing IngestionPolicyEvaluator — because the raw stream would otherwise be the most invasive surface in the system.
moves.integration_points: New connector src/butlers/connectors/mobile_notifications.py accepting authenticated POSTs from a phone-side forwarder (off-repo OSS), following the OwnTracks webhook pattern; connectors.mobile_notifications evidence table (device_id, app_package, posted_at, title, body, category); RFC 0003 amendment registering mobile/<forwarder> as a channel/provider pair; default-deny source-filter rules seeded into the registry described by openspec/specs/source-filter-registry so an unlisted app_package is dropped at the gate and counted in connectors.filtered_events rather than routed; sender.identity = mobile:<device_id> per RFC 0004; per-app allowlist management UI on the existing connector filter surface (openspec/specs/dashboard-connector-filter-ui); spec openspec/specs/connector-mobile-notifications. Serves roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md (ingress ownership) and feeds roster/travel, roster/finance, roster/health, roster/relationship without any per-domain build. Requires an ingestion-policy amendment establishing default-deny as a legal per-channel posture.
moves.slice_plan: S1: connector + evidence table + default-deny gate + one allowlisted app end-to-end, with the filtered-events counter proving the deny path is real. S2: allowlist management on the connector filter UI with a per-app routed/filtered count so the owner can see exactly what the channel perceives. S3: normalization hints per app category (shipment / transaction / appointment) so Switchboard classification does not have to infer domain from a 40-character push body. S4: retention policy — notification bodies are high-volume and low-durability; bound them the way owntracks retention is bounded.

moves.title: Media scrobble connector (Trakt + Jellyfin) for Lifestyle's watched/read promise
moves.why: Lifestyle's manifesto promises to track 'the show you just started, the book you're reading, the game you've been playing' and its weekly-taste-digest schedule prompt asks the LLM to summarize 'what was watched, read, or played this week' — but the butler enables only spotify and steam, so two-thirds of that prompt is answered by searching memory facts for whatever the owner happened to mention in conversation. That is a manifesto promise served by recall rather than evidence. Spotify already proves the shape end to end (connector → connectors table → module tools → SpotifySessionAdapter → Chronicles lane); this is the same shape for the screen. Jellyfin covers the self-hosted half (sovereignty-aligned) and Trakt covers streaming services the owner does not host.
moves.integration_points: New connector src/butlers/connectors/media_scrobble.py with two provider backends (Trakt OAuth, Jellyfin API key against a self-hosted server, both resolved from an account registry public.media_accounts); connectors.media_plays evidence table (title, media_type, series/season/episode, started_at, finished_at, runtime, provider, external_id); RFC 0003 pairs media/trakt and media/jellyfin; new module src/butlers/modules/media.py exposing media_recent_plays / media_currently_watching / media_history for the digest to read instead of guessing, enabled via [modules.media] in roster/lifestyle/butler.toml; Chronicler adapter emitting watching_episode episodes registered in src/butlers/chronicler/jobs.py; specs openspec/specs/connector-media-scrobble and openspec/specs/module-media; provider entries in src/butlers/secrets_provider_catalog.py. Serves roster/lifestyle/MANIFESTO.md directly and roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md by filling the largest remaining evening-hours gap after ActivityWatch fills the workday.
moves.slice_plan: S1: Jellyfin backend only (no OAuth, self-hosted, fastest path to real data) + connectors.media_plays + connector-base obligations. S2: media module tools and rewrite of the weekly-taste-digest schedule prompt in roster/lifestyle/butler.toml to read tools rather than memory facts. S3: Chronicler watching_episode adapter and Chronicles lane. S4: Trakt backend for non-self-hosted viewing, behind the same account registry.

moves.title: Open Food Facts nutrition resolution: stop presenting model guesses as measured macros
moves.why: Health's manifesto promises 'Nutrition: What you eat matters. The butler tracks your meals, aggregates your nutrition, and helps you understand your patterns' — but roster/health/tools/diet.py:13-16 states outright that meals are always entered manually and there is no external connector, and neither health.meals nor the facts row carries any provenance distinguishing a macro the model invented from one that was measured. nutrition_summary() then aggregates those numbers, and MealsAdapter projects them into the Chronicles eating_event lane, where they sit beside genuinely-measured Google Health readings with identical authority. This is the smallest-cost, highest-honesty move in the lens: Open Food Facts is keyless, free, offline-cacheable (no always-on-internet dependency at daemon level, per the anti-pattern list in vision.md), and returns per-100g macros against a barcode or product name with a citable product id.
moves.integration_points: New module src/butlers/modules/nutrition.py (module only, no connector — 'read-only data query' per the decision table in .claude/skills/adding-connectors-and-modules/SKILL.md) exposing nutrition_lookup(barcode|name) returning macros plus off_product_id and source_url; migration on roster/health/migrations adding nutrition_source ('measured' | 'estimated' | 'unknown') and nutrition_source_ref to health.meals; roster/health/tools/diet.py meal_log() records which path produced the numbers; nutrition_summary() reports measured vs estimated coverage rather than one blended total; src/butlers/chronicler/adapters/meals.py carries the provenance onto the point event so the Chronicles meal lane can mark estimated values; spec openspec/specs/module-nutrition and an amendment to the health butler spec. Serves roster/health/MANIFESTO.md ('There's no judgment in the butler's memory, only honesty').
moves.slice_plan: S1: nutrition_source column + honest default of 'estimated' for every existing and new row, and a nutrition_summary() that reports the split — this alone removes the false authority before any lookup exists. S2: nutrition_lookup tool against Open Food Facts with a local response cache. S3: meal_log wires the lookup and writes 'measured' with the product ref. S4: Chronicles meal lane renders the provenance distinction.

moves.title: Read-later / highlights connector: give reading reconstruction and Education source-grounding a real feed
moves.why: ReadingInferredAdapter reconstructs the owner's reading life by regex-matching /\b(read|reading)\b|\b(book|article|paper):/ against calendar titles, and its own docstring names the missing sources: 'browser history connector, Readwise / Pocket integration, dedicated reading capture tool' (src/butlers/chronicler/adapters/reading.py:19-22). Separately, openspec/changes/source-grounded-education lifts Education's content-sourcing exclusion but constrains material to 'owner-provided, never autonomously scraped' — a highlights sync is exactly owner-provided material arriving automatically, so it supplies that change's input without violating its constraint. Karakeep or Wallabag keeps this self-hosted; Readwise is the hosted fallback. Payoff: Chronicler stops inferring reading from calendar-title keywords, and Education can cite the owner's actual highlights rather than waiting for hand-registration of every source.

Serves roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md and roster/education/MANIFESTO.md (already amended by source-grounded-education).

S2: reading adapter rewrite — real evidence primary, calendar-keyword inference retained only as an explicitly-labelled secondary source so the Chronicles lane can tell inferred from observed. audits.ideal: The ideal connector ecosystem gives every distinct *kind* of owner-perceivable evidence exactly one authoritative source, and gives every ingress channel a co-located egress channel so a signal can be answered where it was raised. Concretely: location (OwnTracks), machine work (ActivityWatch), device state and environment (Home Assistant + atmosphere), body (Google Health), communication (Gmail/Telegram/WhatsApp), money (SimpleFIN + receipts), and audio (live-listener) are joined by the four missing perceptual axes — sight (a self-hosted photo library supplying corroborating visual evidence with provenance but never pixels in the butlers DB), media consumption (a scrobble source closing Lifestyle's watched/read promise), consumption of food (a reference database that makes nutrition numbers citable instead of hallucinated), and the long tail of uninstrumented services (a default-deny mobile notification mirror that converts every remaining vendor into routable signal without a per-vendor build). Each lands as the standard four-part pattern — account registry with secured entity_info credentials, a connector meeting the full base contract (filtered-event flush, replay drain, policy gate, heartbeat, metrics, per-account isolation), a module exposing only tools, and a dashboard surface — with a Chronicler adapter carrying source_name, precision, privacy class and retention forward so every projected row is a door back to its evidence. Crucially, the fleet is honest about itself: no catalog entry advertises a channel whose runtime is a stub or whose channel/provider pair ingestion would reject, and no derived value (an inferred reading block, an estimated macro, an unspoken voice reply) is presented with the authority of an observed one. And the loop closes: because Messenger owns a voice channel bound to the mic that heard the request, the owner can speak to the house and be answered by it, with an explicit undeliverable-no-presence outcome when nobody is there to hear.

audits.jarvis_gap: Talking to the butlers is today a one-shot classification pipe with a durable ingress spine bolted to it, not a conversation. The pieces of continuity exist on paper — a channel-agnostic conversation anchor with a provider-resume ledger (`alembic/versions/core/core_185_conversation_anchor_provider_session.py`, wired at `src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py:1015-1027` and consumed at `src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2004-2024`) — but on the owner's primary channel the anchor key is wrong: `telegram_bot` sets `external_thread_id` to `"<chat_id>:<message_id>"` (`src/butlers/connectors/telegram_bot.py:1352-1354`), so every inbound Telegram message mints a *new* anchor, the resume handle can never be re-read, every turn cold-starts, and a titled, zero-message ghost conversation accumulates in the butler's chat list (`src/butlers/api/conversations.py:302-320`, listed unfiltered at `src/butlers/api/conversations.py:137-188`). The specialist is contractually handed a prompt that "must be independently understandable without conversation history" (`src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:461-462`), so the only real memory path is the one that is silently dead. Closure is equally unproven: `route.execute` returns `accepted` immediately (`src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py:1160`) yet the owner sees a 👍 on their Telegram message (`src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:333-341`) that reads as "handled", and the outbound reply row written by Messenger carries no `request_id` back to the inbound message (`roster/switchboard/tools/notification/deliver.py:197-202`), so nothing in the system can answer "did anything the owner said go unanswered?". Cross-channel identity does not exist as a conversation concept at all — the anchor key is `(butler, channel, thread)`, and thread-sticky routing is email-only (`roster/switchboard/tools/triage/thread_affinity.py:348-350`), so the same owner asking the same butler the same question on Telegram, then the dashboard, is three disjoint memories and possibly three different specialists. Against the north star, the conversation spine is broken at the first hop (identity), invisible at the middle hop (resumed vs cold is never surfaced), and unfalsifiable at the last hop (acceptance impersonates completion).

findings.title: Telegram thread identity is per-message, so the conversation anchor and provider-resume ledger are a silent no-op on the owner's primary channel
findings.detail: `telegram_bot._normalize_to_ingest_v1` overloads `event.external_thread_id` as a reply target (`chat_id:message_id`) rather than a conversation identity. `route.execute`'s anchor upsert passes that value verbatim as `source_thread_identity`, so core_185's partial unique index `(butler_name, source_channel, source_thread_identity)` never collides: every inbound Telegram message creates a brand-new `public.dashboard_conversations` row with `message_count 0` and a title auto-derived from the routed prompt. Because the anchor is new each turn, `conversation_get_provider_session` always returns NULL and `resolve_resume_handle` never yields a handle — every Telegram turn cold-starts while the code, spec, and migration all claim 'one memory per thread'. The `pipeline.py` regex that strips `:message_id` before loading history is standing proof the identity is message-scoped; that compensation was never applied to the anchor path.

findings.title: Channel anchors render in the owner's butler chat list as titled, permanently empty conversations
findings.detail: `conversation_list` filters only on `butler_name`/`status` — never on `source_channel` — and the API endpoint passes that through unchanged. Anchor rows created for Telegram/email ingress are therefore listed in `ChatPanel`/`ConversationList` for that butler, titled from the routed message text, but `public.dashboard_messages` rows are only ever written by dashboard paths (`conversation_reply_create` / the dashboard POST-message flow), so opening one shows an empty thread with no explanation of why. Absence is presented with the authority of a real conversation.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/conversations.py:137-188; src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:1273-1303; frontend/src/components/chat/ConversationList.tsx:152; frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx:113; src/butlers/api/conversations.py:299 (_auto_title); src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:1570

findings.title: The Telegram success reaction proves routing acceptance, not that any work was done or any reply was sent
findings.detail: `_process_ingested_message` fires REACTION_SUCCESS/REACTION_FAILURE purely on `pipeline.process` outcome (classification + dispatch). `route.execute` enqueues to the route inbox and returns `accepted` immediately without awaiting the specialist session. So a 👍 on the owner's Telegram message means 'the Switchboard handed this off', while the owner reads it as 'done'. A specialist that crashes, times out, or finishes without calling `notify()` leaves the 👍 standing.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:333-345; src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py:1160; src/butlers/modules/telegram.py:301-349

findings.title: Butler replies are persisted with no causal link back to the message they answer
findings.detail: Messenger's delivery path writes an outbound `switchboard.message_inbox` row whose `request_context` carries only channel/endpoint/sender/thread — no `request_id`, no inbound `message_inbox` id, no session id. There is consequently no join in the system that can answer 'which inbound owner messages were never answered', and the realtime history builder can only re-associate replies by thread proximity.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/notification/deliver.py:197-226; src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:144-171

findings.title: Thread-sticky routing exists only for email; every real-time follow-up is re-classified from scratch and may land on a different specialist
findings.detail: `lookup_thread_affinity` returns MISS for any `source_channel != 'email'`, and the ingest path only calls it under `source_channel == 'email'`. Telegram/WhatsApp follow-ups therefore pay a full classification session each turn and can silently switch specialist mid-thread, splitting one conversation across two butlers with two separate (already-cold) memories. The dashboard has an equivalent stickiness concept (`routed_butler` stamping) that real-time channels do not.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/triage/thread_affinity.py:348-350; roster/switchboard/tools/ingestion/ingest.py:760-770; src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:111-125 (_stamp_routed_butler_best_effort)

findings.title: Whether a turn resumed prior context or cold-started is recorded provider-side and never surfaced anywhere
findings.detail: `provider_session_id` / `provider_runtime_type` / `provider_session_updated_at` are written and read only inside the spawner; no API route, response model, or frontend component reads them. A handle silently expires by TTL, is invalidated by a same-tier failover onto a different runtime adapter, or is evicted after a failed resume — and in every case the owner gets a reply from a butler that has quietly forgotten the thread, with no marker distinguishing it from a continuous one.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/conversations.py:343-420; src/butlers/api/conversations.py:422-457; src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2004-2024, 2690-2700; src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:461-462

findings.title: No channel-native control verbs: the owner can only stop or inspect a turn from the dashboard
findings.detail: `telegram_bot.py` handles no bot commands and has no cancellation path; message-scoped Stop is a dashboard HTTP endpoint bound to a persisted dashboard turn. An owner who starts a long or wrong-headed session from Telegram has no way to stop it, ask what is running, or ask who is handling it from the surface they are actually using.

findings.title: notify() has no way to declare that a reply is expected, so clarification loops depend on classifier guesswork
findings.detail: The notify envelope supports exactly four intents (send, reply, react, insight) and no 'awaits answer' concept. When a butler asks the owner a question, nothing durable records that a question is outstanding; the owner's 'yes' or 'the first one' is re-classified from raw conversation history by the Switchboard, which the conversation-context skill itself documents as fragile enough to need five worked examples and an explicit WRONG-approach warning.
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/core-notify/spec.md:9,259-290; roster/switchboard/.claude/skills/conversation-context/SKILL.md (Examples 4-5, 'the target butler has NO history'); src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:461-462

moves.title: Split conversation identity from reply target in ingest.v1, and rekey every continuity consumer on it
moves.why: Vision success marker 'the owner sends a message from any channel and the right butler handles it' plus Switchboard MANIFESTO 'ingress ownership' make canonical conversation identity a Switchboard responsibility, not a per-connector accident. Today `telegram_bot.py:1352-1354` overloads one field for reply targeting and thread identity, which silently voids the shipped anchor+resume ledger (`core_185`, `src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py:1015-1027`) on the owner's main channel and litters `public.dashboard_conversations` with a ghost row per message. Payoff: Telegram follow-ups actually resume the specialist's prior session; the ghost rows stop; the telegram-specific regex hack in `pipeline.py:134-141` is deleted rather than duplicated into every new consumer.
moves.integration_points: ingest.v1 envelope: add `event.external_conversation_id` (chat/JID/thread scope) and rename the existing field to `event.reply_target_ref`; connectors `src/butlers/connectors/telegram_bot.py:1303-1390`, `telegram_user_client.py:1889-1980`, `whatsapp_user_client.py:2014-2069`, `gmail.py`; `roster/switchboard/tools/ingestion/ingest.py` request_context build; `src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py:903,1015-1027`; `src/butlers/api/conversations.py:274-340`; `src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:114-190`; specs `openspec/specs/connector-telegram-bot`, `openspec/specs/module-pipeline`, `openspec/specs/dashboard-conversations`; migration to backfill/rekey existing anchors. Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract (Ingress ownership, Message classification) — no manifesto amendment needed.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add `external_conversation_id` to the envelope contract with a connector-side derivation per channel and a strict validator; 2) rekey `conversation_get_or_create_by_thread` and the core_185 unique index onto it, with a one-shot migration collapsing per-message Telegram anchors into per-chat anchors (keeping the newest provider handle); 3) move history loading onto the same key and delete `_TELEGRAM_CHAT_MESSAGE_RE`; 4) add a regression that two consecutive Telegram messages in one chat resolve to one anchor and that turn 2 resumes turn 1's provider handle.

moves.title: Continuity receipt: make 'resumed vs cold, and why' a first-class owner-visible property of every turn
moves.why: The north star forbids staleness wearing current-data authority; a butler that silently forgot the last five turns is exactly that. `provider_session_*` is written and read only inside the spawner (`src/butlers/api/conversations.py:343-457`, `src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2004-2024,2690-2700`) — no API or component reads it, so TTL expiry, adapter-swap on same-tier failover, and post-failure eviction are all invisible. Payoff: the owner can tell at a glance whether a reply was written with memory of the thread or from a standing start, and why — the difference between a butler being wrong and a butler being amnesiac.
moves.integration_points: New `public.conversation_turn_continuity` rows (or typed columns on the session row) written by `src/butlers/core/spawner.py` at resume-resolution time: `{outcome: resumed|cold, reason: first_turn|ttl_expired|runtime_type_changed|evicted_after_failed_resume|no_anchor, handle_age_s, history_messages_injected, history_window_minutes, history_truncated}`; exposed on `GET /api/butlers/{name}/conversations/{id}/messages` and the session detail API (`src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py`); rendered as a per-turn chip in `frontend/src/components/chat/MessageThread.tsx`; spec deltas in `openspec/specs/core-spawner` and `openspec/specs/dashboard-conversations`. Distinct from bu-6jv4m.1 (which governs message/evidence reading), this governs how the turn's context was assembled. Serves the Switchboard contract and the general butler base spec.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Emit the receipt from the single resume-resolution site the spawner already owns (pure addition, no behavior change); 2) expose it on the messages read path; 3) render the chip and a 'started fresh — the earlier thread had expired' line in chat; 4) regression: force a TTL expiry and a runtime_type change and assert two distinct reasons, never a bare 'cold'.

moves.title: Thread-sticky specialist routing for every channel with a conversation identity, with an owner-visible stick/unstick control
moves.why: Switchboard MANIFESTO 'Routing execution' and the vision's 'right butler without manual routing' both break when a follow-up lands on a different specialist than the message it follows. Affinity is hard-gated to email (`roster/switchboard/tools/triage/thread_affinity.py:348-350`, `roster/switchboard/tools/ingestion/ingest.py:760-770`) while the dashboard already has an equivalent (`_stamp_routed_butler_best_effort`, `src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:111-125`). Payoff: conversations stop splitting mid-thread, follow-ups get the specialist that already has the resumed session (compounding with move 1), and a full classification session per turn is avoided on the highest-volume channel — a measurable spend reduction with a receipt.
moves.integration_points: Generalize `lookup_thread_affinity` off the canonical conversation id from move 1; `switchboard.thread_affinity_settings` gains per-channel enablement and TTL; write the decision into `switchboard.routing_verdict_log` (migration 019) so a sticky route is as auditable as a classified one; expose `GET/PATCH /api/switchboard/conversations/{id}/affinity` for the owner-facing 'sticky to health since 10:03 · 4 turns · unstick' chip in `frontend/src/components/chat/ConversationHeader.tsx` and a Telegram-side disclosure line; specs `openspec/specs/routing-scorecard`, `openspec/specs/ingestion-policy`, `docs/switchboard/thread_affinity_routing.md`. Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Lift the email-only gate into a per-channel setting with the same conflict/stale outcomes and telemetry that already exist; 2) require an explicit topic-shift escape — classification still runs when the classifier's own confidence in continuity is low, and the verdict log records `sticky_honored` vs `sticky_broken` with reason; 3) surface the sticky state and an unstick action; 4) regression: a stuck thread whose next message is unambiguously another domain must break stickiness and log why.

moves.title: Turn-closure ledger: one durable terminal disposition per inbound owner message, and channel acknowledgement that only fires on it
moves.why: The north star's 'failure never impersonates health' is violated at the most-used surface: the Telegram 👍 fires on `accepted` (`src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:333-345` over `_routing.py:1160`), and Messenger's outbound row carries no link back to the request it answers (`roster/switchboard/tools/notification/deliver.py:197-226`), so no query in the system can produce the set of things the owner said that nobody answered. Payoff: five-second verification that nothing fell on the floor, and a reaction that means what the owner thinks it means.
moves.integration_points: New `switchboard.conversation_turn_closure` table keyed on the inbound `request_id`, with edges to `session_id`, the outbound `message_inbox` id, and a typed terminal state (`replied`, `acted_silently`, `dead_lettered`, `failed`, `abandoned_no_owner`); written by the route-inbox finalizer in `src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py:1090-1150` and by `roster/switchboard/tools/notification/deliver.py` (which must stamp `in_reply_to_request_id` into the outbound `request_context`); reaction lifecycle moves from `_process_ingested_message` to the closure writer, with a distinct glyph for 'handled, no reply by design'; new `GET /api/switchboard/conversations/unclosed` feeding an 'unanswered turns' radar on the dashboard; specs `openspec/specs/butler-switchboard`, `openspec/specs/butler-messenger`, `openspec/specs/core-notify`. Serves both the Switchboard and Messenger infrastructure contracts (Messenger's 'Outcome reporting' and 'Lineage preservation' clauses become provable rather than aspirational).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Stamp `in_reply_to_request_id` on the outbound row and add the closure table with a write from the existing route finalizer (observe-only: no reaction change); 2) add the unclosed-turns query and radar, and let it run for a week against real traffic to calibrate 'acted_silently'; 3) move the terminal Telegram reaction onto the closure writer behind a flag, with an explicit 'still working' state that survives daemon restart; 4) regression: kill the daemon between acceptance and session completion and assert the turn ends `abandoned_no_owner` with the reaction reflecting it, never 👍.

moves.title: Open-question ledger: a butler may declare it is waiting on an answer, and the next message on that thread deterministically returns to it
moves.why: Continuity today survives short answers only because the Switchboard classifier is coached with five worked examples and a WRONG-approach warning (`roster/switchboard/.claude/skills/conversation-context/SKILL.md`), because the specialist is contractually handed a self-contained prompt with no history (`src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:461-462`). A one-word 'yes' resolving to the right pending action must be a deterministic lookup, not an LLM inference. The mechanism is already in the envelope: `control.pinned_target` is validated against the live routable registry before any dedupe return (`roster/switchboard/tools/ingestion/ingest.py:660-680`). Payoff: bare confirmations and selections become reliable; the owner gets a visible list of questions the butlers are waiting on, and questions that expire say so instead of evaporating.
moves.integration_points: `notify()` gains `awaits_reply` + `question_ref` (spec delta on `openspec/specs/core-notify`, tool surface in `src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py`); new `switchboard.conversation_open_questions` (conversation id, asking butler, question text, session id, expires_at, resolution) written by the notify delivery path (`roster/switchboard/tools/notification/deliver.py`); read in `roster/switchboard/tools/ingestion/ingest.py` before rule evaluation to set `control.pinned_target` and attach the pending question to the routed prompt; closed by the answering session; exposed at `GET /api/switchboard/open-questions` and as an 'awaiting your answer' lane on the dashboard chat and the overview. Serves the Switchboard contract plus the domain manifestos that ask the most questions (roster/relationship, roster/health); no amendment required since asking-and-waiting is already implicit in their interactive response modes.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Ledger + notify field, write-only, with a TTL and an owner-visible list (no routing change); 2) pin the next inbound message on that conversation to the asking butler and inject the question verbatim, recording a `pinned_by_open_question` verdict; 3) expire questions visibly ('health stopped waiting on this after 24h') rather than silently; 4) regression: a bare 'yes' on a thread with an open question routes to the asking butler with the question attached, and the same 'yes' with no open question still falls through to classification.

moves.title: Cross-channel conversation braid: one owner-scoped thread of talk that survives changing channel
moves.why: The anchor key is `(butler, channel, thread)` (`alembic/versions/core/core_185_conversation_anchor_provider_session.py`), so the same owner asking the same butler about the same thing on Telegram and then the dashboard is two memories with two provider sessions — precisely the 'no manual routing, any channel' promise in vision.md 'What Success Looks Like' left unmet. Payoff: the owner can start on Telegram and finish on the dashboard (or the reverse) without re-establishing context, and the surface says where the context came from instead of pretending it was always there.
moves.integration_points: New `public.conversation_braids` + `public.conversation_braid_members` linking anchors by (owner entity id from `src/butlers/core/owner.py`, butler, recency/topic window); braid resolution in `src/butlers/core_tools/_routing.py` before the anchor upsert, with the provider handle promoted to the braid rather than the anchor (`src/butlers/api/conversations.py:343-396`, `src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2004-2024`); a `continued from telegram · 4m ago` provenance chip and an explicit 'move this conversation here' handoff action in `frontend/src/components/chat/ConversationHeader.tsx`; read model on `GET /api/butlers/{name}/conversations` (which must gain the `source_channel` filter that finding 2 shows is missing); spec deltas on `openspec/specs/dashboard-conversations` and `openspec/specs/switchboard-identity`. Implies a Switchboard MANIFESTO amendment: 'conversation identity' joins ingress ownership, message classification, and the agent/connector registries as an explicit Switchboard responsibility, since no domain butler may own a concept that spans channels.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Land the `source_channel` filter and a channel badge so the existing anchors stop lying about being dashboard chats; 2) add the braid tables and resolve braids read-only, showing the provenance chip without changing which handle is resumed; 3) promote the provider handle to the braid behind a flag, with one-in-flight-turn-per-braid serialization so two channels cannot fork the same provider session concurrently; 4) add the explicit owner handoff action; 5) regression: a Telegram turn followed by a dashboard turn on the same braid resumes one session, and two simultaneous turns on the braid serialize rather than fork.

audits.ideal: Talking to a butler is one continuous, provable relationship rather than a stream of independent classifications. Every inbound utterance carries a canonical conversation identity that is distinct from its reply target, so one chat is one anchor across restarts, connectors, and channels; that anchor holds the specialist's working memory, and a braid ties anchors together per owner and butler so the conversation follows the person from Telegram to the dashboard and back with a visible 'continued from' provenance rather than a silent reset. Routing is sticky to the specialist that already holds the thread, and stickiness is a logged verdict with an owner-visible stick/unstick door and an explicit topic-shift escape. Every turn carries a continuity receipt stating whether it resumed prior context or started cold and exactly why, so an amnesiac reply is legible as amnesia instead of passing as judgment. When a butler needs an answer, it says so durably: the open question is a ledger row, the owner's one-word reply is deterministically pinned back to the asking butler with the question attached, and an unanswered question expires out loud. And every inbound message ends in exactly one durable terminal disposition — replied, acted silently by design, dead-lettered, failed, or abandoned — with the channel's own acknowledgement glyph driven by that disposition and nothing earlier, the outbound reply linked by request id to the message it answers, and an 'unanswered turns' radar the owner can clear in seconds. Control lives on whichever surface the owner is using: stop, status, and who-is-handling-this work from Telegram as well as the dashboard.

audits.jarvis_gap: The fleet has seven separate cross-butler mechanisms — the Switchboard route() spine, the delegation ledger, the domain-event bus with publisher-owned contracts, the insight broker, the context bus, public.owner_conditions, and sanctioned read-only views like general.v_briefing_contributions and public.atmosphere_readings — and every one of them is single-hop and pairwise. Delegation resolves exactly one target from one catalog hit (src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py:587) and never re-uses its own answers; the bus is fire-and-forget with two migration-seeded subscriptions fleet-wide (alembic/versions/core/core_186_domain_events.py:168, core_189_domain_event_bus_slice2_seed.py:31) and two of its four declared contracts forbid all subscribers outright (roster/finance/domain_events.toml:16, roster/health/domain_events.toml:16); the broker groups correlated candidates but has no vocabulary for two specialists disagreeing (roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:840-874, 1004-1030); the context bus lets travel assert `traveling` while home asserts `at_home` and answers True to both (src/butlers/context_bus.py:295-302). Nothing in the repository represents a multi-domain owner situation as one durable object that several butlers each hold a verifiable slice of, so there is no unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine that crosses a butler boundary: the owner still assembles "I'm moving house" or "I'm sick and flying Thursday" by hand across five pages, and a specialist that had nothing to say is indistinguishable from one that was never asked. The ideal is a fleet that can open a case, resolve a cohort rather than a single target, let stakeholders object before the owner is asked to decide, disagree out loud when it disagrees, remember its own answers with a validity horizon, and declare in Git exactly which butlers participate in each collaboration mechanism so a dark edge is visible instead of assumed. Today the plumbing for all of that exists and is hardened; the collaboration itself is almost entirely unlit.
audits.ideal: A world-class cross-butler ecosystem treats a multi-domain owner situation as a first-class durable object, not as N unrelated single-hop messages. The Switchboard, already the only sanctioned channel and already host to the insight broker, also brokers cases: it resolves a cohort of relevant specialists from the shared memory catalog, opens one typed slice per butler, and closes the case only when every slice reaches a terminal state — answered, declined with a reason, or failed — so the owner reads one door with a completeness receipt instead of assembling five pages. Specialists can be heard before the owner decides: a high-risk approval opens a bounded, non-blocking consultation window in which stakeholder butlers attach exactly one evidence-bearing objection, caution, or endorsement, and a butler that did not answer shows as not-consulted rather than silently absent. When two specialists disagree, disagreement is itself a delivery outcome with a named arbitration line, never two confident bullets. Shared owner state is a single arbitrated answer with a declared exclusivity lattice and a visible contested set, not an unranked pile of assertions from independent writers. The fleet remembers its own answers: every delegated answer carries evidence refs and a validity horizon, is written back into the same catalog that resolution reads, and is served from cache with an explicit cached-and-valid-until plaque or re-asked when expired. And participation in each mechanism — who publishes, who subscribes, who contributes to the briefing — is declared in Git per non-negotiable rule 5 and gated in CI, so adding a butler lights it up everywhere or fails loudly, and no butler is dark by config drift.

findings.title: Two of four declared domain-event contracts forbid every subscriber; the bus is publish-to-nowhere
findings.evidence: roster/finance/domain_events.toml:16, roster/health/domain_events.toml:16 (`permitted_subscribers = []`); alembic/versions/core/core_186_domain_events.py:168 and alembic/versions/core/core_189_domain_event_bus_slice2_seed.py:31 (the only two subscriptions in existence, both migration-seeded); roster/relationship/butler.toml:11-20 (explicit core_groups omits `domain_events`)
findings.detail: Only 3 of 12 roster members declare a domain_events.toml. finance.budget_pressure and health.recovery_state are published into a void by contract — the fail-closed admission layer will refuse any subscription to them. Relationship, the butler that owns people and occasions, is structurally unable to publish or subscribe because its explicit core_groups list predates the `domain_events` group. The bus's contract machinery is hardened; its vocabulary is nearly empty and one participant is locked out by config drift.

findings.title: Delegated answers are dead-end artifacts: no catalog write-back, no evidence, no validity horizon
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py:192-240 (record_answer sets only answer/answered_at/answering_butler); src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py:565-590 (resolve_target_via_catalog reads public.memory_catalog); openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md:116 (Discoverability requires only that the row be readable)
findings.detail: The fleet cannot learn from its own Q&A. The same cross-domain question next month re-resolves, re-routes and re-spawns a target-butler LLM session, because answers never enter the index that resolution reads. And an answer carries no evidence citation and no expiry, so a three-month-old answer read back from the ledger wears exactly the authority of one recorded this morning — the staleness failure the north star forbids, sitting inside the collaboration primitive itself.

findings.title: Delegation truncates a multi-domain question to a single top catalog hit
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py:587 (`search_memory_catalog(pool, question, limit=1, mode="hybrid")`); openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md:31-56 (top hit names the target; no-hit is `unroutable`, self-hit is `self_target`)
findings.detail: A question whose answer genuinely lives in three domains ("can I afford and physically manage the Lisbon trip in November?") either goes to whichever schema happened to score highest or is recorded unroutable. There is no cohort concept anywhere in the codebase: no way to ask N butlers one question and receive a completeness receipt naming who answered, who declined, and who never replied.

findings.title: The context bus can hold mutually exclusive owner states simultaneously with no arbitration
findings.evidence: src/butlers/context_bus.py:295-302 (get_active_context returns every non-superseded, unexpired row ordered by confidence); openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md, User Context Table Schema (UNIQUE is `(signal_type, set_by_butler)` — per-writer, not per-signal); openspec/changes/context-bus-producers/specs/context-bus/spec.md:17-19 (home writes at_home, travel writes traveling, independently)
findings.detail: Nothing declares which signals are incompatible. With the producer change in flight, travel's `traveling` (which can legitimately stay active for the length of a trip) and home's `at_home` can both be active, and is_user_in_context answers True to both. Every downstream consumer — the notify dnd/sleeping gate, the spawner situational preamble, the attention-ledger context reasons, and the broker's presence suppression — reasons from a self-contradictory picture and reports none of it as degraded.

findings.title: Insight brokering groups correlated candidates but has no representation for specialists disagreeing
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:362 (deduplicate_candidates: identical dedup_key only), :840-874 (_cluster_candidates: shared entity or overlapping window, union-find), :1004-1030 (_format_digest renders `Correlated (N):` plus a best-effort LLM synthesis); openspec/changes/archive/2026-02-24-alpha-release-mvp/specs/butler-switchboard/spec.md:525-532 (a Conflict Arbitration Contract was specified as TARGET-STATE and archived unimplemented; the current openspec/specs/butler-switchboard/spec.md has no such requirement)
findings.detail: Clustering makes "these happen in the same week" visible. It cannot make "Health says rest, Travel says the 06:00 flight is booked" visible — those land as two confident numbered bullets, possibly inside the same Correlated group, with a synthesised sentence smoothing over the contradiction. Failure of fleet agreement currently impersonates fleet consensus.

findings.title: Briefing fleet membership is hardcoded in two places and silently drops butler-typed members
findings.evidence: src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:42-50 (SPECIALIST_BUTLERS, seven names), :1393-1394 (`frozenset(SPECIALIST_BUTLERS) & butler_typed_names`), :1517 (missing_butlers derived from that intersection); openspec/specs/cross-butler-briefing-aggregation/spec.md, Cross-Schema Briefing View (a hardcoded 7-schema UNION in migration core_063 that must stay in sync with the Python tuple); roster/chronicler/butler.toml (butler-typed by default, no daily_briefing_contribution schedule)
findings.detail: Chronicler is a domain butler that is intersected out of the expected set, so it contributes nothing and never appears as missing. Adding any butler requires a migration plus two hardcoded lists edited in lockstep, and getting it wrong produces silence rather than an error. The owner's daily briefing therefore asserts fleet coverage the code cannot support.

findings.title: Approvals are single-butler: an owner decision card carries one specialist's view
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/approvals/module.py:618, :668 (unqualified `pending_actions` — a per-butler-schema table under the butler's search_path); openspec/specs/module-approvals/spec.md (requirements cover Gate Wrapper, Pending Actions Queue, Standing Rules, Risk Tier, Authorization — no cross-butler concept anywhere)
findings.detail: A Lifestyle discretionary purchase, a Travel booking, or a Home maintenance spend reaches the owner carrying only the originating butler's reasoning, even though Finance holds public.spend_rules/public.spend_ceiling and Health may hold an open recovery condition that would change the answer. The fleet has the knowledge; the decision surface never sees it.

findings.title: Commitments escalate to the owner but are never routed to a butler that could discharge them
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/owner_conditions.py:37-41 (source is `{origin_butler}:{category}`); src/butlers/jobs/commitment_escalation.py:1-30 (the job walks commitment-class rows, moves the escalation clock, and hands them to the proactive insight engine); src/butlers/core/commitments.py:14-24 (a commitment has no deterministic producer by construction)
findings.detail: "I told Sam I'd send him that book" is captured by Relationship and then escalated L0 through L3 back at the owner. No step asks whether General (order it), Home (locate it) or Finance (budget it) could advance the obligation. The system converts an open loop into a recurring nag rather than into fleet work — the opposite of vision.md's success measure, "the amount of mental labor the system reliably absorbs".

moves.title: Fleet Case File: a durable multi-domain situation object with per-butler slices and a completeness receipt
moves.why: vision.md has the Switchboard "maintain shared situational awareness so butlers adapt to the user's current context", and measures success as mental labor absorbed — but every existing cross-butler primitive is single-hop: delegation resolves one target (delegation_ledger.py:587), the bus is fire-and-forget with no composite outcome (src/butlers/core/domain_events.py module docstring), the broker collapses to one flat digest (broker.py:1004-1030). Payoff: the owner opens one door for "moving house Nov 3" or "sick, flying Thursday" and sees in five seconds which specialists answered, what each committed to, which declined and why, and which never replied — the first unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine that crosses a butler boundary. A butler with nothing to say says so explicitly instead of being silent.
moves.integration_points: New `public.fleet_cases` (id, opened_by, summary, horizon, status, closed_at, closure_evidence) and `public.fleet_case_slices` (case_id, butler, state in open|acked|answered|declined|failed|expired, answer, evidence_refs, terminal_at) with UNIQUE (case_id, butler) mirroring public.domain_event_deliveries' atomic-claim discipline. New Switchboard `case_broker` module alongside roster/switchboard/modules/insight_broker.py (precedent: about/heart-and-soul/architecture.md, "the insight broker module (RFC 0011) runs within the Switchboard daemon ... its scope is cross-butler coordination"). Tools case_open/case_receive/case_answer/case_decline/case_status under a new `cases` core group; cohort resolution reuses search_memory_catalog with limit=N (fixing delegation_ledger.py:587); dispatch reuses the existing route() primitive only, per non-negotiable rule 3. New capability spec `cross-butler-case-file`; API at /api/cases/* mirroring src/butlers/api/routers/delegation.py's non-fan-out shape. Manifesto: requires a Switchboard MANIFESTO.md amendment adding "Multi-domain case brokerage" to Responsibilities — coordination, not domain logic, so the existing "does not execute domain logic" non-responsibility is preserved.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Tables plus case_open/case_receive/case_answer/case_decline with the ledger-honesty contract (every terminal slice state persisted, never silently dropped) and case-closes-only-when-all-slices-terminal. 2) Multi-hit cohort resolution (catalog limit=N, dedup by source_butler, self-exclusion) plus a typed completeness receipt on case read. 3) Owner-visible case door listing open cases with per-slice cohort receipt and evidence links. 4) Auto-open a case from a domain event whose contract declares reaction_expectation='expected' and two or more permitted_subscribers, so the bus and the case file share one spine.

moves.title: Stakeholder consultation window: fleet objections attached to an approval before the owner is asked
moves.why: Non-negotiable rule 6 makes every manifesto binding, and the Finance and Health manifestos promise domain protection — but they have no way to be heard about a decision another butler owns, because pending_actions is per-schema (modules/approvals/module.py:618, :668) and openspec/specs/module-approvals has no cross-butler requirement. Payoff: a one-tap owner decision carries the fleet's view rather than one specialist's, and a stakeholder that did not answer in time renders as not-consulted rather than silently absent — no fabricated consensus. This is collaboration none of them can do alone: only Finance knows the ceiling, only Health knows the recovery state, only the originating butler knows the action.
moves.integration_points: New `public.approval_annotations` (approval_id, origin_butler, source_butler, kind in objection|caution|endorse|no_stake, rationale, evidence_ref, created_at, UNIQUE (approval_id, source_butler)) — the cross-butler half lives in public while pending_actions stays per-schema, respecting RFC 0006. Switchboard-brokered consultation over route(), sharing the cohort resolver with the case file. Hooks at src/butlers/modules/approvals/gate.py (open the window on a risk-tier gate) and module.py's queue read (join annotations). Specs: modify openspec/specs/module-approvals (new Stakeholder Consultation requirement) and feed openspec/specs/dashboard-decisions' detail view. Complements bu-ckkpz by supplying what the Decision Desk renders rather than restating the desk. No manifesto amendment: butlers stay advisory, the owner still decides.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Table plus an annotate_approval tool with one annotation per butler and a mandatory evidence_ref. 2) Bounded, non-blocking consultation window on high-risk-tier gates only — an approval never waits on a slow butler, and the window closing is itself a recorded outcome. 3) Decision-card rendering with explicit not-consulted / did-not-answer states per stakeholder. 4) Wire two real edges: Finance annotating spend-class approvals from public.spend_rules/spend_ceiling, Health annotating scheduling and travel approvals from an open recovery condition.

moves.title: Disagreement as a first-class delivery outcome in the insight broker
moves.why: proactive-insight-engine dedups only identical dedup_keys, and the shipped _cluster_candidates (broker.py:840-874) links by shared entity or overlapping window — grouping, never disagreement. A Conflict Arbitration Contract was specified once and archived unimplemented (openspec/changes/archive/2026-02-24-alpha-release-mvp/specs/butler-switchboard/spec.md:525-532). Payoff: when two specialists recommend opposite actions inside one window, the owner gets one arbitration line naming both butlers and the incompatibility, escalated as a decision, instead of two confident nudges plus a synthesised sentence papering over the conflict. Failure of fleet agreement stops impersonating fleet consensus.
moves.integration_points: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py: a `stance` field on the candidate metadata contract (advises|discourages plus a normalised action key) submitted through the existing propose_insight_candidate tool; a new `_detect_conflicts` pass over each cluster produced by _cluster_candidates; a new terminal candidate status `arbitrated` alongside delivered/expired/filtered (openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine's Valid status transitions scenario needs the addition); _format_digest renders a `Conflict:` block and routes it through the decision path rather than the digest bullet path. Specs: modify proactive-insight-engine and insight-delivery. Producer adoption in the health/finance/travel/relationship insight_scan jobs. Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract — cross-domain arbitration is already its brokering role per RFC 0011 — so no manifesto amendment.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add the stance contract, fail-closed rejecting a stance-bearing candidate with no action key (matching the domain-event contract loader's discipline). 2) _detect_conflicts within existing clusters; render the Conflict block; never silently drop either side. 3) Route a detected conflict to the owner decision path with both evidence cohorts attached. 4) Adopt stance in the two producer pairs most likely to collide: health recovery vs travel departure, finance budget pressure vs lifestyle discretionary.

moves.title: Declared exclusivity for the context bus, and one arbitrated read of owner state
moves.why: context-bus's UNIQUE is (signal_type, set_by_butler) and get_active_context returns every active row (src/butlers/context_bus.py:295-302), so with the in-flight producers (openspec/changes/context-bus-producers/specs/context-bus/spec.md:17-19) `traveling` and `at_home` can both read true and is_user_in_context answers True to both. Every consumer — notify's dnd/sleeping gate, the spawner preamble, the attention ledger, the broker's presence suppression — then reasons from a self-contradictory picture and reports nothing as degraded. Payoff: vision.md's "shared situational awareness" becomes a single coherent answer with a named winner and a visible contested set, rather than a pile of unranked assertions.
moves.integration_points: New `public.context_exclusions` (signal_a, signal_b, resolution in higher_confidence|newer|explicit_priority) seeded by migration with the real pairs (traveling vs at_home, sleeping vs meeting, sleeping vs exercising, away vs at_home). src/butlers/context_bus.py gains `get_arbitrated_context()` returning winners plus a typed contested list, and set_context refuses to silently coexist with an excluded live signal — it supersedes and records that it did. Consumers updated: src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py, src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py, src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py, roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py. Spec: modify openspec/specs/context-bus with an Exclusivity And Arbitration requirement — it is currently silent on cross-writer conflict. No new butler, no manifesto amendment.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Table plus seeded exclusion pairs plus get_arbitrated_context returning winners and contested. 2) Flip the four consumers to the arbitrated read, surfacing contested rather than hiding it. 3) set_context supersession-on-exclusion with an audit reason. 4) Expose contested state on the existing situational surfaces so an unresolved contradiction is owner-visible, never invisible.

moves.title: Delegated answers become fleet knowledge: evidence, a validity horizon, and cache-before-dispatch
moves.why: record_answer writes only the answer text (delegation_ledger.py:192-240) while resolution reads public.memory_catalog (delegation_ledger.py:587), so the fleet is structurally incapable of learning from its own cross-domain Q&A: every repeat question pays a fresh target-butler LLM session, and a stale answer read back wears full current-data authority. Payoff: repeat cross-domain questions become instant and near-free, and an expired answer can never impersonate a fresh one — it becomes an explicit re-ask carrying the prior answer as fenced context. This applies the north star's "staleness never wears current-data authority" clause to the collaboration layer itself.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py: record_answer gains required, non-empty typed `evidence_refs` and a required `valid_until`; a catalog write-back through src/butlers/core/memory_hooks.py registering the answer under kind `delegated_answer` with source_butler = answering_butler. delegate_ask gains a pre-dispatch lookup for a live prior answer to a semantically equivalent question, returning it with an "answered N days ago by X, valid until T" plaque and a receipt naming it cached, never fresh. Spec: modify openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation — extend Discoverability to catalog write-back and add an Answer Freshness Contract requirement. Serves every domain manifesto's honesty clause (e.g. roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md:80, "I will never claim a certainty I do not have") and the Switchboard's routing-economy contract; no amendment.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Required evidence_refs and valid_until on delegate_answer, refused fail-closed when absent. 2) Catalog write-back on answered rows attributed to the answering butler. 3) Cache-before-dispatch in delegate_ask with an explicit cached-vs-fresh receipt in the response. 4) Expiry path: an expired cached answer never returns as current; it opens a re-ask carrying the prior answer and its expiry as fenced context.

moves.title: Declared fleet participation: one Git manifest for who publishes, who listens, and who briefs — with a coverage gate
moves.why: Participation in every collaboration mechanism is either hardcoded in Python plus a migration (SPECIALIST_BUTLERS at briefing.py:42-50, intersected at :1393-1394 against the 7-schema UNION view) or accidentally excluded by config drift (roster/relationship/butler.toml:11-20 omits the `domain_events` core group), and two declared contracts forbid every subscriber (roster/finance/domain_events.toml:16, roster/health/domain_events.toml:16). Non-negotiable rule 5 puts identity — including what a butler is for in the ecosystem — in Git. Payoff: adding a butler lights it up everywhere or fails loudly; Chronicler stops being silently absent from the owner's briefing; a dark bus edge becomes a CI failure instead of an assumption; and the briefing gains a coverage receipt naming who contributed, who declined and why, and who was silent.
moves.integration_points: New `[butler.fleet]` block in each roster/*/butler.toml (publishes_events, subscribes_events, contributes_briefing), parsed in src/butlers/config.py beside the existing runtime_seed parsing and cross-validated against roster/*/domain_events.toml by the loader in src/butlers/core/domain_event_contracts.py. Replace SPECIALIST_BUTLERS and the hardcoded general.v_briefing_contributions UNION with registry-driven membership via a migration that regenerates the view from declared contributors, preserving the RFC 0006/0010 read-only exception. A make-check-level coverage gate refuses a contract with empty permitted_subscribers and no documented intentionally_unsubscribed reason, and refuses a declared subscriber lacking the `domain_events` core group. Add `domain_events` to roster/relationship/butler.toml core_groups. The combined briefing payload carries contributed/declined/silent per butler, replacing the intersection-derived missing_butlers at briefing.py:1517. Specs: modify cross-butler-briefing-aggregation, cross-butler-briefing-contribution, domain-event-bus.
moves.slice_plan: 1) `[butler.fleet]` parsing plus the CI coverage gate run over existing declarations — it fails today on the two empty-subscriber contracts and on Relationship's missing group, which is the point. 2) Registry-driven briefing membership plus coverage receipt replacing the two hardcoded lists. 3) Regenerate the aggregation view from declared contributors; make Chronicler either a declared contributor or an explicit declared non-contributor. 4) Add the high-value bus edges the gate exposes: relationship.occasion_upcoming to finance and general; health.recovery_state to general and travel; finance.budget_pressure to lifestyle.

moves.title: Commitment discharge routing: turn an owner nag into fleet work
moves.why: A commitment is an owner_conditions row sourced `{origin_butler}:{category}` (src/butlers/core/owner_conditions.py:37-41), and commitment_escalation only advances the L0-L3 clock and hands the row to the proactive insight engine (src/butlers/jobs/commitment_escalation.py:1-30) — the fleet never asks whether another butler could advance the obligation. vision.md measures success as "the amount of mental labor the system reliably absorbs", and re-surfacing the same open loop four times absorbs none. Payoff: "I told Sam I'd send him that book" produces a General order draft or a Home "it is on the shelf in the study" answer before the owner is nagged a third time, with the assist recorded as evidence on the condition itself.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/jobs/commitment_escalation.py: before advancing a level, resolve a capable-butler cohort via search_memory_catalog (shared with the case-file cohort resolver) and open a slice — a delegation row today, a fleet_case_slice once the case file lands — asking whether the target can discharge or advance the commitment. The answer or explicit decline is written into the condition's evidence through the existing resolve/confirm path in src/butlers/core/condition_ledger.py, so a commitment closed by another butler still carries the mandatory evidence_closed receipt (REQ-commitment-lifecycle-008, no silent resolution). Spec: modify the shipped commitment-lifecycle capability with a Discharge Routing requirement. Serves the Relationship manifesto (which captures the commitment) and the General/Home manifestos (which can act); no amendment, since each butler acts strictly inside its own domain.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Cohort resolution at escalation-eligibility time with a strict per-commitment attempt budget so a stubborn loop never spams the fleet. 2) Assist request over the existing delegation path; decline and no-answer are recorded outcomes, never silence. 3) Assist result written to condition evidence, so owner surfacing shows "Home checked: not on the study shelf" beside the nag. 4) Escalation level advances only after the assist round terminalises, so the owner is asked last rather than first.

audits.jarvis_gap: The inference loop is unusually well-built at its edges and unusually blind in its middle. Model resolution is genuinely sophisticated — a tiered catalog with circuit breakers (`src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:418-680`), spend rules, quotas, a monthly ceiling, same-tier failover, an API-direct lane that skips the CLI cold start for classification and discretion (`src/butlers/core/runtimes/api.py:1-35`), and speculative MCP/runtime prewarm fired the moment the routing decision settles (`src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1145-1200`). But once a session is chosen, nothing about it is bounded, observed while it runs, or measured afterwards in a way that could change the next decision. Every declared cost bound is inert: `max_turns` is enforced by no adapter (`src/butlers/core/runtimes/claude_code.py:259-262`), `max_tool_calls` defaults to `0` = disabled and is set by no caller anywhere (`src/butlers/core/spawner.py:200`), `max_token_budget` exists on exactly two schedules in one butler (`roster/relationship/butler.toml:32,46`), and every guardrail is explicitly post-invocation (`src/butlers/core/spawner_guardrails.py:3`) — so a spend-rule per-call cap almost always lands in the "cap not enforceable pre-spawn, allowing dispatch" branch (`src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1711-1726`) and the only real bound on any session's cost is a wall clock. Money truth is worse: with up to ten failover attempts per logical session (`src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2038`), only the winning attempt's usage ever reaches `public.token_usage_ledger` (`src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2531-2542, 3249`), and `check_monthly_ceiling()` reads exactly that ledger (`src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:2690`) — a failover or timeout storm burns real provider tokens while the budget gate reports calm. Latency truth is thin: both hot adapters buffer the entire subprocess through `communicate()` and parse only after exit (`claude_code.py:496-499,535`; `codex.py:2414-2417,2478`), the dashboard "SSE" stream is a keepalive poll that emits nothing until the reply row lands (`src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:411-424`), spawn admission is a plain FIFO semaphore with no notion of whether the owner is waiting (`src/butlers/core/spawner.py:221-251,748-777`), and the Switchboard manifesto's binding `< 5 s p99` classification SLA (`roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:37`) has nothing in the admission path defending it. And capability: complexity is a one-shot guess made by a cheap classifier reading only message text (`src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:470-475`), never revisited; the one evidence loop that exists scores models on exit code, p95 latency, and a fictional fixed 2000-in/500-out token profile (`src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:689-690,734-780`) with no term for whether the work was done well or whether a cheaper tier would have sufficed. The ideal is a loop where every consequential number — what a call may spend, what it did spend, how long the owner waited, whether the tier fit — is measured in-band, bounds the next call, and is a door on the same signal-to-session-to-evidence spine; today the loop spends confidently and learns almost nothing.

findings.title: Failover and timeout token spend never reaches the ledger, so the monthly ceiling reports calm while money burns
findings.detail: The failover loop allows up to 10 attempts per logical session, but `record_token_usage` runs once after the loop using the winning attempt's `usage` (plus one narrow empty-response case). A failed attempt's tokens are never assigned to `_ledger_input_tokens`. Worse, on timeout both hot adapters discard the entire buffered stdout — including any completed `result` event carrying usage — so the spend is not merely unrecorded but unmeasurable. `check_monthly_ceiling()` and `/api/spend` read exactly that ledger, so a failover or timeout storm can blow the owner's budget while the ceiling gate answers 'under budget'. This is failure impersonating health on the money axis.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2038 (_MAX_FAILOVER_ATTEMPTS = 10); src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2531-2542 (usage captured only after loop exit); src/butlers/core/spawner.py:3244-3259 (single ledger write); src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2286-2304 (only other write, empty-response case); src/butlers/core/runtimes/claude_code.py:496-499,539-548; src/butlers/core/runtimes/codex.py:2414-2417,2483-2500; src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:2690 (check_monthly_ceiling reads the ledger)

findings.title: Every declared per-session cost bound is inert; a spend-rule per-call cap silently does nothing
findings.detail: `max_turns` is documented as accepted-but-not-enforced in every adapter; `max_tool_calls` defaults to 0 (explicitly 'disables the check') and is set by no caller in the repo; `max_token_budget` appears on exactly two schedule rows in one butler. The guardrail module states outright that it detects budget-exceeding sessions *after* invocation. Consequently `_estimate_worst_case_call_cost()` returns None for essentially every dispatch and the per-call cap enforcement block logs 'cap not enforceable pre-spawn, allowing dispatch' and proceeds. The owner can set a per-call spend cap in the UI that has no effect on any real dispatch, and is never told so.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/runtimes/claude_code.py:259-262,343-345; src/butlers/core/spawner.py:200 (_DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 0); src/butlers/core/spawner_guardrails.py:3,113,120; roster/relationship/butler.toml:32,46; src/butlers/core/spawner.py:294-334,1699-1726

findings.title: stream-json is fully buffered, so a running session is invisible and a timed-out one loses all its work
findings.detail: Both hot adapters spawn the CLI with `--output-format stream-json` and then swallow the whole stream through `communicate()`, parsing only after the process exits. Nothing consumes the incremental events. As a result the dashboard's 'SSE stream' is a keepalive poll that emits nothing between `dispatch_accepted` and the final `message_complete`, and on timeout `stdout_bytes` never binds — every completed tool call, all partial reasoning, the provider session id, and the usage numbers are thrown away. The Claude adapter additionally raises on non-zero exit before parsing stdout it already holds, where Codex has a recovery path.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/runtimes/claude_code.py:445-446,496-499,524-532,535-537,539-548; src/butlers/core/runtimes/codex.py:2414-2417,2439-2453,2478,2483-2500; src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:411-424,1477-1481

findings.title: Spawn admission is priority-blind FIFO; an owner's live turn queues behind or is rejected by background work
findings.detail: The process-wide cap is a plain `asyncio.Semaphore` (default 3) and the per-butler cap defaults to 1. The admission block special-cases only self-trigger deadlock and queue-full backpressure — it has no notion of trigger class, deadline, or whether a human is watching an SSE stream. An owner message routed while three cron/healing sessions hold the global slots waits behind them, and when the waiter queue is full it is rejected outright with 'spawner queue is full'. The Switchboard manifesto binds a `< 5 s p99` classification latency target that nothing in this path defends or measures.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:221-251,448-450,735-777,784-800; roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:33-39

findings.title: Routing evidence scores exit codes and a fictional token profile; nothing measures whether the tier fit
