findings.detail: `compute_routing_score()` combines success rate (only `success` vs `runtime_failure` outcomes), p95 duration, and a per-call USD cost derived from a hardcoded 2000-input/500-output reference profile. There is no term for whether the session produced good work, and the cost axis is priced on a token profile no butler actually runs, even though the real per-butler, per-purpose distribution already sits in `public.token_usage_ledger` with a `purpose` dimension. Nothing anywhere asks whether a task assigned `reasoning` could have run on `workhorse`, or vice versa.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:684-690,734-784,785-800; alembic/versions/core/core_156_token_usage_ledger_purpose.py:51-56

findings.title: Complexity is a one-shot guess by a cheap classifier and 9 of 12 prompt schedules declare none
findings.detail: The routing prompt asks the classifier to set the target butler's `complexity` from message text alone, before anything is known about the target's state or workload. On the scheduled side, only 3 of the 12 prompt-mode schedules in the roster declare a complexity; the other 9 silently inherit `workhorse` per the spec default. The tier is never revisited during or after the session, so both an over-provisioned nudge and an under-provisioned research task are permanent mistakes.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:470-475; roster/*/butler.toml (12 prompt-mode schedules; only chronicler_day_close=reasoning, chronicler_gap_interview=cheap declare a tier); openspec/specs/complexity-classification/spec.md (Tick Trigger Complexity, default workhorse)

findings.title: The API fast-lane classifier carries a hardcoded roster that omits two live routable butlers
findings.detail: `ROUTE_TO_BUTLER_TOOL`'s `butler` parameter description enumerates 'finance, health, relationship, travel, education, lifestyle, general' — 7 of the 9 non-staffer butlers in the roster. `home` and `chronicler` are absent. The CLI lane builds its butler list from the live registry, so the optimization introduced a capability regression the CLI lane does not have, and duplicates git-owned butler identity into code in violation of the identity/tuning split.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/routing/structured_classify.py:93-100; src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:445-452 (CLI lane builds butler_list from live registry); roster/home/butler.toml, roster/chronicler/butler.toml (no type=staffer); about/heart-and-soul/vision.md:88-101 (rule 5)

findings.title: Nothing bounds or totals the inference fan-out of a single owner message, and delegation has no depth guard
findings.detail: One inbound message pays a discretion screen, a classification inference, one butler session per decomposed segment, and any delegated sessions those spawn. Each is gated independently by quota/ceiling; nothing caps the chain or totals it. The delegation ledger tracks no parent, depth, or origin, so a butler-to-butler delegation cycle has no structural stop — only the global monthly ceiling, which (per the first finding) can itself be blind. `effective_request_id` already threads through `sessions.request_id` and `model_dispatch_attempts.logical_session_id`, so the linkage to build this on already exists.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py (no depth/parent/origin column or cycle check); openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md (no hop/depth/budget requirement); src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1689,336-389 (logical_session_id already threaded)

findings.title: Pre-invoke context assembly is five sequential independent DB round trips on the critical path
findings.detail: After the session row is created, the spawner serially awaits the system-prompt override, the situational-context preamble, the general timezone instruction, the switchboard routing instructions, and the memory context, then builds the credential env — all before the adapter is touched. Only the memory fetch depends on the prompt; the rest are mutually independent and mostly change only on dashboard edits. The ceiling prefetch elsewhere in the same function shows the pattern is already understood and simply was not applied here.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1893-1932; src/butlers/core/spawner.py:1658-1666 (ceiling prefetch precedent)

findings.title: Dead argument: the fast lane's bug-report tool can never be enabled
findings.detail: `try_structured_classification` is called only inside a branch guarded by `source != "dashboard"`, yet it is passed `include_bug_report=(source == "dashboard")` — always False. `FILE_BUG_REPORT_TOOL` is therefore never attached in the only call site, making the parameter and half the module's tool schema unreachable.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:2953-2971; roster/switchboard/tools/routing/structured_classify.py:286,319

findings.title: Provider-native session resume is gated to the conversational lane only
findings.detail: The resume-handle lookup is conditioned on `trigger_source == "route"`, so every scheduled, deadline, chain, healing, QA, and dashboard-widget dispatch cold-starts a fresh provider session even where the adapter supports resume and a stable prior lineage exists. The gating is a hardcoded string comparison rather than a policy the catalog or the task can express.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:2004-2010,2686-2700

moves.title: Per-attempt spend truth: ledger every dispatch attempt and name the unmeasurable ones
moves.why: Vision non-negotiable 4 makes the daemon the deterministic, trustworthy layer, and the north star forbids failure impersonating health. Today up to 10 failover attempts can run per logical session (spawner.py:2038) while only the winning attempt's usage is ledgered (spawner.py:2531-2542, 3244-3259), and `check_monthly_ceiling()` reads exactly that ledger (model_routing.py:2690) — so the budget gate can answer 'under budget' after a storm that already overspent. Payoff: the Spend page and the ceiling stop understating real cost, and a call the runtime could not measure is shown as an explicit unknown rather than as zero.
moves.integration_points: Schema: `public.token_usage_ledger` gains `attempt_id` (FK to `public.model_dispatch_attempts`) and `usage_source` in {measured, unmeasurable}; drop the implicit one-row-per-session assumption. Code: `_write_dispatch_attempt()` (src/butlers/core/spawner.py:336-389) writes the paired ledger row inside the failover loop; `record_token_usage()` / `price_mtd_from_ledger()` / `check_monthly_ceiling()` (src/butlers/core/model_routing.py:2649-2760) aggregate measured spend and carry an unmeasurable-attempt count alongside it. API: `/api/spend` (src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py) and the Models tab render `$X measured + N attempts unpriced`, never a single confident number. Specs: openspec/specs/model-failover, openspec/specs/catalog-token-limits, openspec/specs/core-spawner. Manifesto: Switchboard staffer contract (failure modes / recovery table).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Migration + `_write_dispatch_attempt` pairing, no UI change (ledger becomes attempt-grained). 2) Ceiling and MTD pricing consume the new grain and surface an unmeasurable count in `CeilingStatus`. 3) Spend/Models rendering plus the honest-unknown vocabulary. 4) Spec + scenario coverage for a failover storm and a timeout with no parseable usage.

moves.title: Budgets that bind before the money is spent
moves.why: Doctrine puts operational tuning in the database and expects it to be load-bearing (vision.md:88-101). Today every bound is decorative: `max_turns` is enforced by no adapter (claude_code.py:259-262), `max_tool_calls` defaults to 0 = disabled and is set by no caller (spawner.py:200; spawner_guardrails.py:113-121), `max_token_budget` exists on two schedule rows (roster/relationship/butler.toml:32,46), and guardrails are post-invocation by design (spawner_guardrails.py:3) — so the owner's per-call spend cap falls into 'cap not enforceable pre-spawn, allowing dispatch' (spawner.py:1711-1726) for essentially every dispatch. Payoff: a cap the owner sets actually stops a runaway session, and a cap that cannot bind says so instead of pretending.
moves.integration_points: Schema: tier-scoped budget columns on `public.model_catalog` (max_input_tokens, max_tool_calls, max_wall_clock_s) alongside the existing `session_timeout_s`. Enforcement chokepoint: the butler's own FastMCP server, which already knows the dispatch via the `runtime_session_id` query param (src/butlers/core/spawner.py:275-292) and already counts tool calls per session (src/butlers/core/tool_call_capture.py:20-88) — once a budget is exhausted it returns a typed `budget_exhausted` tool result rather than executing, and the spawner records a `budget_stop` dispatch outcome instead of a silent overrun. Code: src/butlers/core/spawner.py:294-334 (`_estimate_worst_case_call_cost`) and 1699-1726 become honest about enforceability; src/butlers/core/spawner_guardrails.py keeps post-hoc checks as a backstop only. API/UI: Models tab budget editor, Spend rule editor shows 'this cap cannot bind for these tiers'. Specs: openspec/specs/core-spawner, openspec/specs/catalog-token-limits, openspec/specs/model-catalog.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Catalog budget columns + resolution through `resolve_model_with_effective_tier()`, values plumbed into the dispatch but not yet enforced. 2) MCP-side tool-call/token counter and the typed `budget_exhausted` result; `budget_stop` dispatch outcome. 3) Truthful pre-spawn cap receipt (replace the log-and-allow branch with a stated non-enforceable verdict on the dispatch record). 4) Retire `max_turns` from the adapter contract or make each adapter that can enforce it do so.

moves.title: Streaming runtime transcript with a live session step channel
moves.why: The north star is five-second verification on an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine, and docs/frontend/purpose-and-single-pane.md:27-31 names Detect/Diagnose/Act latency as the pane's purpose. Today both hot adapters buffer the whole CLI through `communicate()` and parse only after exit (claude_code.py:496-499,535; codex.py:2414-2417,2478), and the dashboard's SSE stream is a keepalive poll that emits nothing until the reply row lands (conversations.py:411-424). A running session is a spinner, and a timed-out one loses every completed tool call and all usage because `stdout_bytes` never binds (claude_code.py:539-548; codex.py:2483-2500). Payoff: perceived latency collapses, a live session becomes a door on the spine, and partial evidence survives a timeout — which is also the enabler for measuring the Switchboard's `< 5 s p99` manifesto SLA per hop.
moves.integration_points: Contract: `RuntimeAdapter` (src/butlers/core/runtimes/base.py) gains an optional async `on_event` callback and a `supports_streaming` capability flag next to `supports_resume`. Adapters: claude_code.py, codex.py, opencode.py, gemini.py read stdout line-by-line and emit typed events (tool_use_start, tool_use_result, text_delta, usage) while retaining the current final-parse as the authority. Persistence: `session_process_logs` (src/butlers/core/session_process_logs.py) plus an append-only per-session step table so a timed-out session keeps its steps and last-known usage. Transport: the existing fleet SSE bus (src/butlers/api/routers/sse.py) and `_stream_conversation_response` (src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py:398-424) relay steps instead of bare keepalives. Specs: openspec/specs/core-spawner (stream-json requirements), openspec/specs/session-process-logs, openspec/specs/dashboard-chat-ui. Manifesto: Switchboard SLAs (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:33-39), Messenger delivery contract.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Adapter contract + incremental reader in the Codex adapter only (the default-enabled runtime), with the existing final parse kept as the source of truth — pure additive, no UI. 2) Durable step persistence + timeout salvage (last-known usage feeds move 1's ledger). 3) SSE relay and the conversation stream's step rendering. 4) Remaining adapters; fix the Claude adapter's non-zero-exit path to parse stdout it already holds before raising (claude_code.py:524-532).

moves.title: Interaction-class admission control for the spawn queue
moves.why: Vision's first success marker is that the owner sends a message from any channel and the right butler handles it; the Switchboard manifesto binds `< 5 s p99` classification latency (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:37). Admission today is a plain FIFO semaphore, default 3 global and 1 per butler, that knows nothing about who is waiting (spawner.py:221-251,448-450,735-777) — an owner's live dashboard or Telegram turn queues behind a nightly consolidation and, when the waiter queue fills, is rejected with 'spawner queue is full'. Payoff: interactive work always has a slot, proactive work yields instead of blocking, and 'why is my message waiting' has an answer with a door to the session holding the slot.
moves.integration_points: Code: the admission block in src/butlers/core/spawner.py:735-810 becomes class-aware over three classes derived from `trigger_source` (owner-interactive: route/dashboard/trigger; proactive: schedule/deadline/chain/classification; maintenance: healing/qa/memory-consolidation); `_get_global_semaphore()` (spawner.py:221-251) becomes a small class-reserving admission controller. Config: `runtime_config` max_concurrent/max_queued gain per-class shape (operational tuning, DB-owned per vision rule 5), seeded from `[butler.runtime_seed]`. Scheduler: proactive dispatch defers via `next_run_at` rather than occupying a waiter slot (src/butlers/core/scheduler.py tick cron pass). API/UI: `/api/butlers/{name}/status` and the Dispatch overview expose queue state naming the butler, trigger, and start time holding each slot, each linking to its session. Specs: openspec/specs/core-spawner, openspec/specs/core-scheduler, openspec/specs/runtime-config-table.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Classify dispatches and record the class on the session row + dispatch attempt (observation only, FIFO unchanged). 2) Reserved interactive slot + cooperative proactive deferral, with the deferral recorded as an honest 'yielded to interactive work' outcome, never as a failure. 3) Per-class runtime_config and its dashboard editor. 4) Queue-state surface with slot-holder doors.

moves.title: Tier fit as a measured, revisable decision
moves.why: Vision rule 5 puts model selection in the database as operational tuning, but nothing in the system ever learns whether the tuning is right. The complexity tier is a one-shot guess by a cheap classifier reading message text alone (pipeline.py:470-475) and 9 of the 12 prompt-mode schedules declare no tier at all; the only evidence loop, `compute_routing_score()` (model_routing.py:734-784), scores exit-code success, p95 latency, and a hardcoded 2000-in/500-out reference cost (model_routing.py:689-690) — a fiction no butler runs, while the real per-butler, per-purpose token distribution already sits in `public.token_usage_ledger.purpose`. Payoff: the owner sees 'these 6 schedules have run on workhorse for 30 days and never exceeded cheap-tier work, here is the evidence' as an approvable door, and an under-provisioned session can escalate mid-flight instead of returning a truncated answer.
moves.integration_points: Schema: `public.tier_fit_observations` keyed to session and dispatch attempt, populated from signals already captured — tool-call count, output tokens, guardrail trips (spawner_guardrails.py), failover attempts, the undelivered-interactive-reply flag (openspec/specs/core-spawner Interactive Reply Delivery Accounting), and owner corrections (src/butlers/core/corrections.py). Code: replace `_reference_cost_usd()`'s fixed profile (model_routing.py:785-800) with the observed per-(butler, purpose) profile from the ledger; add a `RoutingScore` fit term that is `None` — never fabricated — below the sample floor, matching the existing insufficient_data honesty. API/UI: `/api/settings/models` (src/butlers/api/routers/model_settings.py:110-130,380-400) carries per-(butler, trigger) tier recommendations with their evidence cohort; the Models tab renders an approve/reject door. Escalation: a session that trips its tier budget (move 2) re-dispatches one tier up with a recorded `tier_escalation` reason rather than truncating. Specs: openspec/specs/complexity-classification, openspec/specs/routing-scorecard, openspec/specs/model-catalog. Manifesto: none owns this — it is operational tuning, and the Switchboard manifesto should gain a line acknowledging that its classification emits a revisable estimate, not a verdict.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Observation table + writer, no consumer (pure evidence accumulation). 2) Observed-token-profile costing replaces the reference constant in scoring. 3) Per-(butler, trigger) recommendations with evidence cohorts on the Models tab, owner-approved, reversible. 4) In-session tier escalation on budget trip, gated behind move 2's binding budgets.

moves.title: Stop paying twice for the same reading: a typed classification brief in the route envelope
moves.why: The classifier already reads and understands the message in a forced tool-use call it has fully paid for (structured_classify.py:80-119), then hands the target butler only `butler`/`prompt`/`context`/`complexity`. The butler session re-reads it cold and re-derives everything, including a fresh memory-context fetch keyed on the raw prompt (spawner.py:1922-1927). That is one inference's understanding discarded and re-bought at a higher tier, every message. Payoff: fewer turns and fewer tool round trips in the expensive session, a better-grounded answer, and no extra inference — the brief rides the same forced-tool call. The same slice repairs a live capability regression the fast lane introduced.
moves.integration_points: Schema (wire): `ROUTE_TO_BUTLER_TOOL`'s input schema (roster/switchboard/tools/routing/structured_classify.py:80-119) gains typed brief fields (resolved entity refs, intent, urgency, referenced prior conversation id); `_validate_tool_call()` (structured_classify.py:170-207) validates them. Envelope: `route.v1` `input` carries the brief (openspec/specs/complexity-classification 'Complexity in route.v1 envelope', openspec/specs/butler-switchboard). Consumers: `_extract_routed_butlers` in src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py and `route.execute` handlers seed `fetch_memory_context()` (src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py) from the brief's entity refs instead of a raw-prompt search. Regression repair in the same slice: generate the `butler` enum from the live registry instead of the hardcoded 7-name list at structured_classify.py:93-100 (which omits `home` and `chronicler`), and delete the unreachable `include_bug_report=(source == "dashboard")` argument passed under a `source != "dashboard"` guard (pipeline.py:2953-2971). Manifesto: Switchboard responsibilities (classification hand-off); each domain butler's manifesto governs which brief fields it honors.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Registry-generated butler list + dead-argument removal (pure defect repair, no schema change). 2) Additive brief fields on the tool schema and envelope, ignored by consumers. 3) Memory-context seeding from the brief behind a per-butler opt-in. 4) Measure turns/tokens per routed session before and after on the tier-fit observations from the previous move.

moves.title: Request-scoped inference budget and delegation depth guard
moves.why: A single owner message fans out to a discretion screen, a classification inference, one butler session per decomposed segment, and any delegated sessions those spawn — each gated independently, none bounded or totalled as a chain. The delegation ledger records no parent, depth, or origin (src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py), and openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation states no hop or budget requirement, so a butler-to-butler delegation cycle has no structural stop; the only backstop is the monthly ceiling, which per the first move can itself be blind. The linkage to build on already exists: `effective_request_id` threads through the session row and `model_dispatch_attempts.logical_session_id` (spawner.py:336-389,1689). Payoff: the owner can see what a message cost end to end, and a runaway chain stops at a stated boundary instead of at the month's budget.
moves.integration_points: Schema: delegation ledger gains `origin_request_id`, `parent_delegation_id`, and `hop_depth`; a `public.request_inference_budget` row per owner-facing request records max sessions, max USD, and consumption. Code: admission in src/butlers/core/spawner.py:735-810 checks the request budget alongside the class check from the admission move; `src/butlers/core/delegation_ledger.py` and `delegation_wake.py` refuse a hop past the depth bound with a typed, owner-visible reason. API/UI: a request-level cost and inference rollup on the conversation turn and on the session detail ('this message: 4 sessions, $0.42, 2 delegation hops'), built from the ledger grain the first move introduces. Specs: openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation, openspec/specs/core-spawner, openspec/specs/dashboard-conversations. Distinct from the known spend-rule projection work: this is chain-scoped enforcement and rollup, not rule math or a drill-down link. Manifesto: Switchboard staffer contract gains a delegation-depth SLA line.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Delegation lineage columns + depth recorded, no enforcement (makes existing cycles visible first). 2) Depth bound enforced with a typed refusal reason and an owner-visible receipt. 3) Per-request inference/USD budget checked at admission, defaults generous. 4) Request-level rollup on the conversation turn, sourced from the attempt-grained ledger.

audits.ideal: The ideal inference economy makes every number in the loop load-bearing. Before a session runs, the tier is a revisable estimate carrying its own evidence, and the budget attached to it — input tokens, tool calls, wall clock — actually binds, enforced at the one chokepoint the deterministic daemon owns (its own MCP server), so a cap the owner sets is a cap the system honors and a cap that cannot bind says so out loud. While a session runs, its transcript streams: each tool call, each usage update, each step lands durably as it happens, so the owner watching a dashboard turn sees work in progress rather than a spinner, a timed-out session keeps everything it accomplished, and the queue behind it is legible — interactive work always holds a reserved slot while proactive work yields and reschedules rather than blocking a human. After a session ends, every attempt it made is priced into the ledger, and the attempts nobody could measure are named as unknowns rather than silently counted as zero, so the monthly ceiling and the spend page describe the money that actually left. Those same per-session signals — turns, tool calls, guardrail trips, failover, owner corrections — feed a tier-fit ledger that prices candidates on the token profile the butler genuinely runs rather than a constant, and surfaces retiering as an approvable door with its evidence cohort attached. Understanding is bought once: the classifier's forced tool call emits a typed brief that rides the route envelope and seeds the expensive session's context instead of being thrown away, and the whole fan-out from one owner message — classification, segments, delegations — is bounded by a request-scoped budget with a depth guard and totalled into a single honest cost the owner can read. Every one of those is a door on the same signal-to-session-to-evidence spine, and nothing anywhere reports calm it cannot prove.

audits.jarvis_gap: The graph today is three disconnected stores wearing one name. Identity anchors live in `public.entities`; canonical relational and contact edges live in `relationship.entity_facts`; narrative/domain knowledge lives in a private `facts` table per butler schema; and `public.memory_catalog` is a flat summary index over the last of those. Growth works — consolidation, catalog write-behind (default-on), backfill, reverse-reconciliation and atomic disownment are all real and wired. Trust does not. There are two divergent entity-merge authorities that rewire different subsets of references and neither rebinds the shared catalog, so a merge leaves other butlers' memory anchored to a tombstone. The catalog freezes `confidence` at write time and carries no decay coordinates, so cross-butler Fleet Knowledge enters another butler's system prompt with no confidence, no age and no provenance pointer — strictly more authority than the butler's own facts, which at least print a decayed confidence. The only graph-traversal primitive in the fleet, `memory_entity_neighbors`, walks the local `facts` table, which is precisely where the relationship butler's own extraction skill forbids standing relational edges from being written — so the canonical edges are unwalkable by any tool, API or page. The catalog indexes `entity_id`/`object_entity_id` but no reader accepts them, so "what does the fleet know about this person" is answerable only by hoping their name lexically matches a free-text query. And nine of the ten memory-bearing butlers hold `core`+`entity` only: they can write facts and reset decay clocks but cannot retract a wrong one or even list the predicate vocabulary they are validated against. Against the north star, the graph's growth path is solid and its verification spine is not: staleness wears current-data authority at every cross-butler hop, and the merge/repoint path reports success counts that its own exception handler cannot substantiate.

findings.title: Two divergent entity-merge authorities rewire different reference sets; neither rebinds the shared catalog
findings.detail: `memory_entity_merge` (memory module) repoints the caller's own `facts`, `calendar_event_entities` and `chronicler.episode_entities`, then tombstones the source in `public.entities`. `merge_entity_pair` (relationship butler) repoints `relationship.entity_facts` subject+object, `contact_entity_map` and memory `facts` on its own connection, and writes a merge review. Neither touches `public.memory_catalog.entity_id`/`object_entity_id`, and `entity_merge` is always called with `extra_pools=None` (the tool wrapper passes only `chronicler_pool`), so every OTHER butler's `facts.entity_id` stays anchored to a tombstoned entity that `entity_resolve` will never return again. The shared anchor is `public.entities`, but no path owns the fan-out.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:1199-1241; src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:1763-1768; roster/relationship/tools/entity_merge.py:162-294; grep for `memory_catalog` in src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py returns zero hits

findings.title: Merge fact-repointing swallows per-pool failure and still returns success counts
findings.detail: The repoint loop wraps each pool in `except Exception: continue` with the comment "Pool may lack facts table (not a memory schema) — skip". A transient connection drop, a permission error, or a lock timeout on a pool that DOES hold facts is indistinguishable from "this pool has no facts table": both contribute zero, and the returned `facts_repointed`/`edge_facts_repointed` totals plus the `memory_events` audit row read as a clean, complete merge. Failure impersonates health on an irreversible identity operation.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:1205-1214, 1246-1262

findings.title: public.memory_catalog freezes confidence at write time and carries no decay coordinates
findings.detail: `_upsert_catalog` persists the canonical row's `confidence` snapshot and there are no `decay_rate` or `last_confirmed_at` columns on the catalog, so no reader can compute effective confidence. `run_decay_sweep` cascades a catalog disownment only on the terminal expiry transition; a fact that decays from 0.95 to 0.21 and enters `fading` keeps its original catalog confidence forever, and the reverse-reconciliation sweep only marks rows stale for terminal validity. Cross-butler search (`_catalog_semantic_search`) filters on `invalid_at IS NULL` and ranks by RRF over embedding/text only — confidence and recency are not inputs at all.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:432-467, 3031-3070; openspec/specs/memory-catalog-schema/spec.md:16; openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md:153-161; src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:910-970

findings.title: Fleet Knowledge injects cross-butler claims into the system prompt with less qualification than local facts
findings.detail: `_format_fleet_knowledge_line` emits `- [source_butler] title` — no confidence, no age, no `valid_at`, no `source_id`. The same context block prints local facts as `- [subject] [predicate]: content (confidence: 0.42)`. A two-year-old fading fact from another butler therefore reads as a bare, unqualified assertion while the butler's own fresher knowledge carries a hedge. This is on by default for spawned sessions (`include_fleet_knowledge=True` at the hook site), not an opt-in.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:151-169; src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:389-396

findings.title: The canonical relational graph has no traversal path — the one traversal tool walks the wrong table
findings.detail: `entity_neighbors` builds its recursive CTE over the local `facts` table's `object_entity_id` edges. But `relationship-facts` makes `relationship.entity_facts` the canonical registry for standing relational predicates (`knows`, `family-of`, `partner-of`, `works-at`), and the relationship butler's own fact-extraction skill states the memory writer raises `ValueError` if you try to put them in `facts`. So the edges that define the graph are structurally absent from the only tool that walks it. There is no traversal endpoint on the relationship API and no `neighbors` reference anywhere in the frontend, yet `docs/modules/memory.md` advertises the tool as "Get graph neighbors of an entity" and `roster/relationship/AGENTS.md` instructs the butler to use it "to explore the knowledge graph".
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:658-720; openspec/specs/relationship-facts/spec.md:8-25,84-86; roster/relationship/.claude/skills/fact-extraction/SKILL.md:163,192,211-213; docs/modules/memory.md:94; grep 'neighbors|WITH RECURSIVE' over roster/relationship/api/router.py and frontend/src returns zero hits

findings.title: Nine of ten memory-bearing butlers can write to the graph but cannot retract from it or discover its vocabulary
findings.detail: `memory_forget` sits in the `feedback` tool group and `memory_predicate_list`/`memory_predicate_search`/`memory_stats` in `admin`. Only relationship enables either. Health, finance, home, general, education, travel, lifestyle, switchboard and chronicler run `core`+`entity` (+`preferences`): they can store facts and reset decay clocks via `memory_confirm` (core), but a butler that stores a wrong fact has no in-session correction verb and must wait for time-based decay. Worse, `_infer_recovery_steps` — the module's own self-recovery guidance emitted on a predicate validation failure — instructs the caller to "Use memory_predicate_list()", a tool those butlers do not have.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:1265-1291,1322-1360,205-208; roster/relationship/butler.toml:161-162; roster/health/butler.toml:99-100; roster/finance/butler.toml:41-42; roster/travel/butler.toml:32-33; roster/switchboard/butler.toml:38-39

findings.title: Catalog is indexed for entity lookup but has no entity-anchored reader
findings.detail: The catalog schema carries `entity_id` and `object_entity_id` (FK to `public.entities`) and the spec requires "tenant + entity lookups" indexes, but `search_catalog` accepts only `query`, `memory_type`, `limit`, `mode`, `max_sensitivity`; the `memory_catalog_search` MCP tool exposes exactly that surface, and `_fetch_fleet_knowledge` passes the raw trigger prompt. There is no way to ask the catalog "everything the fleet knows about entity X" — the identity anchor the whole graph is built on is not a query key. `delegate_ask` inherits the same limit: it routes a cross-butler question by the top free-text hybrid hit.
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/memory-catalog-schema/spec.md:16; openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md:41; src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:910-970; src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:1798-1823; src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:118-132; src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:284-310

findings.title: Memory's decay model contradicts the relationship manifesto's binding confidence clause
findings.detail: The relationship manifesto states confidence "is immutable (changed certainty is a new, superseding assertion)... an old observation does not lower its confidence; the butler renders the two as separate signals and never lets the passage of time silently rewrite what was once asserted." The memory module computes `confidence * exp(-decay_rate * days_since_last_confirmed)`, renders it as a single `(confidence: 0.42)` figure, and uses it to drive `fading`, archival and expiry. `relationship.entity_facts` honors the manifesto (immutable `conf` column plus separate `last_seen`/`observed_at`); the `facts` table the same butler also writes to does the opposite. Two contradictory doctrines of confidence inside one butler, with no reader able to tell which one produced a given number.
findings.evidence: roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md:63; docs/modules/memory.md:57; src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:135-156; src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:3031-3060; openspec/specs/relationship-facts/spec.md:36-38

findings.title: Predicate vocabulary is a per-schema copy with no shared authority
findings.detail: `predicate_registry` is created and seeded unqualified inside each butler's memory schema, so every memory-enabled butler holds an independent copy that drifts on its own migration timeline — the nine health-scope wellness predicates in `003_wellness_predicates.py` are seeded into every memory-bearing butler's schema, not just health. `relationship.entity_predicate_registry` is a second, separate registry with its own families and cardinality rules. `openspec/specs/predicate-taxonomy.md` documents the intended fleet vocabulary but no runtime artifact or contract test binds either registry to it. Meanwhile the shared catalog exposes a `predicate` filter that is compared across butlers as if one vocabulary existed.
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/001_memory_schema.py:400-406; src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/003_wellness_predicates.py:205-220; openspec/specs/relationship-facts/spec.md:79-91; openspec/specs/predicate-taxonomy.md; grep for 'predicate-taxonomy' across src/ and tests/ returns one unrelated comment at src/butlers/connectors/google_health.py:277

findings.title: Memory module doc lists two tables its own migrations dropped
findings.detail: `docs/modules/memory.md` still enumerates `rule_applications` and `embedding_versions` as tables the module owns in the hosting butler's schema. Migration `mem_006` dropped `rule_applications` (it was INSERT-only — mark_helpful/mark_harmful wrote rows nothing ever read) and `mem_005` dropped `embedding_versions`. A reader auditing rule-maturity provenance is pointed at a table that no longer exists.
findings.evidence: docs/modules/memory.md:244-245; src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/006_drop_rule_applications.py:1-19; src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/005_drop_embedding_versions.py:1-12

moves.title: Fleet identity-rebind ledger: one merge authority, per-schema repoint receipts, no silent skips
moves.why: Vision non-negotiable 3 (no cross-schema reach) is why merge fan-out is hard, and vision non-negotiable 6 makes the relationship manifesto — "your external memory for the people you care about" (roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md:7) — binding on identity integrity. Today `memory_entity_merge` repoints only the calling butler's `facts` (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:1199-1214; extra_pools is never passed, src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:1763-1768) while `merge_entity_pair` repoints a different set (roster/relationship/tools/entity_merge.py:162-294), and neither rebinds `public.memory_catalog.entity_id`/`object_entity_id`. The per-pool `except Exception: continue` (entities.py:1208-1210) turns a real failure into a zero that the returned counts present as success. Payoff: after a merge the owner sees, per butler schema, how many references rebound and which schemas are still unknown — and every butler's memory follows the surviving person instead of a tombstone. This is a new consumer of the already-shipped versioned domain-event/reaction-receipt contract, not a redesign of it.
moves.integration_points: New `public.entity_rebind_log` (rebind_id, source_entity_id, target_entity_id, target_schema, references_rebound, status active|failed|pending, error_class, completed_at); collapse `memory_entity_merge` and `merge_entity_pair` into one relationship-owned merge verb that emits an `entity.rebound.v1` domain event; each memory-bearing daemon reacts by repointing its own `facts`, `calendar_event_entities`, `chronicler.episode_entities` and its `public.memory_catalog` rows, writing one receipt row; `openspec/specs/entity-identity/spec.md` + `openspec/specs/relationship-facts/spec.md` deltas; dashboard entity-detail merge panel renders the receipt cohort with an explicit unknown state for schemas that have not reported.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Ledger table + receipt writer, and make the repoint loop classify UndefinedTable (skip) apart from every other exception (failed receipt) — this alone stops success counts from covering a failure. 2) Add catalog `entity_id`/`object_entity_id` rebinding to both existing merge paths. 3) Emit the domain event and move each daemon's repoint behind a reaction handler. 4) Delete the duplicate memory-module merge implementation; `memory_entity_merge` becomes a thin dispatch to the relationship verb. 5) Dashboard receipt cohort + spec delta.

moves.title: Give the discovery catalog decay coordinates, and make Fleet Knowledge lines carry their own qualification
moves.why: North star: "staleness never wears current-data authority." Today the catalog stores a frozen `confidence` snapshot with no `decay_rate`/`last_confirmed_at` (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:432-467), the decay sweep only cascades on terminal expiry (storage.py:3031-3070; openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md:153-161), and `_format_fleet_knowledge_line` prints `- [butler] title` with no confidence, no age and no source pointer while local facts in the same block print `(confidence: 0.42)` (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:151-169). Fleet Knowledge is on by default for spawned sessions (src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:389-396), so every butler's reasoning currently trusts other butlers' oldest claims more than its own. Payoff: a cross-butler claim arrives in the prompt with its butler, its effective confidence, when it was last confirmed, and a dereferenceable id — and cross-butler ranking stops promoting a decayed fact over a fresh one. Serves every memory-bearing manifesto.
moves.integration_points: `public.memory_catalog` gains `decay_rate`, `last_confirmed_at`, `source_validity`; `_upsert_catalog` and `run_memory_catalog_backfill` (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:432,607) write them; `run_decay_sweep` refreshes them on every fading/recovery transition, not only on expiry; `_catalog_semantic_search`/`search_catalog` (src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:910) add effective-confidence to the fusion score; `_format_fleet_knowledge_line` (tools/context.py:166) renders `[butler] title (confidence X, last confirmed <date>, id …)`; spec deltas on `memory-discovery-catalog` and `memory-catalog-schema`.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Columns + write-path population (upsert, backfill) — no reader change, catalog simply stops being decay-blind. 2) Decay sweep refreshes catalog decay coordinates on fading and recovery transitions, in the same transaction it already owns. 3) Fleet Knowledge line format carries confidence/age/id so local-vs-fleet qualification becomes symmetric. 4) Catalog ranking incorporates effective confidence; add an openspec scenario asserting a decayed fact never outranks an equally-relevant fresh one.

moves.title: Entity-anchored fleet dossier: make the identity anchor a query key on the shared catalog
moves.why: The pursuit question's cross-butler-read half is unanswered: the catalog carries `entity_id`/`object_entity_id` FKs and the spec requires tenant+entity indexes (openspec/specs/memory-catalog-schema/spec.md:16; openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md:41), but the only reader takes free text (src/butlers/modules/memory/search.py:910-970; tool surface at src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:1798-1823). The relationship manifesto promises "a complete picture of the people in your life" (roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md:15) while the fleet's knowledge about a person is reachable only if their name happens to lexically match a hybrid query. Payoff: an entity page, a routed message from a known sender, or any butler holding an `entity_id` can pull a bounded, sensitivity-filtered dossier of what every other butler knows about that person — with per-butler attribution and an explicit list of pools that could not be read.
moves.integration_points: `search_catalog` gains `entity_id`/`object_entity_id` filters; new `memory_entity_dossier(entity_id, max_sensitivity, limit)` MCP tool in the `entity` group; new `GET /api/memory/entities/{id}/fleet-knowledge` returning the standard degraded-envelope shape per docs/api_and_protocols/response-conventions.md; `build_identity_preamble` (src/butlers/identity.py) optionally carries a dossier digest for a known sender; src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:284-310 resolves a delegation target by entity when the question names one; spec delta on `memory-discovery-catalog`.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add the entity filters to `search_catalog` and a covering index — pure read addition. 2) MCP tool + dashboard endpoint with degraded-source list. 3) Wire the entity-detail page's fleet panel. 4) Optional: entity-aware delegation resolution, guarded so a missing entity falls back to today's text routing rather than becoming unroutable.

moves.title: Make the canonical graph walkable: a relationship-owned traversal over entity_facts, and demote memory's neighbors tool
moves.why: `relationship-facts` (openspec/specs/relationship-facts/spec.md:8-25) makes `relationship.entity_facts` the canonical registry for standing relational edges, and the relationship butler's extraction skill forbids writing them to `facts` (roster/relationship/.claude/skills/fact-extraction/SKILL.md:163,192,211-213). Yet the fleet's only traversal primitive walks `facts` (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:658-720), there is no traversal endpoint on the relationship API and no `neighbors` usage anywhere in frontend/src. Docs (docs/modules/memory.md:94) and the butler's own instructions (roster/relationship/AGENTS.md, "entity_get / entity_neighbors: to explore the knowledge graph") both point at a tool that structurally cannot see the graph. Payoff: "who is Chloe connected to, and how" becomes answerable — in a session, on the entity page, and for gift/reconnect/meeting reasoning — with each hop carrying its predicate family, `conf`, `verified` and `last_seen` rather than an undifferentiated blob. Serves the relationship manifesto's Dunbar model, which reasons over relational structure it currently cannot read.
moves.integration_points: New `relationship_entity_neighbors(entity_id, max_depth, predicate_families, direction)` MCP tool over `relationship.entity_facts` using the `(subject, predicate)` and `(predicate, object) WHERE object_kind='literal'` indexes the spec already mandates; new `GET /api/butlers/relationship/entities/{id}/graph` in roster/relationship/api/router.py; entity-detail graph panel in frontend/src/pages/entities/ driven by frontend/src/lib/entity-model.ts predicate metadata (no hardcoded predicate ids, per relationship-facts spec:90-91); rename memory's `entity_neighbors` to `memory_narrative_neighbors` with a docstring naming what it does and does not see; corrections to docs/modules/memory.md:94 and roster/relationship/AGENTS.md.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Recursive-CTE traversal helper over `entity_facts` honoring `validity='active'`, cardinality and object_kind, plus its contract tests. 2) MCP tool for the relationship butler. 3) Dashboard endpoint + entity-detail graph panel. 4) Rename/redocument the memory tool and fix both docs so no reader is told the wrong table is the graph.

moves.title: Split memory's confidence into asserted certainty and read-time staleness, per the relationship manifesto
moves.why: Vision non-negotiable 6 makes manifestos binding, and roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md:63 is explicit: confidence "is immutable... an old observation does not lower its confidence; the butler renders the two as separate signals and never lets the passage of time silently rewrite what was once asserted." The memory module does exactly the forbidden thing — `confidence * exp(-decay_rate * days)` blended into one rendered number (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/context.py:135-156; docs/modules/memory.md:57) that then drives fading, archival and expiry (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:3031-3060). `relationship.entity_facts` already models it correctly with an immutable `conf` plus separate `last_seen`/`observed_at` (openspec/specs/relationship-facts/spec.md:36-38), so the same butler runs two contradictory doctrines. Payoff: a reader can tell "we were sure, a year ago" from "we were never sure" — the distinction the manifesto exists to protect — and retirement decisions become explainable as staleness rather than as a silently rewritten belief.
moves.integration_points: `facts`/`rules` keep `confidence` immutable and gain a derived staleness projection from `last_confirmed_at`/`observed_at`; `run_decay_sweep` (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:3031) keys fading/expiry on (staleness, permanence, retention_class) instead of mutating a confidence product; `_format_fact_line` and `_format_fleet_knowledge_line` (tools/context.py:151-169) render two signals; the `memory_context` composite score (docs/modules/memory.md:110) splits its confidence term into certainty and recency; /api/memory/* fact payloads and the memory console render both axes; spec deltas on `module-memory` and `memory-retention-policy`; a butler that genuinely wants time-eroded belief needs a manifesto amendment naming it, not a silent default.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add the derived staleness projection and expose both axes in read APIs and context lines, leaving decay math untouched — pure additive honesty. 2) Re-key the sweep's thresholds on staleness+retention class behind a per-butler flag, with a contract test that a confirmed-once high-confidence fact never has its stored `confidence` mutated. 3) Flip the fleet default, remove the confidence-mutating write, reconcile docs/modules/memory.md:57. 4) Backfill `observed_at` for facts that only have `created_at`.

moves.title: A self-correcting graph: every memory-bearing butler gets retraction and predicate discovery
moves.why: Vision's success markers require butlers that recover from their own failures and earn progressively more autonomy; a store that nine of ten writers cannot correct accumulates error monotonically. `memory_forget` sits in the `feedback` group and `memory_predicate_list`/`memory_predicate_search`/`memory_stats` in `admin` (src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:1265-1291,1322-1360); only relationship enables either (roster/relationship/butler.toml:161-162), so health, finance, home, general, education, travel, lifestyle, switchboard and chronicler can write facts and reset decay clocks but cannot retract a wrong one. The module's own error-recovery guidance tells those butlers to call `memory_predicate_list()` (src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:205-208) — a tool they do not have — so a predicate validation failure is unrecoverable in-session. Compounding it, `predicate_registry` is an unqualified per-schema table seeded independently per butler (migrations/001_memory_schema.py:400-406), with health's nine wellness predicates landing in every schema (migrations/003_wellness_predicates.py:205-220) and nothing binding any copy to openspec/specs/predicate-taxonomy.md. Payoff: a butler that learns it was wrong can say so immediately, and the predicate filter on cross-butler search means the same thing in every schema.
moves.integration_points: Move `memory_forget` and `memory_predicate_list`/`memory_predicate_search` into the `core` group (or add them to every roster `[modules.memory] groups`), keeping `memory_stats` and the consolidation/cleanup runners in `admin`; promote the predicate vocabulary to a single `public.memory_predicate_registry` with per-scope rows, each butler read-only on it, retiring the per-schema copies via a memory-module migration; add a contract test binding the seeded registry to openspec/specs/predicate-taxonomy.md; spec deltas on `module-memory` and `predicate-taxonomy`; update docs/modules/memory.md:244-245, which still lists `rule_applications` and `embedding_versions` (dropped in mem_006 and mem_005).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Regroup `memory_forget` + predicate discovery so `_infer_recovery_steps` guidance is actually executable everywhere; ship with the butler-tool-review docstring bar. 2) Contract test binding predicate seeds to the taxonomy spec, which will surface the current per-schema drift as a failure. 3) Migrate the registry to `public`, repoint validation, drop the per-schema copies. 4) Doc corrections for the two dropped tables.

audits.ideal: Ideally there is one graph with one anchor and one set of doors. `public.entities` is the identity anchor; every reference to it in any schema is rebindable through a single merge verb that emits an identity-rebind event and collects a per-schema receipt, so an owner looking at a merged person sees exactly which butlers' memory followed and which have not reported yet — never a success count an exception handler could not substantiate. Standing relational edges live once, in `relationship.entity_facts`, and are walkable from a session tool, a dashboard endpoint and an entity page, each hop carrying its predicate family, asserted confidence, verification state and last-observed time. Narrative and domain knowledge stays local to each butler under one fleet-wide predicate vocabulary, and reaches other butlers only through `public.memory_catalog` — which is not a frozen summary but a live projection carrying decay coordinates, so a cross-butler claim can never enter another butler's prompt with more authority than the butler's own. That catalog is queryable by the identity anchor, not just by free text, so "what does the fleet know about this person" is one bounded, sensitivity-filtered, per-butler-attributed read with an explicit degraded list. Confidence and staleness are two signals everywhere, exactly as the relationship manifesto binds: an assertion's certainty is immutable and only the owner rewrites it, while age is derived at read time and is what drives retirement. And every butler that can grow the graph can also prune it — retraction, predicate discovery and correction are core capabilities, not a privilege one butler happens to hold.

audits.jarvis_gap: The proactive spine is architecturally serious but only half-connected. One real broker exists — `public.insight_candidates` with priority, semantic dedup, cooldowns, a global daily budget, verbosity presets, quiet-hours/context-bus gating, an urgent sub-cycle, and terminal attention-ledger rows (roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py; openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md) — and an in-flight v2 adds deterministic clustering, presence-aware holds with max-hold TTLs, and `held_by` telemetry (openspec/changes/insight-broker-v2-clustering-presence/proposal.md). But the spec's central claim, that this "structurally prevents individual butlers from bypassing delivery controls" (openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:4), is false in practice: only four of nine domain butlers ever call `propose_insight_candidate` (health, relationship, travel, finance), while education pushes spaced-repetition questions straight through `notify(intent='send')` from a scheduled session (roster/education/tools/spaced_repetition.py:280,299) and relationship's daily upcoming-dates and weekly reconnection tasks do the same — a second, entirely unmetered proactive channel with no budget, no dedup, and no cooldown. Home, lifestyle, general, and chronicler produce no proactive candidates at all, despite roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:13,35 promising to alert "before you have to ask." Where the broker does run, the owner has no steering wheel: there is no mute, snooze, or useful/not-useful verb anywhere in the codebase; engagement is inferred from "owner sent any message within 60 minutes," category-blind (broker.py:115-122), and the resulting ratchet only turns the whole volume down and never back up (spec:151-154). Candidates that never win a slot are flipped to `expired` with no ledger row at all (broker.py:289-307 vs attention_ledger.py:101), so the surface built to prove attention is not being swallowed cannot see the swallowing. And what proactivity does exist is text: a candidate has no action field and no evidence anchor (broker.py:82-97), the only dashboard reader is filtered to health (frontend/src/hooks/use-insights.ts), calendar prep and the conflict radar are pull-only reads with no producer and no push (src/butlers/jobs/calendar_prep.py; openspec/specs/calendar-conflict-overcommitment-radar/spec.md:13), and event chains fire only after the fact (openspec/specs/event-chains/spec.md:9). The system is closer to "a few domains occasionally text you" than to earned, steerable anticipation.

findings.title: The anti-spam architecture is bypassable and routinely bypassed: a second unmetered proactive channel
findings.detail: openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:4 claims the broker "structurally prevents individual butlers from bypassing delivery controls." Nothing enforces it. `notify(intent='send')` from a scheduled task takes no budget, no dedup_key, no cooldown — only per-butler quiet hours and the owner-attention-policy defer (src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py:900-1125). Education's spaced-repetition tool instructs sessions to "Deliver all questions via notify(channel='telegram', intent='send')" (roster/education/tools/spaced_repetition.py:280,299); relationship's daily `upcoming-dates` and weekly `relationship-maintenance` scheduled skills deliver via notify while the same butler also proposes insight candidates. Two proactive channels, one budget.
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:4; roster/education/tools/spaced_repetition.py:280,299; src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py:900-1125; roster/relationship/.claude/skills/upcoming-dates, relationship-maintenance

findings.title: No owner feedback verb exists anywhere in the proactive path
findings.detail: Grep for mute/snooze/not_useful/thumbs/feedback across src/butlers/core_tools/, roster/switchboard/tools/insight/, and src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py returns nothing. The owner's only controls are five global verbosity presets and an implicit engagement proxy. There is no way to say "never this category," "not this week," or "this one was worth it."
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:51 (VERBOSITY_BUDGETS is the whole control surface); grep over src/butlers/core_tools/, roster/switchboard/tools/insight/, src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py for mute|snooze|feedback returns zero hits

findings.title: Engagement is category-blind and the ratchet is one-way
findings.detail: `insight_engagement` stores only (insight_id, delivered_at, engaged) (broker.py:115-122) and `compute_effective_budget` aggregates one global rate (broker.py:405-455). Disengagement with one noisy category collapses every category's budget, and the spec forbids recovery: "the effective budget SHALL NOT automatically increase" and the user must manually re-raise verbosity. A two-week vacation permanently ratchets the fleet toward silence.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:115-122,405-455; openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:151-154

findings.title: Candidates that expire unseen leave no trace in the attention ledger
findings.detail: `expire_candidates` flips status to 'expired' with a bare UPDATE and no ledger write (broker.py:289-307). `Outcome` is Literal['delivered','coalesced','deferred','suppressed','failed'] — 'expired' is not in the vocabulary (attention_ledger.py:101,104). Expiry is specified to run unconditionally even inside a fully suppressed cycle (spec:217-219), so a time-sensitive candidate held through quiet hours can die without ever appearing in the surface built to catch suppressed-never-delivered egress.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:289-307; src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py:101,104; openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:217-219; src/butlers/api/routers/attention_ledger.py:1-25

findings.title: Five of nine domain butlers have zero proactive scan, including one whose manifesto promises it
findings.detail: `propose_insight_candidate` call counts per roster jobs file: relationship 22, finance 5, health 4, travel 4; education, home, lifestyle, general, chronicler zero. roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:13 promises comfort correction "before you have to ask" and :35 promises "alerting you to problems before they become serious" — the Home butler contributes nothing to the proactive channel.

findings.title: An insight is prose with no door and no evidence anchor
findings.detail: The candidate DDL is id/origin_butler/priority/category/dedup_key/cooldown_days/expires_at/message/channel/metadata/created_at/status/delivered_at/delivery_attempt_count — no action verb, no deep link, no evidence reference (broker.py:82-97). Delivery is a formatted string via notify (openspec/specs/insight-delivery/spec.md, Standalone/Digest requirements). The only dashboard reader is scoped to health with status=pending (frontend/src/hooks/use-insights.ts:1-40); the System tile shows counts only (src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:1232-1255). There is no fleet-wide place where what the system proactively said, and what it decided not to say, can be reviewed or acted on.
findings.evidence: roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:82-97; openspec/specs/insight-delivery/spec.md; frontend/src/hooks/use-insights.ts:1-40; src/butlers/api/routers/system.py:1232-1255

findings.title: Every temporal trigger is post-hoc; nothing fires before a calendar event
findings.detail: `event_chains.trigger_type` is the enum {calendar_event_end, deadline_passed, deadline_threshold} (openspec/specs/event-chains/spec.md:9); the scheduler's event-chain pass implements calendar_event_end over events where `end_at <= now` and deadline_passed (src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:1337-1400,1408-1471). Meeting-prep context is precomputed but written to `state` purely for the pull-only prep-rail endpoint GET /api/calendar/workspace/prep/{event_id} (src/butlers/jobs/calendar_prep.py:1-30). The system knows who you are about to meet, what you owe them, and when — and never says so unless you open the page.
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/event-chains/spec.md:9; src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:1337-1400; src/butlers/jobs/calendar_prep.py:1-30

findings.title: The conflict radar's one-tap fix lane has no producer
findings.detail: The radar spec states issues "carry any `pending` fix proposals from the shared `calendar_event_proposals` store so the UI can offer one-tap fixes, rendering an empty/informational state until a proposal producer runs" — and the only caller of `calendar_propose_event` is the ingestion pipeline for email/message-inferred events (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:784). No producer emits conflict-fix proposals, so the fix lane renders empty by construction. The radar is also read-time only: a double-booking two weeks out is never surfaced until the owner opens the calendar page.
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/calendar-conflict-overcommitment-radar/spec.md:13,16; src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:784; src/butlers/api/read_models/calendar_workspace_v1.py:1230-1260

findings.title: Deferral anchors to a clock, never to a good moment
findings.detail: `deferred_notifications.deliver_at` is "set to the per-butler batch time or an authoritative owner-policy/context anchor" (openspec/specs/time-aware-delivery/spec.md, Deferred Notification Storage), and the notify path computes `_deliver_at = max(_defer_candidates)` from policy end and suppressor expiry (src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py:1006-1021). The context-bus already produces calendar-derived `meeting`/`focused` signals with the event's own end time as expiry (src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:22-26), so the data to find a genuinely free window exists and is only ever used negatively, to hold.
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/time-aware-delivery/spec.md (Deferred Notification Storage); src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py:1006-1021; src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:22-26

moves.title: One attention budget: route every unsolicited owner-directed notify() through the broker
moves.why: openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:4 asserts the broker "structurally prevents individual butlers from bypassing delivery controls"; roster/education/tools/spaced_repetition.py:280,299 and relationship's daily upcoming-dates / weekly reconnection skills prove otherwise — a second proactive channel with zero budget, dedup, or cooldown. Vision's success marker is "surface timely, relevant insights without being asked — and automatically reduce frequency when the owner disengages"; that promise is unenforceable while half the fleet pushes outside the meter. Payoff: the daily volume the owner tunes is the volume they actually receive, and every proactive word the system says is one queryable population.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py (classify each call at the gate); src/butlers/core/spawner_context.py + src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:1198 trigger_source (provenance that says whether this session was owner-triggered or cron-triggered); roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py (admission path); public.insight_candidates gains an `origin_kind` ('scan' | 'session_push'); openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine, insight-delivery, core-notify. Serves the Switchboard staffer contract (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md:23 butler-to-staffer routing) and implies one manifesto amendment naming the Switchboard the sole attention-budget authority.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add trigger provenance to the notify envelope: solicited (session handling an owner ingress request) vs unsolicited (dispatch_mode job / cron / deadline). Record it on the attention-ledger row only — zero behavior change, pure measurement. 2) Publish the measured split on the Trust Console: 'N proactive messages this week, M of them outside the budget'. 3) Flip unsolicited owner-directed notify() into a broker admission that requires dedup_key + expires_at, delivered by the next cycle, with an explicit `bypass_reason` escape hatch for genuinely urgent transport (approval escalations, fleet halt). 4) Migrate education's spaced-repetition push and relationship's upcoming-dates/maintenance tasks onto the admission path and delete their direct notify instructions.

moves.title: Insight feedback verbs and per-category attention shaping, replacing the one-way ratchet
moves.why: No mute, snooze, or usefulness verb exists anywhere (grep over core_tools, the broker, and the attention ledger returns nothing); engagement is a category-blind proxy stored as (insight_id, delivered_at, engaged) (broker.py:115-122) fed into one global scalar (broker.py:405-455); and openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine/spec.md:151-154 forbids the budget from ever recovering. That is a volume knob, not a mix. Payoff: the owner kills one noisy category in one keystroke instead of muting the fleet, and the system can honestly say 'you're hearing less from Health because you ignored 9 of its last 10' — proactivity that earns calm rather than decaying into silence.
moves.integration_points: New `public.insight_feedback` (dedup_family, category, origin_butler, verdict useful|not_now|never, snooze_until, actor, decided_at, evidence ref); `insight_engagement` gains category + origin_butler; roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py compute_effective_budget:405 and filter_by_cooldown:309 become per-category; new Switchboard MCP verbs insight_mark_useful / insight_snooze / insight_mute plus a dashboard action door; openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine (Adaptive Delivery, Verbosity Presets requirements rewritten). Serves the Switchboard staffer contract.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Denormalize category + origin_butler onto engagement rows and split compute_effective_budget into per-category weights over one global cap — behavior-identical when all categories engage equally. 2) Add the insight_feedback table and the three verbs (MCP + REST), with `never` writing an indefinite cooldown row and `not_now` a bounded one, both reversible. 3) Attach the verbs as one-tap doors on the delivered message and on the dashboard insight row. 4) Make the ratchet reversible: an explicit `useful` restores category weight, and the budget carries an owner-visible reason string for its current level.

moves.title: Expired-unseen accounting plus deadline-aware selection
moves.why: expire_candidates flips status with a bare UPDATE and writes nothing (broker.py:289-307), `Outcome` has no 'expired' member (attention_ledger.py:101,104), and expiry is specified to run even inside a fully suppressed cycle (spec:217-219). The attention ledger exists precisely because 'suppressed-but-never-delivered' was invisible for months (src/butlers/api/routers/attention_ledger.py:1-25) — expiry is the same hole, still open, and in-flight max-hold TTLs bound how long a hold lasts without rescuing what is already about to die. Payoff: failure never impersonates health; the owner can see exactly what the system chose not to say and why, and time-critical candidates stop losing to equal-priority evergreen ones.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/core/attention_ledger.py:101,104 (Outcome/VALID_OUTCOMES gain 'expired'); roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py:289 (expire_candidates records one ledger row per expiry carrying the last blocking reason: budget | cooldown | held_by | dedup) and :1466 (selection ORDER BY gains an expires-before-next-cycle tiebreak); src/butlers/api/routers/attention_ledger.py summary rollup and the Trust Console panel; openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine (Expiry, Attention Ledger Recording requirements). Serves the Switchboard staffer contract.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add 'expired' to the ledger vocabulary and write one row per expiry with a `blocked_by` reason derived from the candidate's last cycle evaluation. 2) Surface expired-unseen counts per origin_butler in GET /api/attention/ledger/summary alongside suppressed_never_delivered. 3) Add the deadline-aware tiebreak to candidate selection so a candidate expiring before the next cycle outranks an equal-priority one that will survive.

moves.title: calendar_event_upcoming: a lead-time trigger that turns the prep rail into a push
moves.why: event_chains fires only on calendar_event_end / deadline_passed / deadline_threshold (openspec/specs/event-chains/spec.md:9; src/butlers/core/scheduler.py:1337-1400) — every calendar trigger in the system is post-hoc. Meeting-prep envelopes (attendee entities, Dunbar tier, last_met, open commitments) are already precomputed per event but written to `state` solely for a pull-only read endpoint (src/butlers/jobs/calendar_prep.py:1-55). The most JARVIS-shaped thing the system can do — 'your 3pm with Sam is in 30 minutes; you still owe him the book' — is fully computed and never spoken. Payoff: anticipation at the one moment it is worth anything, using data that already exists at zero new cost.
moves.integration_points: openspec/specs/event-chains/spec.md trigger_type enum gains `calendar_event_upcoming` with lead_minutes; src/butlers/core/scheduler.py `_tick_event_chain_pass` gains a forward pass over calendar_projection.start_at within the lead window (one-shot per chain+instance, mirroring the existing chain_triggered column); payload is the existing calendar/prep/<event_id> state envelope; emission goes through propose_insight_candidate with priority scaled by lead time and attendee tier so it obeys the budget. Serves roster/general (calendar owner) and roster/relationship (prep contributor, RFC-0020 contribution path).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add the trigger type, the lead-window scheduler pass, and a `prep_triggered` one-shot column on calendar_projection. 2) Emit as an insight candidate carrying metadata.event_window so the in-flight clustering work groups it with same-window candidates. 3) Attach the prep envelope's commitments as the candidate's action door once insight candidates carry actions.

moves.title: A declarative insight-scan contract, and proactive coverage for the five silent butlers
moves.why: Only relationship (22), finance (5), health (4), and travel (4) ever call propose_insight_candidate; education, home, lifestyle, general, and chronicler call it zero times — and roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:13,35 binds Home to noticing drift 'before you have to ask' and 'alerting you to problems before they become serious'. Manifestos are binding (vision.md non-negotiable rule 6), so Home's silence is a doctrine violation, not a backlog item. The reason coverage stalled is cost: each existing scan is a bespoke multi-hundred-line job. Payoff: a domain gains proactive presence by declaring a rule, not by writing a job — and the fleet's proactivity stops being four butlers deep.
moves.integration_points: New shared scaffold in src/butlers/jobs/ registered in the existing `_DETERMINISTIC_SCHEDULE_JOB_REGISTRY` (the pattern src/butlers/jobs/calendar_prep.py and calendar_overlay.py already use); a per-butler-schema `insight_scan_rules` table (query name, dedup_key template, priority expression, cooldown_days, category, expires_after); emission via roster/switchboard/tools/insight/broker.py propose_insight_candidate; openspec/specs/proactive-insight-engine gains a Declarative Scan Contract requirement. Serves roster/home/MANIFESTO.md:13,35 directly; education has no proactivity clause in its manifesto at all, so shipping its due-review scan implies a small manifesto amendment adding a surfacing promise.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Extract the common shape from health/travel/finance scans into one scaffold job driven by a rules table; port health's scan onto it as the proof (identical candidates out). 2) Ship the Home scan first (maintenance due from home-maintenance-scheduling, comfort drift from ha_entity_snapshot) — the manifesto obligation. 3) Ship Education's due-review / mastery-decay scan on the same scaffold, replacing the direct-notify push from move 1. 4) Leave lifestyle/general/chronicler as declared-empty with an honest 'no scan rules configured' state rather than silent absence.

moves.title: A conflict-fix proposal producer, and a forward radar that speaks before the page is opened
moves.why: openspec/specs/calendar-conflict-overcommitment-radar/spec.md:13 states the one-tap fix lane renders 'an empty/informational state until a proposal producer runs' — and the only caller of calendar_propose_event is the ingestion pipeline for message-inferred events (src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:784). No producer emits conflict fixes, so a shipped UI affordance is dead by construction, and the radar itself is a read-time scan (calendar_workspace_v1.py:1230-1260) that never surfaces a double-booking until the owner happens to open the calendar. Payoff: the system both notices the collision two weeks out and arrives with the fix already staged — act-before-asked with a reversible door rather than a nag.
moves.integration_points: New deterministic producer job reusing butlers.core.temporal.conflicts.detect_conflict_issues over the forward window, writing pending rows via the existing calendar_event_proposals store and modules/calendar.py:5528 insert path; emission of a bounded, deduped insight candidate (dedup_key scoped to the canonical pair id) so the radar respects the attention budget; accept/dismiss already specified (openspec/specs/calendar-event-proposals/spec.md:83). Serves roster/general (calendar owner); no manifesto amendment needed.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Run the existing detector on a schedule over the forward window and persist detected issues so a conflict has an identity that survives page loads. 2) Emit fix proposals (move-later, shorten, decline-lower-priority) into calendar_event_proposals keyed by the canonical pair id, lighting the already-built one-tap lane. 3) Propose an insight candidate only for issues that are both new and inside a near horizon, with the proposal id as its action door, so the radar speaks once per collision rather than once per scan.

moves.title: Deliver at a free moment, not at a clock time
moves.why: deferred_notifications.deliver_at resolves to a per-butler batch time or `max(policy_end, suppressor_expiry)` (src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py:1006-1021; openspec/specs/time-aware-delivery/spec.md Deferred Notification Storage) — every held message lands the instant the gate lifts, which is exactly when the owner is waking up or walking out of a meeting. The calendar-derived meeting/focused signals that could identify a genuinely free window already exist with the event's own end as expiry (src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py:22-26) and are used only negatively, to hold. The in-flight presence work bounds how long a signal may hold; it does not search for a good moment. Payoff: the same volume felt as far less noise, and a deliver_at the ledger can justify.
moves.integration_points: New deterministic `attention_windows` producer (same RFC-0009 single-writer pattern as src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py) computing the next free window of >= N minutes from calendar_projection plus active context signals; src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py deferral anchors to that window instead of a fixed batch time; deferred_notifications gains a `deliver_at_reason`; attention-ledger deferred rows carry it; openspec/specs/time-aware-delivery gains a Free-Window Anchor requirement. Serves roster/general (calendar owner) and the Switchboard staffer contract.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Ship the free-window producer as a read-only signal and log, for a week, how far the chosen window would differ from today's anchor — measurement before behavior. 2) Anchor routine (low/medium) deferrals to the free window, capped so nothing is delayed past its existing anchor plus a bounded slip. 3) Record deliver_at_reason on both the queue row and the ledger so 'why did this arrive now' is answerable without reading code.

audits.ideal: Ideally there is exactly one meter on the owner's attention. Every unsolicited word the fleet says — scheduled scan, session push, calendar lead-time nudge, conflict alarm — enters through a single broker that knows the owner's budget, what was already said, what is currently on hold and why, and what the owner has told it to stop saying; nothing reaches the owner outside it except a narrow, named, audited urgency escape hatch. That broker learns per category rather than per volume: a noisy Health scan loses its share of the budget while Relationship keeps its own, engagement is measured against explicit owner verdicts (useful / not now / never) rather than inferred from the accident of a nearby message, and the ratchet moves in both directions with a reason the owner can read. Every candidate carries not just prose but a typed action door and an evidence anchor, so a proactive statement is the head of an unbroken signal-to-session-to-evidence spine and can be acted on in one keystroke from wherever it is read. Every domain butler contributes through a declarative scan contract cheap enough that having a proactive presence is the default rather than a bespoke engineering project — and a manifesto that promises anticipation, like Home's, is structurally unable to stay silent. Timing is chosen, not defaulted: held messages land in a free window the calendar can justify, not the instant a gate lifts. And the accounting is complete and honest in both directions — delivered, coalesced, deferred, suppressed, failed, and expired-unseen all land in one ledger with the blocking reason attached, so the owner can verify in five seconds not only what the system said but everything it decided not to say, and be genuinely calm about the difference.
